Coming soon: Threads, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, TikTok, Reddit, Pinterest, Google Business Profile. Each platform's status on this page is read from the API's own configuration, so it only says live when it can post.Do the checks before posting use AI or cost extra?+No. Character limits, image counts, duplicate posts and daily caps are checked in ordinary code in milliseconds. No model is called and nothing is charged for it.Can an AI agent sign up by itself?+Yes. An agent calls POST /v1/workspaces and gets a Free-plan API key back, with no form and no human step. In MCP clients it signs in through your browser instead and never sees a key. Give it your email so you own the workspace.Can an AI agent connect accounts by itself?+No. A person approves access on each network. Nothing is published; you get a link showing the exact text for each network with Approve and Reject buttons, and a rejection note goes back to the agent. You can also give an agent a key that always needs approval, only reaches certain accounts, or has a daily post cap.Can an agent pay for a plan?+No. It asks for an upgrade link and gives it to you; you pay by card on Stripe Checkout and the plan changes when payment completes.What does it cost?+Free for 3 active accounts and 100 posts a month. Hobby is $9 a month for 5 active accounts and Pro is $29 for 25, with unlimited posts. Only accounts that posted that month count, and each account on each network counts once. In practice: you, posting to X and LinkedIn (2 accounts) pays nothing; a creator on 5 networks (5 accounts) pays $9 a month on Hobby; an agency with 12 clients on 3 networks each (36 accounts) pays $40 a month on Pro; an app whose 150 users each post to 2 networks (300 accounts) pays $199 a month on Scale.Can I use it for client accounts or inside my own product?+Yes, on every plan. Tag each connect link with your own client or user id to keep their accounts apart.How do I add it to Claude Code or another MCP client?+Run claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp and sign in from the browser; there's no key to copy. It's in the official MCP Registry as io.github.SocialsForAi/socialsforai, and /setup has the steps for Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex and others.Who runs SocialsForAI?+SocialsForAI is a product of Codehorts LLC, 1421 B St, Eureka, CA 95501, USA. Contact: lee@socialsforai.com. The SDK, CLI, agent skill and plugin manifests are open source on GitHub, and live service status is at /status (machine-readable: GET /v1/health). X, LinkedIn and Mastodon connect on the network's own OAuth screen; Bluesky uses an app password, Telegram a bot token, Discord and Slack a webhook URL, and Nostr a key you paste. Credentials are encrypted at rest, and you can disconnect any account or delete all your data at /data-deletion.Get an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents.body_text: Connect AI Agents to X, LinkedIn and Bluesky: Setup GuidesSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyAgent setup guidesWire your agent to social in a minute.Setup for each agent and automation tool we've tested. Any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP works the same way.Claude CodeConnect Claude Code to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky with one claude mcp add command. Scopes, tool names, permission rules, example prompts and Claude Code-specific fixes.Claude DesktopConnect Claude Desktop to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky through mcp-remote. Exact config per OS, where the logs are, example prompts, approval and Claude Desktop fixes.CursorAdd a social posting MCP server to Cursor with .cursor/mcp.json. Exact config, env-var keys, tool approval and auto-run, example prompts and Cursor-specific fixes.OpenClawLet OpenClaw post to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky. Add the MCP server under mcp.servers, probe it, approve from chat, use toolFilter, and fix OpenClaw-specific errors.Hermes AgentConnect Hermes Agent to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky: mcp_servers entry in config.yaml, /reload-mcp, mcp_socials_ tool names, tool filters, prompts and Hermes fixes.n8nPost to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from n8n with one HTTP Request node. Exact node settings, idempotency keys that survive retries, response handling and n8n fixes.Two ways an agent can postChat agents such as Claude Code, Cursor and Claude Desktop connect to the MCP server and call tools like create_post directly. Workflow tools such as n8n are better served by the REST API: one HTTP request per post, with an Idempotency-Key so a retried workflow never publishes twice.Both paths share the same accounts, rules and results, so you can mix them: an agent drafts and schedules, a workflow posts on a timer, and both show up in GET /v1/posts.What every setup needsThree things, whichever agent you use:An API key: create one at /signup or with POST /v1/workspaces.At least one connected account: the agent can create a connect link, but a person opens it and approves access.A rule for approval: ask the agent to dry-run and show you each post before publishing, at least until you trust the setup.QuestionsWhat people askCan any AI agent post to social media with this?+Any agent that can call an MCP server over Streamable HTTP with an Authorization header, or that can make HTTP requests to a REST API. The guides here cover the clients we've written setup steps for; others follow the same pattern.Do I need to give the agent my social media passwords?+No. The agent only holds an API key. Account owners connect their accounts on each network's own approval screen through a connect link, and you can disconnect an account or revoke the key at any time.What does it cost to let an agent post?+Free covers 3 active accounts and 100 posts a month. After that, Hobby is $9 a month for 5 active accounts and Pro is $29 for 25, with unlimited posts. Only accounts that posted in the month count.Get an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents/claude-c.body_text: Post to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from Claude Code | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPost to social media from Claude CodePost to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from Claude Code.One `claude mcp add` command and Claude Code can draft from your repo, dry run against each network's rules, and publish when you say so.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To post to social media from Claude Code, add SocialsForAI's MCP server with claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY". Claude Code then has tools to list accounts, create a connect link, dry run and publish posts, and check each account's result. You connect accounts once from a link; the agent never sees passwords or tokens.What Claude Code isAnthropic describes Claude Code as "an agentic coding tool that reads your codebase, edits files, runs commands, and integrates with your development tools," available in the terminal, IDEs, a desktop app and the browser. It connects to external tools over MCP, and its docs say MCP servers configured once work across those surfaces.That makes it a good fit for posting that starts from code: release notes from a changelog, a launch post from a merged PR, a weekly summary from commit history. The repo is already in context, so the draft is grounded in what shipped.Setup commandClaude Code's MCP docs give the form claude mcp add --transport http <name> <url> for remote servers, with --header for a bearer token. Export the key, then run:Scope matters. The default local scope keeps the server to you in this project, stored in ~/.claude.json. --scope user loads it in all your projects. --scope project writes .mcp.json in the project root to share through version control, so don't use it with a raw key. Check the connection with claude mcp list, or /mcp inside a session.bashexport SOCIALS_API_KEY=sk_... claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" claude mcp listHow the tools show up in Claude CodeClaude Code names MCP tools mcp__<server>__<tool>, so with the server called socials you'll see mcp__socials__list_accounts, mcp__socials__create_post, mcp__socials__get_post and five more. Those full names are what permission rules match on. You rarely type them: Claude reads each tool's description when the server connects and picks the right one from a plain request. The inputs for all eight are on the hub under every tool and its inputs.Three prompts to start withEach prompt below lists the tool calls Claude Code will make. Claude reads tool descriptions, so you don't have to name tools yourself."Read CHANGELOG.md, draft a release post for LinkedIn and a shorter one for X and Bluesky, dry run all three, and show me the previews." Calls list_accounts, then create_post with dry_run: true, the long text in text and short versions in platform_options.x.text and platform_options.bluesky.text. After your yes, the same call without dry_run and with an idempotency_key."Schedule that post for Tuesday at 9am Pacific, then show me what's scheduled." Calls create_post with scheduled_at: "2026-11-03T09:00:00-08:00", then list_posts with status: "scheduled". If you change your mind, cancel_post works until it starts publishing."Connect my Bluesky account." Calls create_connect_link with platforms: ["bluesky"] and prints the URL. Open it, enter your handle and an app password, then ask Claude to list accounts again.What the release-post dry run looks likeThis is the first prompt's dry run, from the repo's changelog to three previews. One create_post call carries the long LinkedIn text in text and the two short versions in platform_options, so each network gets its own wording from a single request and a single idempotency key. The preview is what Claude shows you before asking to publish. Ids are illustrative.If one version is over its limit, ok is false and the issue names the field to change, for example platform_options.x.text. Claude can edit that string and dry run again without touching the other two. All three networks are live on the hosted server, so this runs as written once each account is connected.text// Claude Code, after reading CHANGELOG.md mcp__socials__create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB", "acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP"], "text": "v2.4 is out. Webhooks now retry for 24 hours, ...", "platform_options": { "x": { "text": "v2.4: webhooks retry for 24h, signed payloads." }, "bluesky": { "text": "v2.4 is out: webhooks retry for 24 hours. Notes: https://example.com/changelog" } }, "dry_run": true }) → { "object": "preflight", "ok": true, "issues": [], "preview": [ { "platform": "linkedin", "text": "v2.4 is out. ..." }, { "platform": "x", "text": "v2.4: webhooks retry for 24h, signed payloads." }, { "platform": "bluesky", "text": "v2.4 is out: webhooks retry for 24 hours. ..." } ] }Approval with Claude Code permission rulesIn Claude Code, permission rules decide whether a tool call prompts you. Don't add an allow rule for mcp__socials__create_post, so every publish asks first. Allowing the read-only tools (mcp__socials__list_accounts, mcp__socials__get_post, mcp__socials__list_posts) is reasonable. You can also put the review rule in CLAUDE.md: "Always dry run social posts and wait for my approval." The server-side controls that back this up, from dry runs to per-account caps, are listed under keeping a human in the loop.Fixing Claude Code connection problemsMost failures in Claude Code happen before any tool runs. Errors that come back from a tool call, such as preflight_failed or account_needs_reauth, carry a fix field, and the full error list explains each code.claude mcp list shows the server as failed or needing authentication: the header didn't arrive. Remove and re-add it with claude mcp remove socials, making sure $SOCIALS_API_KEY is set in that shell.The header was empty from the start. Your shell expands $SOCIALS_API_KEY when you run claude mcp add, so if the variable wasn't exported yet, the stored header is Bearer with nothing after it and every connection gets a 401.The tools exist in one project but not another: the server was added at the default local scope, which belongs to that project. Re-add it with --scope user to have it everywhere.A teammate cloned the repo and has no server: only --scope project writes anything into the repo (.mcp.json), and you shouldn't use it with a raw key. Each person runs the add command with their own key.Set up Claude Code in four steps01Export a key in your shellSign up or call POST /v1/workspaces, then export SOCIALS_API_KEY=sk_... in the terminal you'll run Claude Code from.02Add the serverRun claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY". Add --scope user to use it in every project.03Confirm with claude mcp listThe socials entry should show as connected. Inside a session, /mcp shows the same thing.04Connect an account from the sessionAsk Claude to connect your Bluesky account. It prints a connect link; open it in a browser, finish there, and ask Claude to list accounts again.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Claude Code: connect to MCP servers (code.claude.com) · Claude Code overview (code.claude.com)QuestionsWhat developers askCan I post to LinkedIn from Claude Code?+Yes. LinkedIn is live on our hosted server for personal profiles; Company Pages aren't supported. X, Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram work too.Does Claude Code see my social media passwords?+No. You connect accounts on the network's own OAuth screen, or with a Bluesky app password, Mastodon access token or Telegram bot token, from a connect link. Claude Code only sees account ids.Should I use project scope so my team shares the server?+Project scope writes .mcp.json, which is meant to be committed. Share the server config without the key, and have each person add their key at local or user scope.Does this work in Claude Code on the web or the desktop app?+Claude Code's docs say MCP servers work across its surfaces. The server is remote over HTTP, so nothing has to run on your machine.Can Claude Code post on a schedule?+Yes. It passes scheduled_at, up to 365 days ahead, and we hold the post. No cron job or open session is needed.What is the tool name for posting in Claude Code?+mcp__socials__create_post, if you named the server socials. That's the name to leave out of your allow rules so each publish prompts you.Keep readingLinkedIn MCP serverCursor setupDocsPricingGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents/claude-d.body_text: Post to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from Claude DesktopSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPost to social media from Claude DesktopPost from Claude Desktop without leaving the chat.Add one entry to Claude Desktop's config. Claude drafts, dry runs and publishes, and asks before each action.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To post to social media from Claude Desktop, add SocialsForAI's MCP server to claude_desktop_config.json through mcp-remote, which connects to https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp and sends your API key as an Authorization header. Restart Claude Desktop, then ask Claude to list your accounts; if none are connected it gives you a connect link.What Claude Desktop isClaude Desktop is Anthropic's app for macOS, Windows and Linux. The MCP project's guide to connecting servers uses it as the example client: servers are declared in a JSON config file, and each tool call needs your approval before it runs.The config file starts local servers as commands. Our server is remote, so mcp-remote, a small npm package, runs locally and forwards each request to our URL with your key in the header. It needs Node.js, since Claude Desktop starts it with npx.Config file entryOpen the file from Claude Desktop's Settings, Developer tab, Edit Config. Per the MCP guide it lives at ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json on macOS, %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json on Windows and ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json on Linux. Add the socials entry inside mcpServers, keeping any servers you already have:Two details from the mcp-remote README. The header is written Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER} with no space, because some clients, Claude Desktop on Windows among them, don't escape spaces inside args; the space goes in the env value instead. And after saving, quit Claude Desktop completely and reopen it, since the config is only read at startup.json{ "mcpServers": { "socials": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}"], "env": { "AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer sk_..." } } } }What Claude Desktop can callAfter the restart, the socials server's thirty tools appear under connectors: list_accounts, create_post, get_post and the rest. Claude picks them from what you ask for in the chat. Each one's inputs are documented on the hub under every tool and its inputs; the two you'll see most in a writing session are create_post and get_post.Three prompts to start withClaude Desktop is where you already write, so these lean on pasting text into the chat."Here's my blog post. Turn it into a LinkedIn post under 1,500 characters and a Bluesky post under 300, dry run both, and show me the previews." Calls list_accounts, then create_post with dry_run: true and platform_options.bluesky.text. After your yes, the same call without dry_run."What did we post this week, and did anything fail?" Calls list_posts, then get_post for any post whose status isn't published, and reads you the error.fix for each failed account."How many accounts are active this month and what would that cost?" Calls get_usage. An account counts as active once it publishes in a month; see pricing.From a pasted draft to a published postThe first prompt in practice. You paste the article; Claude writes a LinkedIn version and a shorter Bluesky version, and sends both in one dry-run call, with the Bluesky wording in platform_options. Claude Desktop shows you the call's arguments in its approval prompt, and the preview comes back in the chat. When you say it's good, Claude sends the same body without dry_run and with an idempotency_key, so a dropped connection that leads Claude to try again can't post twice.The result has one target per account. A Bluesky target links to bsky.app; if a LinkedIn account had an expired token, its target would show account_needs_reauth while the Bluesky post still goes out. Ids are left out here for brevity.text// You paste a blog post; Claude proposes two versions create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP"], "text": "<1,400-character LinkedIn version>", "platform_options": { "bluesky": { "text": "<280-grapheme Bluesky version>" } }, "dry_run": true }) → { "object": "preflight", "ok": true, "issues": [], "preview": [ ... ] } // After you approve in the chat and on the tool prompt create_post({ ...same body without dry_run..., "idempotency_key": "blog-2026-11-01" }) → { "status": "published", "targets": [ { "platform": "bluesky", "url": "https://bsky.app/profile/...", ... }, ... ] }Approving tool calls in Claude DesktopClaude Desktop asks for approval before running a tool, per the MCP guide. Read the create_post arguments in that prompt, including dry_run, before you allow it. Approve the read-only tools freely and slow down on the publish. A prompt with dry_run: true is safe to allow; one without it publishes. The other safeguards, which run on our side whatever the client does, are under keeping a human in the loop.When Claude Desktop can't reach the serverProblems specific to Claude Desktop are almost always in the config file or in starting mcp-remote. Once a tool runs, any error it returns has a code and a fix; each code is explained in the error reference.The socials tools don't appear after restart: check the JSON syntax, confirm npx works in a terminal, and read the logs. The MCP guide puts them in ~/Library/Logs/Claude on macOS (mcp*.log) and %APPDATA%\Claude\logs on Windows.Connection fails only on Windows: you probably have a space after Authorization: inside args. Move the Bearer sk_... value into env as shown.You edited the file but nothing changed: the config is read at startup only, so quit Claude Desktop completely and reopen it.The server starts but every call is refused: the AUTH_HEADER value is wrong or the key was revoked. It must read Bearer sk_..., with the word Bearer and one space.Set up Claude Desktop in five steps01Get a key and check Node.jsCreate a workspace at /signup for an sk_ key. Run npx --version in a terminal; Claude Desktop needs it to start mcp-remote.02Open the config fileIn Claude Desktop, open Settings, then the Developer tab, then Edit Config.03Add the socials serverAdd an entry that runs npx -y mcp-remote https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp --header Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}, with AUTH_HEADER set to Bearer sk_... in env. Save the file.04Restart Claude DesktopQuit the app fully and reopen it. The socials tools appear under connectors.05Ask Claude for a connect linkIn a new chat, ask which social accounts are connected. With none, Claude offers a link; open it in your browser, approve, and come back to the chat.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Connect to local MCP servers: Claude Desktop (modelcontextprotocol.io) · mcp-remote README (GitHub)QuestionsWhat developers askWhy does Claude Desktop need mcp-remote?+The config file launches servers as local commands. mcp-remote is a local command that forwards to our remote server and adds your Authorization header.Can I add the server as a custom connector instead?+Yes. Add https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp as a custom connector and leave the key out: the server supports MCP's OAuth sign-in, so a browser window opens where you sign in with your email, pick or create a workspace, and approve. That also creates your account if you don't have one. The connector gets its own API key, listed on the dashboard's API keys page, where you can revoke it. The mcp-remote config with a header still works if you prefer a key.Where is claude_desktop_config.json?+macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/. Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\. Linux: ~/.config/Claude/. Settings, Developer, Edit Config opens it.Can I post to LinkedIn from Claude Desktop?+Yes, to personal profiles; Company Pages aren't supported. X, Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram work too.Is my API key stored safely?+It sits in your local config file in plain text, like any key in a config file. Keep the file private and revoke the key if it leaks.Where are Claude Desktop's MCP logs?+Per the MCP guide, ~/Library/Logs/Claude on macOS, in files named mcp*.log, and %APPDATA%\Claude\logs on Windows.Keep readingBluesky MCP serverClaude Code setupMCP serverGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents/cursor.body_text: Post to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from Cursor | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPost to social media from CursorPost to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from Cursor.Add four lines to `.cursor/mcp.json`. Cursor's agent drafts from your code, dry runs, and publishes once you approve the tool call.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To post to social media from Cursor, add SocialsForAI's MCP server to .cursor/mcp.json (or ~/.cursor/mcp.json) with "url": "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp" and an Authorization: Bearer header. Cursor connects over Streamable HTTP, and its agent gets tools to list accounts, dry run and publish posts, and read each account's result.What Cursor isCursor's docs describe it as "a coding agent for building ambitious software." It supports MCP servers over stdio, SSE and Streamable HTTP, configured per project or globally, and asks for approval before running MCP tools by default.As with Claude Code, posting from Cursor works best when the post is about the code in front of you: a changelog entry, a release, a demo GIF you already host somewhere.mcp.json entryPer Cursor's MCP docs, create .cursor/mcp.json in your project for project-only tools, or ~/.cursor/mcp.json in your home directory for every project. A remote server takes url and headers. Cursor resolves ${env:NAME} inside headers, so the key can come from your environment instead of the file:If you commit .cursor/mcp.json, the ${env:SOCIALS_API_KEY} form keeps the key out of git; each teammate sets the variable. Cursor has to be started from an environment where the variable is set, or it resolves to nothing and the server returns 401.json{ "mcpServers": { "socials": { "url": "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:SOCIALS_API_KEY}" } } } }The tools in Cursor's agentOnce Cursor connects to the server, its agent can choose among the eight socials tools based on your request. When it wants to call one, Cursor shows the call so you can expand it and read the arguments. The agent doesn't need you to name tools, but it helps to know that drafts go through create_post with dry_run: true and results come from get_post. Inputs for each tool are on the hub, under every tool and its inputs.Three prompts to start withRun these in Cursor's agent chat. Each lists the tools it will call."Summarize the changes on this branch as a short launch post for X and a longer one for LinkedIn. Dry run both and show me." Calls list_accounts and create_post with dry_run: true, using platform_options.x.text for the short version."Post this screenshot to Bluesky with alt text describing it: https://example.com/shot.png." Calls create_post with media: [{"url": "https://example.com/shot.png", "type": "image", "alt": "..."}]. The image must be at a public URL and under 2 MB for Bluesky."Why did the last post fail?" Calls list_posts with limit: 1, then get_post, and reads you each failed account's error.code and error.fix.Posting screenshots from a branchCursor sessions tend to produce images: screenshots of a new screen, a chart from a test run. They have to be at a public URL first, because we download each one rather than accepting file uploads; a local path or a private host fails with invalid_media_url or media_fetch_failed. Each network then applies its own limits: 4 images on Bluesky (2 MB each) and X (5 MB each), 20 on LinkedIn (20 MB each).If the agent attaches five screenshots to a Bluesky post, the dry run stops it before anything is uploaded. The fix tells the agent how many to drop. Ask it to pick the four that best show the change and to write alt text for each from what the code does.text// Five screenshots, one Bluesky account create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP"], "text": "New settings page", "media": [ { "url": "https://example.com/1.png", "alt": "..." }, ... 5 items ], "dry_run": true }) → { "object": "preflight", "ok": false, "issues": [ { "platform": "bluesky", "severity": "error", "code": "too_many_media", "field": "media", "message": "5 images; Bluesky allows 4.", "fix": "Send at most 4 images to this account." } ], ... }Tool approval and auto-run in CursorCursor asks for approval before using MCP tools by default, and lets you expand the call to see its arguments. Keep create_post out of any auto-run allowlist. Its docs say allowlisted MCP tools in Auto-review mode run immediately. Read-only tools such as list_accounts and get_post are reasonable to allowlist if the prompts slow you down. What the server enforces regardless of Cursor's settings is listed under keeping a human in the loop.Fixing Cursor connection problemsCursor-specific problems are mostly about where the key comes from. Errors returned by a tool call have a code and fix, and every code is described in the troubleshooting reference.The server shows an error in Cursor's MCP settings: usually SOCIALS_API_KEY wasn't set when Cursor started. Set it and restart Cursor, or put the key in ~/.cursor/mcp.json, which isn't committed.It works on your machine but not a teammate's: the project file uses ${env:SOCIALS_API_KEY} and their environment doesn't have it. Each person needs their own variable, or their own key in the global file.The agent posts without asking: create_post is on an allowlist and Auto-review mode ran it. Remove it from the list.Set up Cursor in four steps01Set SOCIALS_API_KEYCreate a workspace at /signup and put the sk_ key in SOCIALS_API_KEY in the environment Cursor starts from.02Add the server to mcp.jsonIn .cursor/mcp.json or ~/.cursor/mcp.json, add a socials entry with url https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp and headers {"Authorization": "Bearer ${env:SOCIALS_API_KEY}"}.03Check Cursor's MCP settingsThe socials server should show without an error. If it shows one, the variable probably wasn't set when Cursor launched.04Connect an account from agent chatAsk the agent to connect Bluesky. It returns a link; open it, use an app password, then ask the agent to dry run a first post.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Cursor: Model Context Protocol (cursor.com) · Cursor docs home (cursor.com)QuestionsWhat developers askShould I use .cursor/mcp.json or ~/.cursor/mcp.json?+Use the global file if you post from many projects. Use the project file with ${env:SOCIALS_API_KEY} if your team shares the setup through git.Does Cursor support remote MCP servers with headers?+Yes. Cursor's docs list Streamable HTTP and show remote servers configured with url and headers.Can Cursor's agent post without asking me?+Only if you allowlist the tool. By default Cursor asks before each MCP tool call.Can I post images from Cursor?+Yes, from a public URL: up to 4 on X and Bluesky, up to 20 on LinkedIn. Video works too: 1 per post on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn and Mastodon, not mixed with images.Is X live?+Yes. X posting is live on the hosted server, along with Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon and Telegram.Keep readingX MCP serverClaude Code setupDocsGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents/hermes-a.body_text: Post to LinkedIn, X and Bluesky from Hermes Agent | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPost to social media from Hermes AgentHermes Agent, posting to Bluesky, X and LinkedIn.Add one `mcp_servers` entry to Hermes's config, reload, and the agent can draft, dry run and publish from the CLI or your messaging apps.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To give Hermes Agent social media posting, add SocialsForAI's server under mcp_servers in ~/.hermes/config.yaml with url: "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp" and an Authorization: Bearer header, then run /reload-mcp. The tools appear as mcp_socials_create_post and so on. The REST API at https://socialsforai.com/v1 works too.What Hermes Agent isHermes Agent is "the self-improving AI agent built by Nous Research," per its docs. It runs wherever you host it, from a small VPS to a GPU cluster, and you use it from the command line or from messaging platforms including Telegram, Discord and Slack.Its MCP support connects it to external tool servers. Remote servers are HTTP entries with a URL and optional headers, which is what our server needs.config.yaml entryHermes's MCP docs put servers under mcp_servers in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. An entry has either command (stdio) or url (HTTP), and headers are sent with every request:Run /reload-mcp to load it; the docs say it reloads servers from config and refreshes the tool list. The docs also describe ${VAR} placeholders resolved from environment variables. If you'd rather not keep the key in the file, test that form on your version first.yaml# ~/.hermes/config.yaml mcp_servers: socials: url: "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp" headers: Authorization: "Bearer sk_..."REST fallbackHermes can also call HTTP APIs directly. The REST endpoints mirror the MCP tools: GET /v1/accounts, POST /v1/connect-links, POST /v1/posts, GET /v1/posts/:id, with the same dry runs, idempotency keys and error codes. Our plain-text docs at /llms.txt are written for an agent to read. Full reference in the docs.Tool names in HermesHermes prefixes each MCP tool with mcp_ and the server name, so ours become mcp_socials_list_accounts, mcp_socials_create_connect_link, mcp_socials_create_post, mcp_socials_get_post and the rest. The inputs are the same as on any client and are listed on the hub under every tool and its inputs.Three prompts to start withUse these from the Hermes CLI or a connected messaging app."Draft a Bluesky post about today's release notes, dry run it, and send me the preview." Calls mcp_socials_list_accounts, then mcp_socials_create_post with dry_run: true. After your approval, the same call without dry_run and with an idempotency_key."Which of my accounts need reconnecting?" Calls mcp_socials_list_accounts and reports any with status: "needs_reauth", then mcp_socials_create_connect_link for those platforms if you ask."Post the same announcement to Bluesky and X, short version for X." Calls mcp_socials_create_post with both account ids and platform_options.x.text, then reports each target's status and URL.A reporting setup and a posting setupBecause Hermes runs on your own server and can be reached from several messaging apps, it's worth deciding what it may do from where. A read-only configuration, with create_post and cancel_post excluded through the tools filter, can still answer "what went out this week" through mcp_socials_list_posts, check failures through mcp_socials_get_post, and report spend through mcp_socials_get_usage, which returns active accounts, posts and the estimated cost on your plan.For the posting setup, ask Hermes to keep scheduled posts rather than holding drafts itself: scheduled_at up to 365 days ahead puts the post on our queue, so it goes out on time even if the Hermes host is down. Until then mcp_socials_cancel_post can withdraw it.Approval with Hermes tool filtersHermes's per-server tools filter takes include or exclude lists (glob patterns allowed). Excluding create_post gives a read-only reporting setup; for posting, instruct Hermes to always dry run and wait for your explicit approval in the chat. The limits our server applies to every post, whatever Hermes decides, are listed under keeping a human in the loop.Fixing Hermes setup problemsHermes-side problems usually show up as missing tools after a reload. An error from a tool call itself has a code and a fix; each code is explained in the error list on the hub.No mcp_socials_ tools after /reload-mcp: check the YAML indentation and that the entry has url, not command. A 401 in the logs means the header value is wrong.The tools vanished after you switched to a ${VAR} placeholder: the variable may not be set where Hermes runs, or your version may not resolve it there. Put the key back in the file to confirm, then set the variable for the Hermes process.Some tools are missing but not others: a tools filter on the entry is including or excluding them. Check the patterns.Set up Hermes Agent in four steps01Create a workspace keySign up at /signup or send POST /v1/workspaces from the machine Hermes runs on. Copy the sk_ key.02Add the server to config.yamlUnder mcp_servers in ~/.hermes/config.yaml, add socials with url https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp and headers Authorization: Bearer sk_....03ReloadRun /reload-mcp. The socials tools appear with the mcp_socials_ prefix.04Connect a Bluesky accountAsk Hermes, from the CLI or a messaging app, for a Bluesky connect link. Open it, enter an app password, then ask Hermes which accounts it can post to.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Hermes Agent docs (Nous Research) · Hermes Agent: MCPQuestionsWhat developers askCan Hermes Agent post to social media?+Yes, through an MCP server. Add ours under mcp_servers and Hermes can post to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon and Telegram today.Does Hermes support remote MCP servers?+Yes. Its docs show HTTP entries with url and a headers map, including an Authorization bearer header.What are the tool names in Hermes?+Hermes prefixes MCP tools with the server name: mcp_socials_create_post, mcp_socials_list_accounts and so on.Can I limit which tools Hermes sees?+Yes, with tools.include or tools.exclude on the server entry. Exclude create_post for a read-only setup.Do I need MCP, or can Hermes use the REST API?+Either works. MCP gives Hermes tool descriptions automatically; REST works from any HTTP-capable tool.Keep readingX MCP serverOpenClaw setupMCP serverGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents/n8n.body_text: n8n Social Media Posting: LinkedIn, X and Bluesky | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPost to social media from n8nPost to Bluesky, X and LinkedIn from an n8n workflow.One HTTP Request node, one JSON body. Every network, a per-account receipt, and no double posts when a workflow retries.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To post to social media from n8n, add an HTTP Request node that sends POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts with your API key in an Authorization: Bearer header and a JSON body listing account ids and text. Add "wait": true to get each account's result in the response, and send an Idempotency-Key built from the source item's id so a retried execution never posts twice.What n8n isn8n's docs describe it as "a fair-code licensed workflow automation tool that combines AI features with business process automation." Workflows are chains of nodes, and the HTTP Request node calls any REST API.For posting, n8n is the right tool when something else decides what to post: a new row in a sheet, an RSS item, a form submission, a release webhook. We use the social media API over REST here rather than MCP. n8n's MCP Client Tool node documents its connection field as an SSE endpoint, and our server speaks Streamable HTTP, so the HTTP Request node is the reliable route.HTTP Request node settingsThese settings use the HTTP Request node's own labels from n8n's docs. For authentication, either turn on Send Headers and add the header by hand, or use a Generic credential of type Header Auth so the key isn't stored in the workflow.With wait: true the response is the post itself, with one target per account (status, url, error). Without it, the request returns as soon as the post is queued and you poll GET /v1/posts/:id or use webhooks. Turn on Never Error under Response if you want to branch on 422 responses instead of failing the node.textHTTP Request node Method: POST URL: https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts Authentication: Generic credential type → Header Auth (Name: Authorization, Value: Bearer sk_...) Send Headers: on Idempotency-Key = {{ $json.id }}-bluesky Send Body: on Body Content Type: JSON Specify Body: Using JSON { "accounts": ["acc_..."], "text": "{{ $json.text }}", "wait": true, "metadata": { "source": "n8n", "row": "{{ $json.id }}" } }Idempotency keys that survive retriesn8n's error-handling docs show a retried execution as a separate execution with its own id and a retryOf field pointing at the original. $execution.id is unique per execution, so using it as the key protects you within one execution but not across a retry. Build the key from the source item instead, such as a sheet row id, an RSS guid or an order number. Same key and same body returns the original post with Idempotent-Replayed: true; same key and a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused. The docs cover every field.You can paste this curl into the node's Import cURL option to fill the fields. n8n's docs note imported numbers and booleans arrive as strings, so switch Specify Body to Using JSON afterward to keep wait a boolean.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_..." \ -H "Idempotency-Key: row-42-bluesky" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"accounts":["acc_..."],"text":"New post","wait":true}'Reading the response in the next nodeWith wait: true, the node's output item is the post. Branch on its top-level status: published when every account succeeded, partially_published when some did, failed when none did. For detail, split targets into items and route each by its own status; a failed target carries error.code, error.fix and error.retryable. Retryable failures are already being retried on our side (after 30 seconds, 2, 10 and 30 minutes, then 2 hours), so a workflow should not resend them.The metadata object you sent comes back on the post unchanged, which is how a later node or a webhook handler finds the sheet row or RSS item the post came from. With Never Error on, a 422 arrives as a normal item whose error.issues lists every check that failed.text// HTTP Request node output with "wait": true { "id": "post_Zt6Mw1Qe8Rn4Yb2C", "object": "post", "status": "partially_published", "metadata": { "source": "n8n", "row": "42" }, "targets": [ { "account_id": "acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP", "platform": "bluesky", "status": "published", "url": "https://bsky.app/profile/you.bsky.social/post/<rkey>", "error": null, ... }, { "account_id": "acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "platform": "linkedin", "status": "failed", "error": { "code": "account_needs_reauth", "fix": "Reconnect the LinkedIn account with a new connect link.", "retryable": false }, ... } ] } // A 422 when preflight fails (Never Error on) { "error": { "code": "preflight_failed", "message": "The post would fail on 1 check(s). Nothing was published.", "issues": [ { "code": "text_too_long", "field": "platform_options.bluesky.text", "fix": "..." } ] } }Three workflows to start withn8n runs workflows rather than chat prompts, so here are three common shapes and the API calls each makes.Sheet row to scheduled post: a trigger on new spreadsheet rows, then the HTTP Request node with text from the row, scheduled_at from a date column, and Idempotency-Key set to the row id. We hold the post until it's due; DELETE /v1/posts/:id cancels it until it starts publishing. More in schedule LinkedIn posts.RSS to Bluesky and LinkedIn: an RSS trigger, then one request with both account ids, the full text for LinkedIn and platform_options.bluesky.text for the 300-grapheme version. The key is the item's guid.Failure alerts: register a webhook with POST /v1/webhooks pointing at a webhook trigger in your workflow, and branch on post.failed and account.needs_reauth events to message yourself. Verify the Socials-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of <t>.<raw body>) before trusting the payload. See webhooks.An approval step in the workflowFor approval in n8n, put a human step between the draft and the publish: send the dry-run response to yourself (email, Slack, a form) and continue the workflow only on approval. n8n's Wait node can pause an execution until a resume URL is called. Keep the same Idempotency-Key for the dry run's follow-up publish; a dry run doesn't use the key up. The account caps and duplicate check described under keeping a human in the loop apply to REST calls exactly as they do to agents.n8n-specific fixesThese come from how n8n builds requests. The API's own codes are the same over REST as over MCP and are listed in the hub's troubleshooting by error code; n8n sees them in the response body under error.Imported fields arrive as strings: after Import cURL, "wait": "true" is a string and fails validation. Switch Specify Body to Using JSON and write true without quotes.The node fails on 422: that's preflight_failed. Turn on Never Error to route on the status code, and read error.issues[].fix in the response.A retried execution published nothing new and returned the old post: that's the idempotency key working. The response header Idempotent-Replayed: true confirms it.409 idempotency_key_reused: the key came from a field that repeats across items, so two different posts shared it. Add something unique per item, such as the row id plus the network.Set up n8n in five steps01Get a keyCall POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/workspaces or sign up. The response includes an sk_ key; Free allows 100 posts a month, enough to build and test a workflow.02Connect an account and copy its idCreate a connect link with POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/connect-links, open it, approve, then GET /v1/accounts and copy the acc_ id.03Add a Header Auth credentialIn n8n, create a Generic credential of type Header Auth with name Authorization and value Bearer sk_....04Add the HTTP Request nodeMethod POST, URL https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts, Send Body on, JSON, with accounts, text and wait: true. Add an Idempotency-Key header built from the source item's id.05Test with a dry runAdd "dry_run": true to the body, run the node once, and read the issues. Remove it when ok is true.Sources, read 2026-11-01: n8n docs home · n8n HTTP Request node · n8n error handling (retries) · n8n metadata: $execution · n8n MCP Client Tool nodeQuestionsWhat developers askDoes n8n need the MCP server?+No. The REST API is simpler from n8n and has the same features. The MCP server is for chat agents.Is $execution.id a good idempotency key?+Only within one execution. n8n records a retry as a new execution with its own id, so build the key from the source item's id instead.Can n8n schedule posts?+Yes. Pass scheduled_at up to 365 days ahead and we hold the post, so the workflow doesn't have to wait.How do I post different text per network?+Use platform_options, for example {"x": {"text": "short version"}}. Accounts on other networks get the main text.Where should the API key go in n8n?+In a Generic credential of type Header Auth rather than typed into the node, so it isn't copied around with the node's parameters.Which networks can an n8n workflow post to today?+X, Bluesky, LinkedIn personal profiles and Company Pages, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live. Others need each network's review.Keep readingSocial media APISchedule LinkedIn postsPricingGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/agents/openclaw.body_text: OpenClaw Social Media Posting: LinkedIn, X, BlueskySkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPost to social media from OpenClawOpenClaw, posting to Bluesky, X and LinkedIn.Save one remote MCP server in OpenClaw and ask from any chat app you already use. You approve, it publishes, you get the link back.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To give OpenClaw social media posting, save SocialsForAI's MCP server under mcp.servers in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json with url: "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp", transport: "streamable-http" and an Authorization: Bearer header, or with openclaw mcp set. OpenClaw then offers our posting tools to its agent runs. If your runtime doesn't load MCP tools, the agent can call the REST API at https://socialsforai.com/v1 instead.What OpenClaw isOpenClaw's docs describe it as "an open-source AI assistant that runs on your own hardware and meets you in every chat app you already use," with a gateway process bridging channels such as Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal and WhatsApp to the agent.For social posting that means you can ask from your phone in a chat thread, "post this to Bluesky," and get the post URL back in the same thread. OpenClaw saves third-party MCP servers in its config and, per its docs, projects them into runtimes that expose configured MCP tools.openclaw.json entryOpenClaw's configuration docs put MCP server definitions under mcp.servers in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json. Remote entries take url, transport (streamable-http or sse) and headers, and the docs' example builds the header from an environment variable the same way. Use streamable-http; that's what our server speaks.Or save it from the CLI. The docs list openclaw mcp set <name> <json>, and openclaw mcp probe <name> connects to the server and lists its tools without running an agent turn. If the probe lists thirty tools, the setup works.json5// ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json { mcp: { servers: { socials: { url: "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp", transport: "streamable-http", headers: { Authorization: "Bearer ${SOCIALS_API_KEY}", }, }, }, }, } # or from the CLI openclaw mcp set socials '{"url":"https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp","transport":"streamable-http","headers":{"Authorization":"Bearer sk_..."}}' openclaw mcp probe socialsREST fallbackIf the runtime you use in OpenClaw doesn't load MCP tools, any agent that can make HTTP requests can use the same features over REST. Give it the key and point it at our docs in plain text at /llms.txt. The endpoints mirror the tools: GET /v1/accounts, POST /v1/connect-links, POST /v1/posts (with dry_run and Idempotency-Key), GET /v1/posts/:id. Full reference in the docs.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: bsky-2026-11-01-1" \ -d '{"accounts":["acc_..."],"text":"...","dry_run":true}'Which tools OpenClaw seesopenclaw mcp probe socials is the quickest check of what the agent will get: it should list list_platforms, list_accounts, create_connect_link, create_post, get_post, list_posts, cancel_post and get_usage. OpenClaw's toolFilter can trim that list per server. The inputs each tool takes are documented once on the hub, in every tool and its inputs.Three prompts to start withSend these from any channel OpenClaw is connected to."Post this to Bluesky: <text>. Dry run first and send me the preview." Calls list_accounts with platform: "bluesky", then create_post with dry_run: true. After you reply yes, the same call without dry_run and with an idempotency_key, and it sends you the post URL from the target."Connect my Bluesky account." Calls create_connect_link with platforms: ["bluesky"] and sends you the URL. Open it on your phone and use an app password."Every Friday, summarize what I shipped and draft a post, but don't publish until I approve." Each run calls create_post with dry_run: true and waits for your reply. Pass scheduled_at if you want it held for a set time.A post from a chat thread, start to finishChat changes the shape of a session. You might send the request from Telegram, wait an hour, and approve from Slack, so the agent should carry the dry-run body forward unchanged and send it with the same idempotency_key it picked for the draft. If the gateway restarts and the agent sends the publish twice, the second call returns the first post with nothing new published.What comes back to the thread is the receipt for each account: published with a bsky.app URL, or failed with an error and its fix. A connect link sent to your phone stays valid for 7 days by default, so you can approve the account later from the same thread. For an app that connects accounts for other people, external_ref on the link tags every account it creates, and list_accounts can filter by it.Approval in OpenClaw chatsChat makes approval natural: tell OpenClaw to always reply with the dry-run preview and wait for "yes" in the thread. OpenClaw's toolFilter can also hide tools per server; exclude: ["create_post"] gives you a read-only setup for status checks. Our own checks, including the daily caps and the duplicate block, apply whichever channel the request came from; see keeping a human in the loop.Fixing OpenClaw setup problemsThese are the failures that come from OpenClaw's side. When a tool runs and returns an error, the body has a code and a fix; the hub's error code list covers each one.openclaw mcp probe socials fails: check that transport is streamable-http, not sse, and that SOCIALS_API_KEY is set for the gateway process if you used the variable form.The tools don't show up in a run even though the probe works: the runtime may not expose configured MCP tools. Use the REST fallback above.Status checks work but the agent says it can't post: a toolFilter on the server entry excludes create_post. Remove it from exclude if you want posting from that setup.Set up OpenClaw in four steps01Get a key for the gatewayCreate a workspace at /signup and make the sk_ key available to the OpenClaw gateway, in the config or as SOCIALS_API_KEY.02Save the MCP serverAdd a socials entry under mcp.servers in ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json with url https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp, transport streamable-http and an Authorization: Bearer header, or save it with openclaw mcp set.03Probe itRun openclaw mcp probe socials. It connects and lists the tools. A 401 means the header is wrong.04Connect from your phoneIn a chat thread, ask OpenClaw to connect your Bluesky account. Open the link it sends, enter an app password, and reply when you're done.Sources, read 2026-11-01: OpenClaw docs (docs.openclaw.ai) · OpenClaw: Configuration, MCP, skills and plugins · OpenClaw CLI: manage saved MCP serversQuestionsWhat developers askCan OpenClaw post to social media?+Yes, through an MCP server or an HTTP API. Save our server under mcp.servers and OpenClaw's agent can post to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon and Telegram today.Does OpenClaw support remote MCP servers with headers?+Its configuration docs show remote entries with url, transport streamable-http and a headers object with an Authorization bearer token.Can I post from Telegram or WhatsApp through OpenClaw?+Those are OpenClaw channels. Ask from the channel; OpenClaw's agent calls our tools and replies with the result.Where does OpenClaw keep my API key?+In ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, or in an environment variable referenced from it. Both stay on your own machine.Is there a REST option if MCP isn't available?+Yes. Every MCP tool has a REST endpoint under /v1. The plain-text docs at /llms.txt are written for agents to read.Keep readingBluesky MCP serverHermes Agent setupSocial media APIGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/bluesky-api.body_text: Bluesky API: How to Post, Limits, Facets (2026) | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyBluesky APIBluesky is the easiest network to automate. Mostly.No app review, no paid tier, open protocol. The catches are graphemes, facets, link cards and session limits. Bluesky is one of eight networks live on our API today.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Bluesky's API is the AT Protocol: a post is an app.bsky.feed.post record written to the account's repository with com.atproto.repo.createRecord. Text is limited to 300 graphemes (and 3,000 bytes), links and mentions need "facets" with byte offsets, and a post can embed up to 4 images of up to 2 MB each. Bots authenticate with an app password, not the main password.Bluesky: live. Posting to Bluesky works on the API today.Bluesky post and account limitsLimitValueSourcePost text300 graphemes and 3,000 bytesapp.bsky.feed.post lexiconImages per post4app.bsky.embed.images lexiconImage size2 MB each (formerly 1 MB)app.bsky.embed.images lexiconLanguages per postUp to 3 in langsapp.bsky.feed.post lexiconLogins (createSession)30 per 5 minutes, 300 per day, per accountBluesky rate limitsRepository writes5,000 points per hour, 35,000 per day; a create costs 3Bluesky rate limitsAll API requests3,000 per 5 minutes per IPBluesky rate limitsLexicons read in @atproto/api; rate limits from Bluesky's docs for hosted (bsky.social) accounts. Read 2026-11-01. Self-hosted PDSes set their own limits.Is the Bluesky API free?Yes. Posting to Bluesky through the API has no fee, no paid tier and no app review. You log in as the account, get a session token and write records. The limits are rate limits, counted in points, not dollars.That makes Bluesky the network where going direct is most reasonable. If Bluesky is the only network you post to, the raw API below is a fine choice. A unified API helps when you post to Bluesky alongside X and LinkedIn, as in crossposting.How do you post to Bluesky with the API?Two calls. com.atproto.server.createSession exchanges a handle and app password for an access JWT; com.atproto.repo.createRecord writes the post to the app.bsky.feed.post collection. Each post needs text and createdAt, and the response returns the record's uri and cid.These are Bluesky's own quick-start examples. $PDSHOST is https://bsky.social for most accounts, or the account's own PDS if it's self-hosted.bashcurl -X POST $PDSHOST/xrpc/com.atproto.server.createSession \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"identifier": "'"$BLUESKY_HANDLE"'", "password": "'"$BLUESKY_PASSWORD"'"}' curl -X POST $PDSHOST/xrpc/com.atproto.repo.createRecord \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_JWT" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d "{\"repo\": \"$BLUESKY_HANDLE\", \"collection\": \"app.bsky.feed.post\", \"record\": {\"text\": \"Hello world! I posted this via the API.\", \"createdAt\": \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\"}}"What are the Bluesky API rate limits?Writes are metered in points per account: creating a record costs 3, updating 2, deleting 1, within 5,000 points an hour and 35,000 a day. That works out to about 1,666 new posts an hour or 11,666 a day, far above anything a well-behaved bot needs.The limit that bites is logins. createSession allows 30 calls per 5 minutes and 300 per day per account, so a script that logs in before every post will hit it. Store the session and refresh it; we resume a saved session and only log in again with the app password when the session is rejected.Bluesky's docs say these limits are aimed at bots that follow or like at bulk scale, and that moderation and app-specific limits may apply on top. Our own fair-use cap is 300 posts per Bluesky account per 24 hours.Why does Bluesky count graphemes, not characters?Bluesky's lexicon limits post text to 300 graphemes and 3,000 bytes. A grapheme is what a reader sees as one character: a family emoji is several code points but one grapheme, so it counts as 1.JavaScript's .length counts UTF-16 code units and gets this wrong; Intl.Segmenter gets it right. The 3,000-byte cap rarely matters in English but can in scripts with multi-byte characters or emoji-heavy posts; our preflight checks both limits. Our Bluesky character counter counts the way Bluesky does, and the Bluesky character limit page has the detail.How do links, mentions and hashtags work on Bluesky?Bluesky won't turn https://... in text into a link on its own. The client sends a facet: a byteStart and byteEnd into the UTF-8 encoded text, plus a feature saying what the range is. The lexicon defines three features: link, mention and tag.Mentions need the handle resolved to a DID with com.atproto.identity.resolveHandle; Bluesky's docs say to leave it as plain text if the handle doesn't resolve. Offsets are bytes, not characters, so any emoji before the link shifts them.Through SocialsForAI, links, mentions and hashtags get facets automatically. Link preview cards are a separate app.bsky.embed.external embed that the client must fetch and upload itself; we don't generate link cards yet, so links are clickable but show no preview.json{ "$type": "app.bsky.feed.post", "text": "Read the docs: https://example.com/docs", "createdAt": "2026-11-01T15:04:05Z", "langs": ["en"], "facets": [ { "index": { "byteStart": 15, "byteEnd": 39 }, "features": [{ "$type": "app.bsky.richtext.facet#link", "uri": "https://example.com/docs" }] } ] }How do you attach images with the Bluesky API?Upload each file with com.atproto.repo.uploadBlob, then reference the returned blob in an app.bsky.embed.images embed with alt text and, if you know it, aspectRatio. Bluesky's docs advise leaving aspectRatio out rather than guessing.The lexicon allows 4 images of up to 2,000,000 bytes each. Bluesky's prose guide still mentions 1 MB in one place while its sample code checks 2 MB; the lexicon is the authority. We download each image from your public URL and return media_too_large if it's over 2 MB.Should a Bluesky app use app passwords or OAuth?Bluesky's quick start says apps with end-user login should use OAuth, and that bots and command-line tools can stick with passwords. In every password case it says to use an app password rather than the main account password.Our connect page uses app passwords today: the account owner creates one in Bluesky's settings, enters it on our hosted page, and we store it encrypted. It can be revoked in Bluesky without changing the main password. Accounts on a self-hosted PDS work too; enter the PDS URL on the connect page.What errors come back from Bluesky through SocialsForAI?Each Bluesky failure maps to one of our error codes, with a fix and a retry decision:401 or AuthenticationRequired: account_needs_reauth. The app password was revoked; create a new one and reconnect with a connect link.429: platform_rate_limited, retried at 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m and 2h.400: platform_rejected, not retried; the message carries Bluesky's reason.Other failures: platform_unavailable, retried.Over 300 graphemes or 3,000 UTF-8 bytes: text_too_long at preflight, before any call to Bluesky.How do you post to Bluesky with one call?Send text and image URLs to POST /v1/posts. We count graphemes, build facets, upload blobs, write the record, then read it back with getPosts so verified: true in the response means the post exists. For agents, the Bluesky MCP server exposes the same call as a tool.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-0412" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_bluesky", "acc_linkedin", "acc_x"], "text": "We just shipped webhooks.", "wait": true }'Post to Bluesky through our API01Get a keyPOST /v1/workspaces returns a Free-plan API key.02Create a connect linkPOST /v1/connect-links with platforms set to bluesky, and send the URL to the account owner.03Owner adds an app passwordThey create an app password in Bluesky's settings and paste it with their handle on the connect page.04PublishPOST /v1/posts with the new account id. The response includes the bsky.app URL and verified set to true once the post is read back.Sources, read 2026-11-01: app.bsky.feed.post lexicon (atproto) · Bluesky API quick start (Bluesky docs) · Posts in depth: facets, embeds, replies (Bluesky docs) · Bluesky PDS rate limits (Bluesky docs)QuestionsWhat developers askIs the Bluesky API free?+Yes. There's no paid tier and no app review for posting from your own or a consenting user's account. Usage is governed by rate limits instead: 5,000 write points an hour and 35,000 a day per account on Bluesky's hosted service, with a post costing 3 points.Does Bluesky have an API for posting?+Yes. Bluesky runs on the AT Protocol, and posting is a call to com.atproto.repo.createRecord that writes an app.bsky.feed.post record after logging in with com.atproto.server.createSession. Bluesky's quick start shows the same two calls in TypeScript, Python and plain curl, with no app registration needed.What is a Bluesky app password?+A separate password created in Bluesky's settings for one app or bot. It logs in like the main password but can be revoked on its own. Bluesky's docs say to use an app password rather than the main password for API access.Why aren't my links clickable on Bluesky?+Bluesky needs a facet for each link: a byte range in the UTF-8 text plus the link URI. Text alone stays plain. Posts sent through our API get link, mention and hashtag facets automatically. Link preview cards are a separate embed we don't generate yet.How many posts can a Bluesky bot make per day?+Bluesky's write limit allows about 11,666 new records per day per account, at 3 points each within 35,000 daily points. The tighter limit is logins: 300 createSession calls per day, so reuse sessions. Our fair-use cap is 300 posts per account per day.Can I post to a self-hosted Bluesky PDS?+Yes. The AT Protocol lets accounts live on any PDS, and the same createSession and createRecord calls work against that host. On our connect page, enter the PDS URL alongside the handle and app password; leave it blank for bsky.social.Keep readingBluesky MCP serverBluesky character limitBluesky character counterCrosspost to X, Bluesky and LinkedInSocial media APIGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/bluesky-charact.body_text: Bluesky Character Limit: 300 Graphemes (How It's Counted)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyBluesky character limit300 graphemes. An emoji family counts as one.Bluesky limits post text by graphemes, what a reader sees as one character, plus a 3,000-byte ceiling. Here is how both work, with counted examples.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Bluesky posts are limited to 300 graphemes and 3,000 bytes of text, as defined in the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon. A grapheme is one user-perceived character, so a multi-part emoji like 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 counts once. Links count at their full length, and images don't count. Most posts only ever hit the 300-grapheme limit.Bluesky: live. Posting to Bluesky works on the API today.How Bluesky counts, with examplesTextGraphemes (limit 300)UTF-8 bytes (limit 3,000)hello55café45👍14👍🏽 (skin tone)18🇺🇸18👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 (family, 7 code points)125こんにちは世界721A 56-character https URL5656Limits from the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon, read 2026-11-01. Counts computed with Intl.Segmenter, the same segmentation our API and counter use.What is the Bluesky character limit?300 graphemes. The text field of the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon, the schema every Bluesky post follows, sets maxGraphemes: 300 and maxLength: 3000, the second measured in UTF-8 bytes. A post must satisfy both.The text may be empty if the post has an embed such as images, per the lexicon's description of the field. Through our API, a post with neither text nor media fails preflight with empty_post.What is a grapheme?A grapheme, formally an extended grapheme cluster, is what a reader sees as a single character, however many Unicode code points it's built from. é written as e plus a combining accent is two code points and one grapheme. A flag is two regional-indicator code points and one grapheme. The family emoji 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 is four people joined by three zero-width joiners: seven code points, 11 JavaScript string units, 25 bytes, one grapheme.Browsers and Node.js expose this as Intl.Segmenter with granularity: "grapheme". That's what our Bluesky character counter and our API's preflight use. text.length in JavaScript counts UTF-16 units instead and over-counts every emoji.javascriptconst seg = new Intl.Segmenter("en", { granularity: "grapheme" }); const graphemes = (s) => [...seg.segment(s)].length; const bytes = (s) => new TextEncoder().encode(s).length; graphemes("👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"); // 1 ("👨‍👩‍👧‍👦".length is 11) bytes("👨‍👩‍👧‍👦"); // 25 graphemes("こんにちは世界"); // 7When does the 3,000-byte limit matter?Almost never. 3,000 bytes over 300 graphemes allows an average of 10 bytes per grapheme. English is 1 byte per character, accented Latin letters 2, Japanese and Chinese 3, so 300 Japanese characters use only 900 bytes.Only emoji-heavy text gets near it. The family emoji is 25 bytes, so 120 of them are exactly 3,000 bytes and 121 are 3,025: over the byte limit while only 121 of 300 graphemes. Our preflight checks both limits, so a post over 3,000 bytes fails with text_too_long and a message that gives the byte count, before anything is sent.Do links, mentions and hashtags count on Bluesky?Yes, all at their full length. Unlike X, Bluesky doesn't count a URL as a fixed 23. New guide: how Bluesky counts characters https://socialsforai.com/bluesky-character-limit is 89 graphemes on Bluesky and 64 on X.Links, @mentions and #hashtags are made clickable through facets, annotations stored next to the text that point at byte ranges in UTF-8. Our API detects them for you with the official @atproto/api RichText helper and resolves mentions to the account's DID. Bare domains such as example.com are linked too. Hashtag facets are limited to 64 graphemes each by the facet lexicon.Do images count toward the 300?No. Images are a separate embed, not part of the text. The app.bsky.embed.images lexicon allows up to 4 images per post, each at most 2,000,000 bytes, with optional alt text. Through our API, pass them in media with an alt field and they're uploaded as blobs before the post is created. A video (1 MP4, up to 100 MB through our API) goes through Bluesky's video service instead and can't share a post with images.What happens if a post is over 300 graphemes?With our API, nothing is sent to Bluesky. Preflight returns a 422 preflight_failed with a text_too_long issue, for example "Text is 303 characters; Bluesky allows 300." and the fix "Shorten it by 3+ characters, or set platform_options.bluesky.text to a shorter version." Send dry_run: true to check without publishing.Bluesky is one of eight networks live on our API today; the Bluesky API page covers connecting with an app password and posting. For agents, our Bluesky MCP server exposes the same check through the create_post tool.How do I fit a post into 300 graphemes?Bluesky's math rewards different edits than X's does.Shorten URLs. On Bluesky every character of a link counts, so a 90-character tracking link is 30% of the post.Keep emoji. They count 1 each here, not 2 as on X, so they're cheap.Drop redundant hashtags; each costs its full length including the #.When crossposting, check both counts. A 294-grapheme post with one 34-character link fits Bluesky but weighs 283 on X, 3 over. Emoji-heavy text goes the other way: 100 emoji are 100 graphemes on Bluesky but 200 on X. See crossposting and the X character limit.Sources, read 2026-11-01: app.bsky.feed.post lexicon (atproto) · app.bsky.richtext.facet lexicon (atproto)QuestionsWhat developers askWhat is the character limit on Bluesky?+300 graphemes, with a second ceiling of 3,000 bytes of UTF-8 text. Both are defined on the text field of the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon. A grapheme is one character as a reader sees it, so complex emoji count once. In practice only emoji-heavy posts ever reach the byte limit.Do links count toward Bluesky's limit?+Yes, at their full length. Unlike X, which counts every URL as 23, Bluesky counts the URL text as written, so a 60-character link uses 60 of your 300 graphemes. Use a short URL if you need the room; the link is still clickable because it's stored as a facet.Do emoji count as one character on Bluesky?+Yes. Each emoji is one grapheme, including skin-tone variants, flags and multi-person family emoji. That's a difference from X, where every emoji counts as 2. Emoji do take 4 to 25 bytes each, which only matters against the 3,000-byte ceiling in very emoji-heavy posts.Why does my Bluesky count differ from string length?+JavaScript's .length counts UTF-16 code units, so a single emoji reports 2 to 11 and Bluesky reports 1. Count with Intl.Segmenter at grapheme granularity, which is what our Bluesky character counter and our API's preflight use, and you'll match Bluesky.Do images count toward the Bluesky character limit?+No. Images are attached as an embed, separate from the text. Bluesky allows up to 4 images per post, each at most 2,000,000 bytes per the app.bsky.embed.images lexicon, and alt text for each. All 300 graphemes stay available for text.Can I post more than 300 characters on Bluesky?+Not in one post. The 300-grapheme limit is part of the post record schema, so it applies whichever app or API client creates the post. Through our API, a longer text fails preflight with text_too_long and an exact overage. Split the content into separate posts or write a shorter Bluesky version with platform_options.Keep readingBluesky character counterBluesky APIBluesky MCP serverX character limitCrosspostGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →
