https://socialsforai.com/crosspost.body_text: Crosspost to X, Bluesky and LinkedIn with One API CallSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyCrosspost to X, Bluesky and LinkedInWrite it once. Fit it to every network.Crossposting fails on the details: 280 weighted characters on X, 300 graphemes on Bluesky, escaping on LinkedIn, duplicate checks everywhere. We check all of them before anything goes out.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Crossposting means publishing the same post to several social networks. Through our API, list several account ids in one POST /v1/posts, and use platform_options to give a network its own version, for example {"x": {"text": "..."}}. Each account publishes independently, so one network's failure doesn't block the others.Crossposting limits by networkNetworkText limitCounted asImagesOur daily cap per accountX280Weighted characters: URLs 23, emoji and CJK 24, 5 MB each100Bluesky300Graphemes (and 3,000 bytes)4, 2 MB each300LinkedIn3,000CharactersUp to 20, 20 MB each50Text limits from docs.x.com, the Bluesky post lexicon and LinkedIn Help, read 2026-11-01. Image limits and daily caps are what our API enforces.What does crossposting mean?Crossposting is publishing one piece of content to several networks or accounts, usually adjusted for each. For a developer it typically means one announcement going to X, Bluesky and LinkedIn at the same moment, from one place in your code.The adjusting is where it goes wrong. Each network counts length differently, formats text differently, and rejects identical repeats on the same account. A crossposting tool's job is to make those differences visible before you publish, not after one network has posted and another has refused.Why one text rarely fits every networkTake a 294-character release note with a 34-character link. On Bluesky it is 294 graphemes, under the 300 limit. On X it is 283 weighted characters, because the link counts as 23 but the limit is 280. On LinkedIn it is far under 3,000. One text, three answers.Emoji and non-Latin text change the math again. Every emoji counts 2 on X and 1 on Bluesky. A Japanese sentence like 新機能: 予約投稿をAPIから取り消せるようになりました。 is 29 graphemes on Bluesky but 53 weighted characters on X, because each Japanese character counts 2 there. The X, Bluesky and LinkedIn limit pages have the full rules.A worked example: one release note, three networksThis request sends the full note to Bluesky and LinkedIn and a shorter version to X. dry_run: true means nothing is published; we only check it.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_bsky_team", "acc_linkedin_cto", "acc_x_company"], "text": "Release notes for v2.4 are up. Scheduled posts can now be canceled from the API, webhooks retry for 24 hours, and the Bluesky connector supports custom PDS hosts. Everything new, with request examples for curl, TypeScript and Python, is on the changelog page: https://example.com/changelog/v2-4", "platform_options": { "x": { "text": "v2.4 is out: cancel scheduled posts from the API, 24h webhook retries, custom Bluesky PDS hosts. https://example.com/changelog/v2-4" } }, "dry_run": true }'What does the dry run return?The preview shows the exact text each account will get (shortened here). ok is true because the X override is 120 weighted characters. The only issue is the x_link_cost warning, which doesn't block. Without the override, the issues list would contain a text_too_long error for acc_x_company: "Text is 283 characters; X allows 280.", with the fix "Shorten it by 3+ characters, or set platform_options.x.text to a shorter version."json{ "object": "preflight", "ok": true, "issues": [ { "account_id": "acc_x_company", "platform": "x", "severity": "warning", "code": "x_link_cost", "message": "Posts with a URL cost $0.200 through the X API instead of $0.015 (docs.x.com pricing).", "fix": "Remove the link, or send a link-free version for X in platform_options.x.text. A link in a reply is also billed at the with-URL rate." } ], "preview": [ { "account_id": "acc_bsky_team", "platform": "bluesky", "text": "Release notes for v2.4 are up. ..." }, { "account_id": "acc_linkedin_cto", "platform": "linkedin", "text": "Release notes for v2.4 are up. ..." }, { "account_id": "acc_x_company", "platform": "x", "text": "v2.4 is out: cancel scheduled posts ..." } ] }What happens if one network fails?The others still publish. Each account is a separate target with its own status, attempts and error. If all succeed, the post is published. If some succeed and others fail permanently, it's partially_published, and the post.partially_published webhook lists which target failed and why.Retryable failures, such as a rate limit or a 5xx from one network, retry only that target after 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m and 2h. The post's final status is set once every target has finished. To resend only the failed network, create a new post with only that account id; resending all three would trip duplicate_content on the ones that already published.How does each network handle links, mentions and formatting?These are differences you don't see in the text itself but that change what readers get.X: every URL is wrapped by t.co and counts 23. Each link puts the post in X's $0.200 price tier instead of $0.015.Bluesky: links, @mentions and #hashtags become rich-text facets automatically; mentions are resolved to the account's DID. The URL text counts at full length.LinkedIn: the text is sent in LinkedIn's "little" text format. We escape the reserved characters ( ) [ ] { } < > @ | * _ ~ \ so they show as typed, and leave hashtags intact. An @name from X becomes plain text, not a LinkedIn mention.Images: X allows 4 (5 MB each), Bluesky 4 (2 MB each, per its lexicon), LinkedIn up to 20 (20 MB each). Sending 5 images to an X account fails preflight with too_many_media.Common crossposting mistakes and how to fix themEach of these has an error code, so an agent can fix it without a human.One text for all networks: text_too_long on X. Add platform_options.x.text.Reposting to the same account: duplicate_content within 24 hours. Vary the wording per account or wait.A video plus images, or two videos, in one post: mixed_media or too_many_videos on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn and Mastodon. Telegram takes up to 10 photos and videos in one album.An account that needs reconnecting: account_needs_reauth on that target only. Send its owner a new connect link; the rest still publish.Too many accounts on the Free plan: plan_limit_active_accounts once a post would make more than 3 accounts active this month. See pricing.When is a dashboard tool better for crossposting?If a person writes each post and wants to see it on a calendar, a dashboard scheduler is a better fit; we have no composer or calendar. We're built for crossposting from code: an app that posts on its users' behalf, a release pipeline, or an AI agent using our MCP server. X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live today. See the docs to start.How to crosspost with one API call01Connect each account onceCreate one connect link per person with the platforms they use. Bluesky asks for an app password, Mastodon for a server URL and access token, Telegram for a bot token and chat; X and LinkedIn use OAuth. You end up with one account id per network.02Write the longest version as textPut the full version in text. It goes to every account that has no override.03Add shorter versions where neededSet platform_options.x.text (or bluesky, or linkedin) for any network where the main text doesn't fit or shouldn't be identical.04Dry-run the whole requestSend it with dry_run: true. The response has a preview of the exact text each account will get, and any issue names the account and the fix.05Publish and read each targetSend it for real. The post is published, partially_published or failed, and each target carries its own URL or error.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Counting characters (docs.x.com) · app.bsky.feed.post lexicon (atproto) · LinkedIn Help: post limits · LinkedIn Posts API (Microsoft Learn)QuestionsWhat developers askDoes a failure on one network stop the others?+No. Each account publishes on its own as a separate target. If some succeed and one fails permanently, the post ends as partially_published, and the failed target carries an error code, message and fix. Retryable failures retry only that target, on a schedule of 30 seconds up to 2 hours.Can I send different text to each network?+Yes. Put the default in text and per-network versions in platform_options, keyed by platform: x, bluesky or linkedin. Each account gets its platform's override if there is one, otherwise the default. A dry run's preview shows the exact text every account will receive.Is crossposting the same text penalized?+Posting identical text to the same account twice is what platforms reject, and our preflight blocks it within 24 hours as duplicate_content. Posting the same text once each to different accounts on different networks isn't blocked by our checks. Whether a network ranks it lower is up to that network.Can I crosspost on a schedule?+Yes. Add scheduled_at to the same request and every account publishes at that time, up to 365 days ahead. Length and duplicate checks run when you create the post, so problems show up immediately rather than at publish time. Cancel with DELETE /v1/posts/:id any time before publishing starts.Which networks can I crosspost to today?+Five: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn (personal profiles), Mastodon and Telegram, with OAuth or token connect, media upload, retries and verification where the network allows it. Instagram, Threads, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest and Reddit are coming and need platform review or aren't built yet.Can an AI agent crosspost for me?+Yes. Through our MCP server, an agent in Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP client gets a create_post tool that takes the same accounts, text and platform_options fields. Because every error has a code and a fix, the agent can shorten an X version after a text_too_long and try again.Keep readingX character limitBluesky character limitLinkedIn character limitSocial media APISchedule tweetsGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/data-deletion.body_text: Delete your data | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyDelete your dataSocialsForAI (Codehorts LLC) stores a connected social account's id, name, profile image link and access credentials, plus the posts sent through it, so it can publish on the owner's behalf. Here is how to remove that data. See the privacy policy for everything we store.If you connected Facebook, Instagram, Threads or another networkRemove our access on the network. On Facebook: Settings & privacy → Settings → Business integrations (or Apps and websites), select SocialsForAI and remove it. On Instagram: Settings → Apps and websites. On Threads: Settings → Account → Website permissions. On other networks, use their connected apps settings.Or disconnect it in SocialsForAI. Whoever connected it can disconnect the account from the dashboard's Accounts page or with DELETE /v1/accounts/:id. Disconnecting deletes the stored credentials immediately.Ask us to delete everything. Email lee@socialsforai.com from any address with the network and your account name or handle. We delete the account record, its credentials and its post history within 30 days and confirm by email.If you have a SocialsForAI workspaceDelete the workspace on its Settings page in the dashboard. That immediately deletes its connected accounts and their credentials, posts, API keys and webhooks. A workspace with an active plan needs that plan cancelled first, in Billing → Manage billing. To delete your sign-in email and everything else we hold about you, email lee@socialsforai.com.What staysPosts already published remain on the networks; delete them there. Billing records are kept as tax and accounting rules require. Database backups roll off after a limited period.

https://socialsforai.com/docs.body_text: Docs: quickstart, API reference, MCP and webhooks | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyAPI documentationOne API. JSON in, JSON out.Base URL https://socialsforai.com. Every error has a code and a fix. Machine-readable: /llms.txt, /openapi.json and this page as Markdown at /docs.md.QuickstartCreate a workspace to get a key (agents can do this too), send a connect link to the account owner, then post.bashcurl -X POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/workspaces -d '{"name":"My agent"}' # → {"api_key":"sk_..."} store it; it isn't shown again curl -X POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/connect-links -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -d '{"platforms":["bluesky","x","linkedin"],"external_ref":"client-42"}' # → {"url":"https://socialsforai.com/connect/..."} the account owner opens this curl https://socialsforai.com/v1/accounts -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" # → {"data":[{"id":"acc_...","platform":"bluesky","status":"active",...}]} curl -X POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" -H "Idempotency-Key: first-post" \ -d '{"accounts":["acc_..."],"text":"Hello from the API","wait":true}'AuthenticationSend Authorization: Bearer sk_... on every request. Keys belong to a workspace; everything a key creates is scoped to it.An agent can get a key by itself: POST /v1/workspaces {name, email?} needs no auth and returns a Free-plan api_key once. MCP clients that support OAuth sign in through the browser and never see a key. The whole flow for agents is at /auth.md.Connect linksPOST /v1/connect-links with optional platforms, external_ref (your id for the person or client), redirect_url and expires_in (seconds, default 7 days). Returns a url, an id and start_urls: one URL per network for your own "Connect X" buttons. For OAuth networks (X, LinkedIn, Threads) it goes straight to the network's sign-in, and a link for a single network does the same from url.To wait for the person, call GET /v1/connect-links/:id?wait=45 (up to 120 seconds; add until=any to return after the first network). It returns status (connected, partially_connected, waiting or expired), the connected accounts and pending_platforms. Agents use the wait_for_connection MCP tool for the same thing.Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram can also connect without a link: POST /v1/accounts with {platform, credentials, external_ref?}, where credentials are {identifier, app_password}, {instance, access_token} or {bot_token, chat_id}. X and LinkedIn return requires_owner_approval, because only the owner can approve on those networks.The person opens it and approves each network: OAuth for X and LinkedIn, an app password for Bluesky, the server URL and an access token for Mastodon (Preferences → Development, scopes write:statuses write:media read:accounts), and for Telegram a bot token from @BotFather plus the channel's @username or chat id (add the bot as an admin that can post first). With redirect_url, they return to you with ?account_id=&platform=&status=connected.Getting app passwords and tokensBluesky: (1) On bsky.app, open Settings → Privacy and security → App passwords. (2) Choose Add App Password, name it SocialsForAI, and leave direct-message access off. (3) Copy the password it shows (four groups like abcd-efgh-ijkl-mnop). It's shown once. (4) Enter your handle (for example yourname.bsky.social) and that app password here. Revoke the app password in the same screen any time to disconnect.Mastodon: (1) Sign in to your Mastodon server's website (for example mastodon.social) and open Preferences → Development. (2) Choose New application and name it SocialsForAI. Leave the redirect URI as it is. (3) Under Scopes, untick the broad read, write and follow boxes and tick only read:accounts, write:statuses and write:media. Submit. (4) Open the application you created and copy “Your access token”. (5) Enter your server's address (https://mastodon.social) and the token here. Delete the application on that page any time to disconnect.Telegram: (1) In Telegram, open @BotFather, send /newbot, and pick a name and a username ending in “bot”. Copy the token it replies with. (2) Open your channel → Administrators → Add Admin, search for your bot's username, turn on “Post Messages”, and save. For a group, add the bot as a member. (3) Paste the bot token below and leave the channel blank: we find the channel or group you just added the bot to. If the bot is in several, enter the one you want (a public channel's @username, or its chat id). (4) To disconnect later, remove the bot from the channel or revoke its token in @BotFather.Discord: (1) In Discord, open the channel's settings (the gear next to its name) → Integrations → Webhooks → New Webhook. You need the Manage Webhooks permission on the server. (2) Give it the name and picture posts should appear under, then choose Copy Webhook URL. (3) Paste the URL below. Anyone with this URL can post to the channel, so treat it like a password. (4) To disconnect later, delete the webhook in the same Discord screen.Slack: (1) Open api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From scratch, and pick your workspace. (An existing app works too.) (2) In the app: Incoming Webhooks → turn on Activate Incoming Webhooks → Add New Webhook to Workspace, choose the channel, and Allow. (3) Copy the Webhook URL it shows and paste it below. Anyone with this URL can post to the channel, so treat it like a password. (4) To disconnect later, remove the webhook on the same Slack page.Nostr: (1) In your Nostr app, open the key settings (Damus: Settings → Keys; Primal: Settings → Keys; Amethyst: Backup keys) and copy the private key. It starts with nsec1. (2) Paste it below. This key is your whole account, so we store it encrypted and use it only to sign the posts you send. For extra safety, use a key made just for publishing. (3) Relays are optional: leave the field empty to publish to well-known public relays, or list the ones your followers read (wss://…, comma-separated). (4) To disconnect, remove the account here. A Nostr key can't be revoked, so if it ever leaks, move to a new one.AccountsGET /v1/accounts?platform=&external_ref=&status= · GET /v1/accounts/:id · DELETE /v1/accounts/:id (disconnect).Status is active or needs_reauth. When a token expires or is revoked, the account flips to needs_reauth and an account.needs_reauth webhook fires; send a new connect link for that platform.PostsPOST /v1/posts fields: accounts (required: account ids, or a network name like "x" when the workspace has exactly one active account on it), text, media ([{url, type?, alt?, title?, thumbnail?}]; each URL is checked when the post is created or dry-run (media_unreachable, media_not_a_file for share and preview pages, media_too_large for video), and images in a format or size a network doesn't take are converted to JPEG and shrunk for you; public URLs; type is image, video or document, guessed from the file extension when omitted. A document (PDF, PowerPoint or Word, up to 100 MB) posts to LinkedIn profiles and Pages as a swipeable document, titled with title or the file name; it goes alone, one per post, and other networks reject it with document_not_supported. A video can carry a title (LinkedIn, Facebook) and a thumbnail image URL (LinkedIn, Facebook, and the Instagram Reel cover)), link ({url, title?, description?, thumbnail?}: a clickable preview card, see below), thread ([{text, media?}]: follow-up posts, each a reply to the one before, on X, Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram), auto_thread (true splits text that is over a network's limit into a thread there, at paragraph and sentence breaks, instead of failing with text_too_long; the dry run's preview shows each piece), reply_to (a post_… id from this workspace to reply to, on each account it was published to), first_comment (up to 1,250 characters, posted as a comment by the same LinkedIn profile or Page right after the post goes out, for example to hold a link; its id comes back as first_comment_id on the target. If the comment is refused, the post stays published and the target's error is first_comment_failed. Other networks skip it with a first_comment_not_supported warning; use thread on X, Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram), poll ({question?, options, duration_minutes?, multiple?} on X, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram and Threads (2 to 4 options of 25 characters; Threads sets the open time), never with media: X takes 2 to 4 options of 25 characters for 5 minutes to 7 days; LinkedIn 2 to 4 options of 30 characters plus a question of up to 140 (defaults to the text), open 1, 3, 7 or 14 days (rounded); Mastodon 2 to 4 options of 50 characters for up to 30 days, multiple allowed; Telegram up to 10 options with a question, sent right after the text when both are given. Default open time is 1 day; other networks reject polls with poll_not_supported), platform_options (per-network settings keyed by platform: a text override for any network, like {"x":{"text":"…"}}, plus x.reply_settings (following, mentionedUsers, subscribers, verified), bluesky.langs (e.g. ["en"]), mastodon.visibility (public, unlisted, private, direct), mastodon.spoiler_text (content warning), mastodon.sensitive, mastodon.language, telegram.disable_notification (silent), telegram.protect_content (no forwarding or saving), instagram.format (post or story), Reel settings instagram.share_to_feed, instagram.cover_url, instagram.thumb_offset (ms) and instagram.audio_name, instagram.collaborators (up to 3 usernames), linkedin.visibility (PUBLIC, CONNECTIONS, LOGGED_IN), linkedin_page.visibility (PUBLIC, LOGGED_IN) and threads.reply_control (everyone, accounts_you_follow, mentioned_only, parent_post_author_only, followers_only). Unknown networks or settings are rejected, so typos don't pass silently), scheduled_at (ISO-8601 with an offset, a local time like 2026-11-05T09:00 together with timezone, an IANA name such as America/Los_Angeles, or "best" to use the hour that has had the most engagement on these accounts, falling back to a weekday at 9:00 in timezone), repeat ({every: day|week|month, interval?, count} creates that many dated posts at the same local time; they share a series_id, and DELETE /v1/posts/:id?series=true cancels the rest), approval ("required" holds the post for a person, see Approvals), dry_run, wait, metadata.dry_run: true returns {ok, issues, preview} and publishes nothing. wait: true publishes before responding and returns final per-account status. Without wait, the response is publishing and webhooks report the outcome.Link cards: link turns a URL into a clickable preview. On LinkedIn (profiles and Pages) and Bluesky we build the card: image, title and domain, and clicking anywhere on it opens the URL. Title, description and thumbnail default to the page's own og: tags; set them to override, and use link.thumbnail instead of media there, since those cards can't carry media. Facebook Pages and Threads show their own card from the page's tags. On X, Mastodon and Telegram the URL is added to the text (and counts toward the limit), and the network shows its preview. Instagram has no clickable links in posts, so the link is left out there with a link_not_supported warning.Status: scheduled → publishing → published, partially_published, failed or canceled (and pending_approval first when approval is required, see Approvals). Each target carries status, url, external_post_id, attempts, verified and error {code, message, fix, retryable}.GET /v1/analytics summarizes a period (days, default 30, or from/to; filter with account_id or platform): posts published, totals and engagement per account, the top posts (limit), and best_times, the days and hours (in the timezone you pass) whose posts drew the most engagement, once a slot has at least 3 measured posts. It is built from metrics already read for each post, so it never calls a network and costs nothing; read metrics for recent posts first. MCP tool: get_analytics.POST /v1/posts/batch {posts: [...], dry_run?} creates up to 50 posts in one request, for example a month of scheduled content. Each is checked and created by itself, and the response lists a result per item. GET /v1/posts/:id/replies returns what people replied under each published copy (Bluesky, Mastodon and X today; X bills $0.005 for each reply returned, passed through at cost, and only searches the last 7 days), each with an id, parent_id, author, text and created_at. To answer one, create a post with one account, reply_to set to the post and reply_to_comment set to the reply's id; it goes through the same checks and approvals as any post. To change a post before it goes out, PATCH /v1/posts/:id with any of text, media, link, thread, poll, first_comment, platform_options, scheduled_at and timezone. Fields you leave out stay as they are; scheduled_at: null publishes it now. Only posts that haven't started publishing (scheduled or pending_approval) can change; anything else answers 409 post_not_editable, and a published post has to be deleted and posted again because networks don't let us edit it. The edit is checked like a new post (422 preflight_failed, or dry_run: true to check without saving), fires a post.updated webhook, and sends an approved post back for approval if its content changed. MCP tool: update_post.GET /v1/posts?status=&limit=&before= · GET /v1/posts/:id · DELETE /v1/posts/:id deletes it everywhere it went out: published copies are deleted from X, Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn, Telegram, Discord, Nostr, Reddit and Facebook (threads included) and copies not yet published are canceled. Add ?accounts=acc_1,acc_2 to delete from some accounts only. Deleted targets show status: "deleted" and deleted_at; a network that refuses comes back in warnings with its error, and deleting again retries it. Instagram and Threads posts can't be deleted through the API yet (delete_not_supported). Deleted posts still count toward usage, and X's $0.010 delete fee is passed through. GET /v1/posts/:id/metrics returns likes, reposts, replies, quotes, views and more for each published copy, plus totals; numbers are read from each network and cached for 15 minutes. Available on X (X bills $0.005 per read, passed through), Bluesky, Mastodon and LinkedIn Pages; LinkedIn profiles and Telegram don't report post metrics, and Facebook, Instagram and Threads follow once Meta approves the permissions.Networks and what each supportsGET /v1/platforms (no key needed; MCP list_platforms) returns this for every network, read from the running service: whether it is available, its limits, and a features object (threads, polls, documents, first_comment, delete, metrics, read_replies, and how a link is shared). Check it before using a feature on a network instead of assuming.X: 280 characters, 4 images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports threads, polls, delete, metrics, reading replies.Bluesky: 300 characters, 4 images, video; connects by credentials. Supports threads, delete, metrics, reading replies.LinkedIn: 3,000 characters, 20 images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports polls, documents, first comments, delete.Mastodon: 500 characters, 4 images, video; connects by credentials. Supports threads, polls, delete, metrics, reading replies.Telegram: 4,096 characters, 10 images, video; connects by credentials. Supports threads, polls, delete.Threads (in the network's app review): 500 characters, 20 images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports polls.Facebook (in the network's app review): 63,206 characters, 10 images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports delete.Instagram (in the network's app review): 2,200 characters, 10 images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Text and media only.YouTube (in the network's app review): 5,000 characters, no images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports metrics.TikTok (in the network's app review): 2,200 characters, no images, video; connects by connect link (OAuth). Text and media only.Discord: 2,000 characters, 10 images, video; connects by credentials. Supports polls, delete.Slack: 12,000 characters, 10 images; connects by credentials. Text and media only.Nostr: 4,000 characters, 4 images, video; connects by credentials. Supports threads, delete.Reddit (not switched on yet): 40,000 characters, no images; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports first comments, delete, metrics, reading replies.Pinterest (in the network's app review): 800 characters, 5 images; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports delete, metrics.Google Business Profile (not switched on yet): 1,500 characters, 1 images; connects by connect link (OAuth). Supports delete.Discord, Slack, Nostr, Reddit, Pinterest and Google Business ProfileDiscord: connect with a channel webhook URL (the channel's settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy Webhook URL). Posts take up to 2,000 characters, 10 files of up to 10 MB, and polls of up to 10 answers, and can be deleted. One webhook is one channel. Mentions such as @everyone in the text don't notify anyone unless platform_options.discord.allow_mentions is true; platform_options.discord.username posts under another name.Slack: connect with an incoming webhook URL (a Slack app → Incoming Webhooks → Add New Webhook to Workspace). Text up to 12,000 characters and up to 10 images, in the webhook's channel. Slack gives webhooks no message id, so Slack posts have no link (url: null) and can't be deleted or measured.Nostr: connect with the account's private key (nsec1…) and, optionally, the relays to publish to (by default, well-known public relays). The key is the whole account and can't be revoked, so it is stored encrypted, and the owner should paste it into a connect link rather than send it to an agent. Notes take up to 4,000 characters; media is shared by link rather than uploaded. Threads and deletion requests work (relays decide whether to honour a deletion). A note counts as published once one relay accepts it.Reddit (when switched on): text posts to a subreddit as the connected user, through a connect link. platform_options.reddit.subreddit is required; the title is platform_options.reddit.title, else the first line of the text, and the rest is the body. Also flair_id, nsfw and spoiler. Each subreddit has its own rules, and a refusal comes back as platform_rejected with Reddit's reason. First comments, reading and answering replies, metrics and delete work.Pinterest (when switched on): a post is a Pin with one image, or 2 to 5 as a carousel; the text is its description (800 characters) and link is where the Pin leads. platform_options.pinterest.board picks the board by name or id; it's required unless the account has exactly one board, and the error lists the boards. platform_options.pinterest.title sets a title. Metrics (impressions, saves, clicks) and delete work.Google Business Profile (when switched on, platform google_business): an update on the business's listing on Google Search and Maps. Connecting adds one account per location the person manages. Text up to 1,500 characters, one photo, and a button: platform_options.google_business.call_to_action is LEARN_MORE (the default when the post has a link), BOOK, ORDER, SHOP, SIGN_UP or CALL, which uses the profile's phone number. Google rejects updates with a phone number in the text. Delete works.YouTube and TikTokBoth take exactly one video per post and no images, and both connect with a connect link (OAuth). GET /v1/platforms says whether each is available; while a network's own app review is pending it is listed with in_review: true and has the limits described here.YouTube: the title comes from platform_options.youtube.title, else the title on the video in media, else the first line of the text (100 characters, no < or >). The text is the description (5,000 bytes). Options: privacy (public, unlisted, private), tags, category_id, made_for_kids, notify_subscribers, contains_synthetic_media. A vertical or square video of 3 minutes or less becomes a Short; there is no flag for it. media[].thumbnail sets a custom thumbnail when the channel is allowed one. GET /v1/posts/:id/metrics returns views, likes and comments. Deleting a video isn't available through the API. Until Google verifies our app, only test accounts can connect, and all customers share a daily upload quota.TikTok: the text is the caption (2,200 characters). platform_options.tiktok.privacy_level is required and has no default, because TikTok asks that the person posting choose it. The simplest way is approval: "required": the approval page then shows TikTok's own settings (the creator's name, who can watch, comments, Duets and Stitches, the branded-content disclosure and TikTok's consent line) and the person picks there. Otherwise set it yourself: PUBLIC_TO_EVERYONE, MUTUAL_FOLLOW_FRIENDS, FOLLOWER_OF_CREATOR or SELF_ONLY. Until TikTok audits our app, only SELF_ONLY is accepted, and only on accounts set to private (tiktok_private_only); the owner can change the video's visibility in the TikTok app afterwards. Other options: disable_comment, disable_duet, disable_stitch, cover_timestamp_ms, brand_organic, brand_content, ai_generated. TikTok processes the video after the upload, so the target's url is the video's link once TikTok reports it and the profile until then, and verified stays false while processing. There are no metrics or deletes for TikTok through the API.Idempotency and retriesSend Idempotency-Key (header) or idempotency_key (body). The same key and body returns the original post with Idempotent-Replayed: true; the same key with a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused.Retryable delivery failures are retried at 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m and 2h. After the last attempt the target is failed.Preflight issuesErrors block the post (422 preflight_failed with issues); warnings come back on the created post. Codes: text_too_long, too_many_media, too_many_videos, mixed_media, empty_post, duplicate_content, daily_cap_reached, account_needs_reauth, scheduled_in_past, scheduled_too_far, plan_limit_active_accounts, plan_limit_posts, x_credit_exhausted, key_daily_limit_reached; warning x_link_cost. When a Free-plan limit blocks a post, POST /v1/upgrade-links returns a payment link for the owner.Media uploadsMedia in a post is a list of public URLs. If your files aren't hosted anywhere, upload them to us first and use the returned url.Up to 4 MB: POST /v1/media with the raw bytes and their Content-Type, or JSON {data_base64, content_type}. Larger files, up to 200 MB: POST /v1/media/uploads {content_type, size_bytes?} returns a one-time upload_url (valid 2 hours); PUT the bytes to it with that Content-Type, for example curl --upload-file video.mp4 -H "Content-Type: video/mp4" "$UPLOAD_URL". Types: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, MP4, MOV, WebM. Files are stored in a private bucket; the url you get is an unguessable socialsforai.com link, so share it only as you would a private link. Files are deleted after 400 days. MCP tools: upload_media and create_media_upload.WebhooksPOST /v1/webhooks {url, events} returns a secret once. Events: post.published, post.partially_published, post.failed, post.canceled, post.deleted, post.updated, post.approval_requested, post.approved, post.rejected, account.connected, account.needs_reauth, account.disconnected. If you can't receive webhooks, GET /v1/events?after=<last_id> returns the same events (kept 30 days, oldest first) with a last_id to pass next time; wait holds the request until something arrives.Verify Socials-Signature: t=<unix>,v1=<hex>: v1 is HMAC-SHA256 of <t>.<raw body> with your secret. Non-2xx responses are retried for about a day.UsageGET /v1/usage returns active accounts this month, posts, your plan, the estimated cost and a cheaper plan if there is one.API keysGET /v1/keys lists your keys (prefix, name, scopes and limits, last used, and which one made the request). POST /v1/keys {name} returns a new key once. DELETE /v1/keys/:id revokes a key immediately.Limited keys, for handing one agent less than everything: POST /v1/keys {name, scopes?, account_ids?, require_approval?, daily_post_limit?}. Scopes are posts:read, posts:write (includes posts:read and accounts:read), accounts:read, accounts:write (includes accounts:read) and admin (everything, plus keys, webhooks, the owner email and upgrade links); leave scopes out for full access. account_ids limits the key to those accounts: it only lists them and can only post to them. require_approval: true makes every post from the key wait for a person. daily_post_limit caps the posts it creates in any 24 hours. A key with one of those three limits can't hold admin, and a key with account_ids can't hold accounts:write. Errors: 403 insufficient_scope (the fix names the scope), 403 account_not_allowed, 429 key_daily_limit_reached.Add an owner email when you create the workspace (POST /v1/workspaces {name, email}) or later with PATCH /v1/workspace {email} (only while none is set; GET /v1/workspace shows it). The owner signs in at /login with a one-time email link to create and revoke keys, add workspaces and recover access.To rotate: create a new key, deploy it, then revoke the old one. You can't revoke a workspace's last active key (409 last_active_key), so you can't lock yourself out. Up to 20 active keys per workspace.MCP serverNo key needed in clients that support MCP's OAuth sign-in (custom connectors, Claude Code and others): add https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp, and a browser window opens where you sign in with your email, pick or create a workspace, and approve. New users get an account in the same step. The client receives its own API key, which appears on the dashboard's API keys page and can be revoked there.Streamable HTTP at https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp with the same bearer key. Tools: list_platforms, list_accounts, create_connect_link, wait_for_connection, connect_account, upload_media, create_media_upload, create_post (waits by default), create_posts, wait_for_approval, get_post, list_posts, update_post, cancel_post, delete_post, get_post_metrics, list_replies, get_analytics, get_usage, create_upgrade_link, list_events, disconnect_account, get_workspace, set_owner_email, list_webhooks, create_webhook, delete_webhook, list_keys, create_key, revoke_key. Each tool is marked read-only, write or destructive so clients can decide what to run without asking. Four prompts give clients ready-made commands: post_everywhere (one message to every account, adapted per network), plan_week (draft and schedule a week of posts), answer_replies (draft answers to the replies under a post) and whats_new (failed posts, approvals and accounts needing reconnection since last time).OAuth scopes are the same five as API keys (posts:read, posts:write, accounts:read, accounts:write, admin); the consent screen lists what the client asked for, and the key it receives is limited to that. Clients can register dynamically or identify themselves with a Client ID Metadata Document URL. Server card: /.well-known/mcp/server-card.json.bashclaude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY"ApprovalsTo have a person sign off before anything goes out, create the post with approval: "required" (keys made with require_approval always do this). The post is stored as pending_approval, nothing is published, and the response carries approval: {status: "pending", url, note, decided_at}.Give approval.url to the person. It opens a page showing the exact text each account would publish, with Approve and Reject buttons and a note field; no sign-in is needed, and the link works for that one post only. If the workspace has an owner email, we send them the link too.Approve releases the post: it publishes right away, or stays scheduled for its scheduled_at. Reject cancels it (status: "canceled", approval.status: "rejected") and approval.note holds what the person wrote, so the agent can revise and submit a new post.To wait for the decision, call GET /v1/posts/:id?wait=45 (up to 120 seconds; call again while it is still pending_approval), or use the wait_for_approval MCP tool. Webhooks: post.approval_requested, post.approved, post.rejected. GET /v1/posts?status=pending_approval lists what is waiting, and DELETE /v1/posts/:id withdraws one.bashcurl -X POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -d '{"accounts":["acc_..."],"text":"Draft for review","approval":"required"}' # → {"status":"pending_approval","approval":{"status":"pending","url":"https://socialsforai.com/approve/..."}} curl "https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts/post_...?wait=45" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" # → approval.status: "approved" (publishing) or "rejected" (see approval.note)Upgrade linksAn agent can't pay, so it asks for a link: POST /v1/upgrade-links {plan} with hobby, pro, growth or scale returns {url, plan, kind, monthly_price}. Give url to the workspace owner; they pay by card on Stripe Checkout and the plan changes as soon as payment completes. A workspace that already subscribes gets Stripe's customer portal instead (kind: "portal").The workspace needs an owner email first (409 owner_email_required; set it with PATCH /v1/workspace {email}), so someone can sign in to manage or cancel the plan. MCP tool: create_upgrade_link.Rate limits and request idsRequests are limited per workspace per minute: 60 on Free, 120 on Hobby, 300 on Pro, 600 on Growth, 1,500 on Scale. Every authenticated response carries RateLimit-Limit, RateLimit-Remaining and RateLimit-Reset (seconds until the window resets). Over the limit you get 429 rate_limited with Retry-After; wait and retry with the same idempotency key.GET /v1/health (no key) reports the service's status: the API, the database, the publisher's last run and any overdue deliveries, and each network's delivery success over the last 24 hours. It answers 503 when the database or the publisher is down. The same numbers are at /status.Every response has a Request-Id header, and error bodies repeat it as error.request_id. Quote it when you ask us about a failed call.The API allows cross-origin requests (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *); auth is always the bearer key, never a cookie. Unknown paths under /v1 answer 404 not_found in the same JSON error shape.SDK, CLI and agent skillJavaScript and TypeScript: npm install @socialsforai/sdk. It covers every endpoint, has no dependencies, ships types, retries rate limits and server errors (honouring Retry-After), and sends an idempotency key with every post so its own retries can never publish twice. verifyWebhook checks webhook signatures. Example: const post = await new SocialsForAI({ apiKey }).posts.create({ accounts: ["linkedin"], text: "Hello", wait: true }).Python: pip install socialsforai. The same client with no dependencies (Python 3.9+): SocialsForAI().posts.create(["linkedin"], "Hello", wait=True). It also ships agent tools: from socialsforai.integrations.langchain import socials_tools (LangChain and LangGraph), .crewai (CrewAI) and .openai_agents (OpenAI Agents SDK), installed with the extras socialsforai[langchain], [crewai] or [openai-agents].Vercel AI SDK: npm install @socialsforai/ai-sdk, then generateText({ model, tools: socialsTools(), prompt }). The tools are the same in every framework: list_accounts, list_platforms, create_connect_link, create_post, create_posts, get_post, list_posts, get_post_metrics, list_replies, list_events, and delete_post, which you have to turn on. Errors come back to the model with their fix.npx @socialsforai/cli wraps the REST API for agents with a shell: JSON on stdout, errors (with their fix) as JSON on stderr and a non-zero exit code. socials signup creates a workspace and saves the key; socials post --dry-run validates; socials connect --wait creates a connect link and waits for the owner.The agent skill teaches an agent the whole workflow: npx skills add SocialsForAi/socialsforai. The same repository is a Claude Code plugin (/plugin marketplace add SocialsForAi/socialsforai) and carries manifests for Cursor and Gemini CLI. Source: https://github.com/SocialsForAi/socialsforai. The skill is also served at /skill.md.bashnpx @socialsforai/cli signup --name "My agent" --email you@example.com npx @socialsforai/cli connect --platforms bluesky,linkedin --wait npx @socialsforai/cli post --accounts linkedin --text "Hello" --dry-run npx @socialsforai/cli post --accounts linkedin --text "Hello" --idempotency-key first-postMachine-readable docs/llms.txt is the full API guide in plain text; /llms-full.txt adds every guide and comparison page. /openapi.json is the OpenAPI 3.1 description, generated from the same schemas the API validates with. GET /v1 lists every endpoint.Every page on this site is available as Markdown: add .md to the path (/pricing.md, /docs.md, /mcp/linkedin.md) or send Accept: text/markdown. /auth.md explains how an agent gets credentials, and /.well-known/api-catalog links all of the above.SandboxThe sandbox is a fake network for building and testing: nothing is posted anywhere. Connect one with POST /v1/accounts {"platform": "sandbox", "credentials": {}} (MCP connect_account), or with a connect link for platforms: ["sandbox"]. Sandbox accounts don't count toward your plan.Put [fail:retryable], [fail:permanent] or [fail:auth] in the text to test each failure path, and [replies] to get two replies under the post for trying GET /v1/posts/:id/replies.

https://socialsforai.com/instagram-api.body_text: Instagram Posting API (2026): Requirements, Limits | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyInstagram posting APIPosting to Instagram by API means passing Meta's review first.Instagram publishing isn't live on our API yet. This is a guide to Meta's own Content Publishing API: what it needs, what it accepts, and its limits.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Instagram's Content Publishing API lets an app publish images, carousels of up to 20 items, reels and stories to Instagram professional accounts (business or creator). Publishing takes two calls: create a media container from a public URL, then publish it. Serving accounts your app doesn't own or manage needs Advanced Access, which requires Meta App Review and Business Verification.Instagram: coming soon. Built; in Meta app review. Everything else on this page describes the API as it works today.Instagram API media requirementsMediaFormatSize and lengthShapeFeed imageJPEG onlyUp to 8 MBAspect ratio 4:5 to 1.91:1; width 320 to 1440 pxReelMOV or MP4, H.264 or HEVC, AAC audio3 seconds to 15 minutes; up to 300 MBUp to 1920 px wide; 9:16 recommended; 23 to 60 fpsStory videoSame as reels3 to 60 seconds; up to 100 MB9:16 recommendedStory imageJPEGUp to 8 MB9:16 recommendedCarouselImages, videos or a mixUp to 20 itemsCropped to the first item's ratio, default 1:1CaptionText2,200 characters, 30 hashtags, 20 @ tagsNot supported on carousel itemsFrom Meta's IG User Media reference and content publishing guide, read 2026-11-01.Does SocialsForAI support Instagram yet?No. Instagram publishing isn't available on our API yet: it needs Meta's App Review for the publishing permissions, and our app doesn't have that approval. We'll mark it live only after a real post goes through end to end, and it will appear in GET /v1/platforms when it does.What works today: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live. If you need Instagram now, the official API below is the route. Our social media API page covers what one call does on the networks that are ready.What do you need to publish to Instagram by API?Meta's content publishing guide requires an Instagram professional account, which Meta describes as a business or creator account. Personal accounts aren't covered by the publishing API. Beyond the account, you need a Meta app, a login flow and the publishing permission for that login type.Instagram Login (graph.instagram.com): works without a linked Facebook Page. Permissions instagram_business_basic and instagram_business_content_publish.Facebook Login (graph.facebook.com): the professional account must be linked to a Facebook Page the user can administer. Permissions instagram_basic, instagram_content_publish and pages_read_engagement.Advanced Access: needed to serve accounts you don't own or manage. It requires Meta App Review and Business Verification; Standard Access only covers people with a role on your app.Public media hosting: Meta fetches the file from your URL, which must be publicly reachable at the moment of the request.Page Publishing Authorization: if the linked Page requires it, the account can't be published to until it's completed.How does Instagram's two-step publishing flow work?First POST /<IG_ID>/media with an image_url (or video_url and a media_type such as REELS or STORIES) and a caption. Meta returns a container id. Then POST /<IG_ID>/media_publish with creation_id set to that id, and Meta returns the published media id.Videos process asynchronously. Check GET /<CONTAINER_ID>?fields=status_code until it reads FINISHED; Meta suggests polling once a minute for no more than 5 minutes. Other values are IN_PROGRESS, ERROR, PUBLISHED and EXPIRED, which means the container wasn't published within 24 hours.Carousels add a step: create a container per item with is_carousel_item=true, then a CAROUSEL container listing up to 20 child ids, then publish that.bash# 1. Create a container (Instagram Login host shown) curl -X POST "https://graph.instagram.com/<API_VERSION>/<IG_ID>/media" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $IG_USER_TOKEN" \ -d "image_url=https://cdn.example.com/launch.jpg" \ -d "caption=We shipped webhooks." # → { "id": "<IG_CONTAINER_ID>" } # 2. Publish it curl -X POST "https://graph.instagram.com/<API_VERSION>/<IG_ID>/media_publish" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $IG_USER_TOKEN" \ -d "creation_id=<IG_CONTAINER_ID>" # → { "id": "<IG_MEDIA_ID>" }How many posts can you publish per day with the Instagram API?Meta's rate limit section says 100 API-published posts per account within a 24-hour moving period, with a carousel counting as one post. The same guide's carousel section says 50, so plan for the lower number until your own limit check says otherwise.Check the live number with GET /<IG_ID>/content_publishing_limit before a batch. The limit is enforced on the media_publish call, so that is where an over-limit error appears.What can't the Instagram API publish?Meta's guide lists the gaps. The ones that surprise people:Image formats other than JPEG. PNG and WebP must be converted first.Shopping tags and filters.Link, poll and location stickers on stories.Alt text on reels and stories; alt_text (up to 1,000 characters) works on image posts only.Captions, locations or tags on individual carousel items; they go on the carousel container.Personal accounts. The account has to be converted to business or creator.How long do Instagram API tokens last?Authorization codes and short-lived access tokens are valid for one hour. Exchange the short-lived token for a long-lived one, which is valid for 60 days and can be refreshed before it expires, per Meta's platform overview.Build the refresh into a scheduled job. A token that lapses means the account owner has to log in again, which is the same failure mode as LinkedIn's 60-day tokens described on our LinkedIn API page.What will Instagram look like on SocialsForAI?When Instagram goes live, accounts will connect through the same connect link and post through the same POST /v1/posts as X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr. Our API already takes media as public URLs, which is what Meta's container flow expects.One honest limit: every Instagram container needs an image or video URL, so text-only crossposts won't apply there. Video itself already posts through our API on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon and Telegram. Until Instagram is live, the TikTok API guide covers the other video-first network on our list, and pricing shows how accounts are billed.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Instagram content publishing (Meta for Developers) · Instagram Platform overview: login types, access levels, tokens (Meta) · IG User Media reference: media specs and parameters (Meta) · Meta App Review (Meta for Developers)QuestionsWhat developers askCan I post to a personal Instagram account by API?+No. Meta's content publishing guide requires an Instagram professional account, which Meta describes as representing a business or creator. The publishing permissions, instagram_business_content_publish or instagram_content_publish, act on that professional account through Instagram Login or Facebook Login. Personal accounts aren't covered.Is the Instagram API free?+Meta's content publishing docs list no per-call price. The costs are access and limits: Advanced Access to publish for accounts you don't manage requires Meta App Review and Business Verification, and each account can publish a limited number of API posts per 24 hours.Do I need a Facebook Page to use the Instagram API?+Not with Instagram Login, which serves professional accounts without a linked Facebook Page through graph.instagram.com. Facebook Login does need the account linked to a Facebook Page that the user can administer, and uses graph.facebook.com with Page tokens. Pick the login type before you build.How many posts per day can the Instagram API publish?+Meta's rate limit section says 100 API-published posts per account in a 24-hour moving period, counting a carousel as one. Another section of the same guide says 50. Check the account's current usage with the content_publishing_limit endpoint before publishing a batch.Why does the Instagram API need a public image URL?+The publishing flow doesn't take a file upload for images. You pass image_url, and Meta fetches the file from it, so it must be publicly reachable at that moment. Only JPEG is supported for images. Videos can also use resumable uploads with Facebook Login for Business.When will Instagram work on your API?+After our app has Meta's App Review approval, which it doesn't have yet. This page will show the change, Instagram will appear in the platforms endpoint, and we only mark Instagram live once a real post goes through end to end. Connected accounts will then use the same connect link and posts endpoint.Keep readingSocial media APITikTok posting APICrosspost to X, Bluesky and LinkedInMCP server for social mediaGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/linkedin-api.body_text: LinkedIn API for Posting (2026): Permissions, ExampleSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyLinkedIn API for postingPost to LinkedIn from code without the Restli homework.LinkedIn's Posts API wants a versioned header, a protocol header, a person URN and its own text format. Here is all of it, from LinkedIn's docs, and the one-call version.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026LinkedIn's API lets an app create posts on a member's behalf through the Posts API (POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts) with the self-serve w_member_social permission, or on a Company Page with w_organization_social, which needs Community Management API approval. Every request needs a Linkedin-Version header in YYYYMM format and X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0. Posts can be up to 3,000 characters.LinkedIn: live. Posting to LinkedIn works on the API today.LinkedIn posting permissionsPermissionWhat it allowsHow you get itw_member_socialPost, comment and like as the signed-in memberSelf-serve: add the Share on LinkedIn product in the Developer Portalopenid, profileIdentify the member (gives the id for the person URN)Self-serve: Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connectw_organization_socialPost, comment and like as a Company PageCommunity Management API approval; member must be ADMINISTRATOR, CONTENT_ADMIN or DIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTERr_member_socialRead a member's postsClosed: LinkedIn isn't accepting requestsFrom LinkedIn's Posts API, Share on LinkedIn and Community Management docs on Microsoft Learn, read 2026-11-01.What can you post with the LinkedIn API?LinkedIn's Posts API creates organic posts with text, images, video, documents, articles, multi-image sets, polls and celebrations. Carousels are sponsored-only: LinkedIn's docs say organic carousels are not currently supported.The Posts API replaces the older ugcPosts API. Some LinkedIn pages, including Share on LinkedIn, still show ugcPosts examples, so check which one a tutorial uses before copying it.Through SocialsForAI you can post text, up to 20 images, or 1 MP4 video up to 200 MB to personal profiles today. Documents, polls and Company Pages aren't supported yet.How do you get a LinkedIn API access token?LinkedIn uses a standard 3-legged OAuth flow: send the member to https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization with your scopes, receive a code on your redirect URL, and exchange it at https://www.linkedin.com/oauth/v2/accessToken. The authorization code lives 30 minutes.Access tokens currently last 60 days. Programmatic refresh tokens are only available to a limited set of partners; everyone else sends the member back through the authorization flow, which skips the consent screen if they're still logged in and the old token hasn't expired.Two gotchas from LinkedIn's OAuth page: requesting a different set of scopes invalidates the member's previous tokens, and you should store tokens with room for at least 1,000 characters even though they are about 500 today.What does a raw LinkedIn post request look like?A text post is a JSON body with author (a urn:li:person:{id} URN), commentary, visibility, a distribution object and lifecycleState: PUBLISHED. The person id is the sub field from the OpenID Connect userinfo endpoint (GET https://api.linkedin.com/v2/userinfo).LinkedIn answers 201 and puts the post id, such as urn:li:share:6844785523593134080, in the x-restli-id response header rather than the body, so a client that only parses the body misses it.bashcurl -X POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $LINKEDIN_TOKEN" \ -H "Linkedin-Version: 202610" \ -H "X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "author": "urn:li:person:782bbtaQ", "commentary": "Shipped webhooks today \\(finally\\).", "visibility": "PUBLIC", "distribution": { "feedDistribution": "MAIN_FEED", "targetEntities": [], "thirdPartyDistributionChannels": [] }, "lifecycleState": "PUBLISHED", "isReshareDisabledByAuthor": false }' # 201 Created, header x-restli-id: urn:li:share:...Why does LinkedIn drop parentheses and @ signs?The commentary field uses LinkedIn's "little text" format, where ( ) [ ] { } < > @ | * _ ~ \ are reserved. A mention is written @[Name](urn:li:organization:123), so a stray parenthesis or @ can be read as markup and the text around it lost or rejected. Escape each reserved character with a backslash.We escape them all automatically and leave hashtags intact. The trade-off: because @ is escaped, LinkedIn @mentions aren't supported through our API yet. Preview how a post will look with the LinkedIn text formatter, and check length against the LinkedIn character limit.How do images work in the LinkedIn API?Images are a separate two-step upload. Call POST /rest/images?action=initializeUpload with the owner URN, upload the bytes to the returned uploadUrl, then reference the returned urn:li:image:... in the post's content.media.id.The Images API accepts JPG, GIF and PNG under 36,152,320 pixels, and GIFs up to 250 frames. Several images in one organic post use the MultiImage format. A token with only w_member_social can upload but can't GET the image back on the versioned API.jsonPOST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/images?action=initializeUpload { "initializeUploadRequest": { "owner": "urn:li:person:782bbtaQ" } } 200 → { "value": { "uploadUrlExpiresAt": 1650567510704, "uploadUrl": "https://www.linkedin.com/dms-uploads/...", "image": "urn:li:image:C4E10AQFoyyAjHPMQuQ" } }What errors does the LinkedIn Posts API return?LinkedIn documents its Posts API errors by HTTP status and message. The ones you hit in practice, and what each becomes when you post through us:400 FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG: commentary over the limit. We catch it first as text_too_long at 3,000 characters.400 MISSING_FIELD or INVALID_URN_TYPE: a malformed body or the wrong URN in author. We build the body, so you shouldn't see these.401 EMPTY_ACCESS_TOKEN or an expired token: becomes auth_expired; we try one refresh, and without a refresh token the account moves to needs_reauth.403 ACCESS_DENIED: the scope or the Company Page role is missing.429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: becomes platform_rate_limited and retries on our backoff schedule.500 and 503: become platform_unavailable and retry.What are the LinkedIn API rate limits?LinkedIn doesn't publish standard rate limits. They are per day, reset at midnight UTC, and come in two kinds: per application and per member per application. You see your app's limits in the Developer Portal's Analytics tab, only for endpoints you've called at least once that day.Two published numbers exist. The Share on LinkedIn page lists 150 requests per member and 100,000 per application per day. The Community Management API's development tier allows 500 requests per app and 100 per member. Over a limit, LinkedIn returns 429.Separately, LinkedIn Help says it may limit how many posts a member or Page makes in a period, without giving a number. Our own cap is 50 posts per LinkedIn account per 24 hours.What does the Linkedin-Version header do?Linkedin-Version pins the monthly API version your request is written against, in YYYYMM format. LinkedIn retires old versions: the November 2025 version (202511) sunsets on November 16, 2026, per the deprecation notice on the Posts API page.If you call LinkedIn directly, keep the version in one config value and schedule a check before each sunset. We send the header on every request and keep the version in one place on our side.How do you post to LinkedIn with one call?Send plain text and public image URLs to POST /v1/posts. We escape reserved characters, upload images through the Images API, add both headers, read the post id from x-restli-id and return the post URL.When a 60-day token expires, the next publish attempt fails with account_needs_reauth, the account flips to needs_reauth and an account.needs_reauth webhook fires, so you can send the owner a fresh connect link before the next scheduled post. To plan posts ahead, see schedule LinkedIn posts; for agents, the LinkedIn MCP server.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-0412" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_bluesky", "acc_linkedin", "acc_x"], "text": "We just shipped webhooks.", "wait": true }'Posting to LinkedIn with the raw API01Create a developer appCreate an app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal and add an absolute HTTPS redirect URL on the Auth tab. Note the client id and secret.02Add two productsOn the Products tab add Share on LinkedIn (grants w_member_social) and Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect (grants openid and profile).03Run OAuthSend the member to the authorization URL with scope openid profile w_member_social, then exchange the code within 30 minutes for a 60-day access token.04Build the person URNCall the userinfo endpoint with the token and prefix its sub value: urn:li:person:{sub}.05Create the postPOST to /rest/posts with the Linkedin-Version and X-Restli-Protocol-Version headers, escaped commentary, and read the post id from the x-restli-id header.Sources, read 2026-11-01: LinkedIn Posts API (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn Help: post limits · Share on LinkedIn: w_member_social and daily limits (Microsoft Learn) · Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn 3-legged OAuth flow: token lifetimes (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn Images API (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn API rate limiting (Microsoft Learn) · Community Management API overview and tiers (Microsoft Learn)QuestionsWhat developers askIs the LinkedIn API free?+LinkedIn doesn't charge per call for posting. Member posting through Share on LinkedIn is self-serve and free. The cost is access: Company Page posting needs Community Management API approval, reading member posts is closed, and tokens expire every 60 days without partner-level refresh tokens.How do I get LinkedIn API access for posting?+Create an app in the LinkedIn Developer Portal, open the Products tab and add Share on LinkedIn, which grants w_member_social, plus Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect to identify the member. Both are self-serve. Company Page posting needs a separate Community Management API application.Can I post to a LinkedIn Company Page with the API?+Yes, with w_organization_social, when the authenticated member is an administrator, content admin or direct sponsored content poster of the page and the app has Community Management API access, which LinkedIn vets in two tiers. Our API posts to personal profiles only for now.How long is a LinkedIn post allowed to be?+Up to 3,000 characters, per LinkedIn Help. Over the limit, the Posts API returns 400 FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG. Our preflight check rejects longer text with text_too_long before anything is sent, so a too-long post never reaches LinkedIn and you can fix it in the same request cycle.Why did my LinkedIn post lose its parentheses?+Commentary uses LinkedIn's little text format, where parentheses, brackets, braces, angle brackets, @, pipe, asterisk, underscore, tilde and backslash are reserved and must be escaped with a backslash. Unescaped, LinkedIn can treat them as markup. Our API escapes them for you.How long do LinkedIn API access tokens last?+LinkedIn currently issues access tokens with a 60-day lifespan. Programmatic refresh tokens are limited to approved partners. Without one, the member goes through the authorization flow again; if they're still logged in and the token is valid, LinkedIn skips the consent screen.What is the LinkedIn API rate limit for posting?+LinkedIn doesn't publish standard limits; you see your app's limits in the Developer Portal Analytics tab. The Share on LinkedIn page lists 150 requests per member and 100,000 per app per day. Limits reset at midnight UTC and over-limit calls return 429.Keep readingLinkedIn API pricingLinkedIn MCP serverLinkedIn text formatterSchedule LinkedIn postsLinkedIn character limitGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/linkedin-api-pr.body_text: LinkedIn API Pricing (2026): What Posting Costs | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyLinkedIn API pricingLinkedIn's API costs nothing per call. Access is the price.There's no per-post fee from LinkedIn. What you pay in is approval time, scope limits, 60-day token refreshes and version migrations.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026LinkedIn doesn't publish per-request prices for its posting APIs. Creating member posts with w_member_social is available to any app through the self-serve Share on LinkedIn product. Posting as a Company Page needs Community Management API approval, and reading member posts is closed to new applicants. The practical costs are review time, 60-day access tokens and keeping up with versioned headers.LinkedIn: live. Posting to LinkedIn works on the API today.LinkedIn posting access: what's free and what's gatedProductPermissionAccessFeeShare on LinkedInw_member_socialSelf-serve from the Developer Portal Products tabNone publishedSign In with LinkedIn (OpenID Connect)openid, profile, emailSelf-serveNone publishedCommunity Management APIw_organization_social and page analyticsVetted: development tier, then standard tier with a screencastNone publishedMember Post Managementr_member_socialClosed to new requestsNot availableFrom LinkedIn's docs on Microsoft Learn, read 2026-11-01. LinkedIn's docs list no per-call price for these products.Cost of LinkedIn accounts through SocialsForAIActive accounts in a monthCheapest planMonthly price1 to 3Free (100 posts a month)$05Hobby$910Hobby + 5 extra at $2$1925Pro$2960Pro + 35 extra at $1$64100Growth$79Computed with cheapestPlan() from src/lib/pricing.ts. Active means the account published that month, on any network. Paid plans never block a post; overage is billed at period end, capped at this cheapest-plan price.Does LinkedIn charge for API access?No per-call fee is published for posting. The Posts API, Share on LinkedIn and Community Management API pages describe permissions, tiers and rate limits but no prices, so a post you create through LinkedIn's API costs nothing from LinkedIn.Many results for "LinkedIn API pricing" are about third-party data APIs that scrape profiles and charge per lookup. Those are separate companies with their own pricing, not LinkedIn's official API. For publishing posts, the official Posts API is the route this page prices.What does Community Management API approval involve?The Community Management API is how an app posts as a Company Page and reads page analytics. LinkedIn calls it a vetted product with two tiers: a development tier with limited call volume, then a standard tier you apply for with a screencast showing each use case on your access form.The development tier allows 500 requests per app and 100 per member per day. LinkedIn only lets you request it on a new developer app that has no other API products; if you already have Advertising API access, LinkedIn's FAQ describes creating a second app for verification, then adding standard access to the original.Partners also go through a technical sign-off against LinkedIn's integration requirements. None of this has a published fee; it costs calendar time and a working product to demo.What are the hidden costs of LinkedIn's free API?The bill is zero; the maintenance isn't. What you sign up to when you integrate directly:Reauthorization every 60 days. Access tokens last 60 days and programmatic refresh tokens are limited to partners, so members click through OAuth again.Version migrations. Every request carries a Linkedin-Version header, and versions retire: 202511 sunsets on November 16, 2026.Unpublished rate limits. You discover them per endpoint in the Developer Portal Analytics tab, after making at least one call that day.Little text escaping. Reserved characters in commentary need backslashes, or text goes missing. See the LinkedIn API guide.Two-step image uploads through the Images API, and the post id returned in a header rather than the body.What does LinkedIn posting cost through SocialsForAI?A LinkedIn account counts as one active account in any month it publishes, the same as an X or Bluesky account. Posts are unlimited on paid plans, and connected accounts that sit idle that month cost nothing.So a consultant posting from one profile fits on Free; an agency posting for 25 clients' profiles fits on Pro at $29; 60 profiles is $64 on Pro with overage. LinkedIn is live on our API for personal profiles only. Full plan table on pricing.When is LinkedIn's own API the cheaper choice?If you post to your own LinkedIn profile and nothing else, the direct API is the cheapest option: free, self-serve, and two OAuth calls plus one post request. Budget a reconnect every 60 days and a version bump now and then.If you need Company Pages, LinkedIn's own API with Community Management approval is currently the only option we'd recommend, because we don't post to pages yet. A unified API earns its keep when you post to LinkedIn and other networks together, or for many people's profiles, and want token expiry handled with a webhook instead of a support ticket. For agents, see the LinkedIn MCP server.Sources, read 2026-11-01: LinkedIn Posts API (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn Help: post limits · Share on LinkedIn: w_member_social and daily limits (Microsoft Learn) · Sign In with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect (Microsoft Learn) · Community Management API overview and tiers (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn 3-legged OAuth flow: token lifetimes (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn API rate limiting (Microsoft Learn)QuestionsWhat developers askDoes LinkedIn charge for API calls?+Not for posting. LinkedIn's docs for the Posts API, Share on LinkedIn and the Community Management API list permissions, tiers and rate limits but no per-call prices. Access is gated by approval rather than metered. Third-party LinkedIn data APIs do charge, but they are separate companies, not LinkedIn.Is the LinkedIn Posts API free for personal profiles?+Yes. Add the self-serve Share on LinkedIn product to your developer app to get w_member_social, run OAuth, and post as the member at no charge. The Share on LinkedIn page lists 150 requests per member and 100,000 per application per day.How do I get Community Management API access?+Apply from a new developer app with no other API products. You start on a development tier with 500 requests per app and 100 per member per day, then apply for the standard tier with a screencast of each use case. No fee is published.How long do LinkedIn access tokens last?+LinkedIn currently issues access tokens with a 60-day lifespan. Programmatic refresh tokens are available to a limited set of partners only, so most apps send members back through OAuth every 60 days. Through our API, the account flips to needs_reauth and a webhook fires.Can I get r_member_social to read LinkedIn posts?+Not at the moment. LinkedIn describes r_member_social as a closed permission and says it isn't accepting access requests due to resource constraints. Apps that only post don't need it: LinkedIn returns the new post's id in the x-restli-id header when the post is created.What do you charge per LinkedIn post?+Nothing per post. You pay per active account per month, meaning an account that published that month on any network. Posts are unlimited on paid plans. Free covers 3 active accounts and 100 posts a month; Hobby is $9 for 5 accounts.Keep readingLinkedIn API guideLinkedIn MCP serverSchedule LinkedIn postsX API pricingPricingGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →
