https://socialsforai.com/linkedin-charac.body_text: LinkedIn Character Limit (2026): 3,000 Characters per PostSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyLinkedIn character limit3,000 characters per post. Here's what counts.LinkedIn allows 3,000 characters in a post. What counts, what LinkedIn's API does with longer text, and what our API checks before sending.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026LinkedIn posts can contain up to 3,000 characters, according to LinkedIn Help. Spaces, line breaks, emoji, hashtags and links all count toward it; images don't. Through LinkedIn's Posts API, text that's too long is rejected with FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG. LinkedIn suggests writing an article if a post won't fit.LinkedIn: live. Posting to LinkedIn works on the API today.LinkedIn post length versus X and BlueskyNetworkPost limitCounted asA URL countsAn emoji countsLinkedIn3,000CharactersIts full length1 in our countX280Weighted characters232Bluesky300 (and 3,000 bytes)GraphemesIts full length1Limits from LinkedIn Help, docs.x.com and the Bluesky post lexicon, read 2026-11-01. LinkedIn doesn't publish its counting unit; the LinkedIn emoji column is how our API counts.What is the LinkedIn character limit for posts?3,000 characters. LinkedIn Help's page on posting updates says "Posts can contain up to 3,000 characters," and that if you need more, you can write an article using LinkedIn's publishing platform instead. That's roughly 10 times X's 280 and 10 times Bluesky's 300.LinkedIn Help also says it "may limit how many posts a member or a LinkedIn Page can make in a certain time period." Length isn't the only constraint; frequency is limited too, though LinkedIn doesn't publish the number. Our API caps each LinkedIn account at 50 posts per 24 hours.What counts toward the 3,000 characters?Everything in the text: letters, spaces, punctuation, line breaks, emoji, hashtags and URLs at their full length. Unlike X, LinkedIn doesn't count links as a fixed 23. Images, documents and other attachments don't count toward the text limit.LinkedIn doesn't document its counting unit. Our API counts graphemes, what a reader sees as one character, so 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 counts 1 and café counts 4. For ordinary text, every method gives the same answer. Where they differ, mostly with emoji and Unicode bold letters, leave some headroom near 3,000.Worked examples: how long is a LinkedIn post?Counts below are graphemes, as our API's preflight measures them.Hiring: staff engineer, platform team. Remote in US time zones. Details and the full job description are on our careers page. is 125 characters, about 4% of the limit.A post with a 56-character tracking URL spends 56 of the 3,000 on it, not 23 as on X.Two paragraphs separated by a blank line spend 2 characters on the line breaks.𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱 in Unicode bold is 4 graphemes but 8 UTF-16 code units. If LinkedIn counts code units, bold text costs double; we don't know which it uses, so treat bold-heavy posts near the limit with care.A 3,001-character post fails our preflight with text_too_long before LinkedIn sees it.What happens if a post is over 3,000 characters?In LinkedIn's app, you can't publish it until you shorten it. Through LinkedIn's Posts API, the request fails with a 400 and the error FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG, which LinkedIn describes as a field length exceeding the allowed maximum, with the advice to reduce the commentary.Through our API, it doesn't get that far. Preflight returns a 422 preflight_failed with a text_too_long issue such as "Text is 3120 characters; LinkedIn allows 3000." and the fix "Shorten it by 120+ characters, or set platform_options.linkedin.text to a shorter version." Nothing is published, and dry_run: true gives the same check without storing anything.Do mentions, hashtags and special characters cost extra?LinkedIn's API takes post text in its "little" text format, where characters like ( ) [ ] { } < > @ | * _ ~ \ have meaning; a mention is written @[Name](urn:li:organization:...). We escape those reserved characters with a backslash so they appear as typed, and leave #hashtags intact so they still link.That escaping happens after we count. Q&A (live) with @team: bring [questions] *now* is 46 characters as you wrote it and 53 after escaping. LinkedIn doesn't document whether escape characters count toward its limit, so a post right at 3,000 with many brackets or asterisks is worth trimming a little.Can you use bold or italic text on LinkedIn?Not natively. LinkedIn posts have no bold or italic formatting, so people use Unicode letters that look bold or italic. Our LinkedIn text formatter converts text that way, and warns that screen readers read those letters poorly. Use it for a word or two, not whole paragraphs.To see how a draft will look in the feed, including where line breaks fall, paste it into the LinkedIn post preview.How do I shorten a LinkedIn post?If you're over 3,000, these give back the most characters for the least rewriting.Shorten tracking URLs. Every character of a link counts on LinkedIn.Cut blank lines between short paragraphs; each one costs 1 to 2 characters and they add up in list-style posts.Move long-form content into a LinkedIn article, which LinkedIn Help suggests when a post won't fit, and link to it from a short post.If you crosspost, keep the long version for LinkedIn and send shorter ones to X and Bluesky with platform_options. See crossposting and scheduling LinkedIn posts from the API.Sources, read 2026-11-01: LinkedIn Posts API (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn Help: post limitsQuestionsWhat developers askWhat is the character limit for a LinkedIn post?+3,000 characters, according to LinkedIn Help. Spaces, line breaks, emoji, hashtags and links all count, and links count at their full length. Attachments such as images don't count. If a post needs more room, LinkedIn suggests writing an article with its publishing platform instead.Do spaces and line breaks count on LinkedIn?+Yes. Every space and line break counts toward the 3,000-character limit. A blank line between paragraphs costs at least 2 characters, which matters in list-style posts with many short lines. Our API counts them the same way when it checks length before publishing.Do links count toward LinkedIn's character limit?+Yes, at their full length. LinkedIn doesn't shorten links to a fixed count the way X does with t.co, so a 120-character tracking URL uses 120 of your 3,000 characters. Shorten long URLs before posting if you're close to the limit.What happens if I post more than 3,000 characters through the API?+LinkedIn's Posts API rejects it with a 400 FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG error. Our API checks first and returns a 422 with a text_too_long issue that states your count, the 3,000 limit and how much to cut. Nothing is published, and a dry run gives the same answer without storing the post.Is the LinkedIn comment limit the same as the post limit?+This page covers posts. LinkedIn Help's page on posting lists the post limit at 3,000 characters and doesn't give a comment limit, so we don't state one here. Our API creates posts, not comments, and checks every post against 3,000 characters before sending it to LinkedIn, returning text_too_long with the exact overage.Can I use bold text in a LinkedIn post?+LinkedIn has no native bold or italic in posts. People substitute Unicode letters that look bold, which our LinkedIn text formatter produces. Screen readers often read them letter by letter or skip them, and each one may cost more than one character, so use them sparingly.Keep readingLinkedIn text formatterLinkedIn post previewLinkedIn APISchedule LinkedIn postsX character limitGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/mcp.body_text: Social Media MCP Server for AI Agents (LinkedIn, X, Bluesky)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keySocial media MCP serverOne MCP server for every network your agent posts to.Hosted, Streamable HTTP, bearer-key auth. The same preflight, idempotency and receipts as the REST API.LinkedIn MCP serverHosted LinkedIn MCP server for personal profiles. What each tool returns for LinkedIn, a worked dry-run session, the 60-day token, escaping, caps and error fixes.X (Twitter) MCP serverHosted X MCP server. What each tool returns for X, the 280 weighted-character and $0.20 link-post rules, OAuth with refresh, and X-specific error fixes.Bluesky MCP serverHosted Bluesky MCP server, live today. What each tool returns for Bluesky, app-password setup, facets, a worked session, caps and Bluesky error fixes.What is a social media MCP server?A social media MCP server exposes posting as tools an AI agent can call through the Model Context Protocol. Instead of writing an integration per network, the agent calls create_post with account ids and text, and the server handles each network's API, limits and errors.SocialsForAI's server runs at https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp over Streamable HTTP and authenticates with the same bearer API key as the REST API. It exposes thirty tools: list_platforms, list_accounts, create_connect_link, wait_for_connection, connect_account, upload_media, create_media_upload, create_post, create_posts, wait_for_approval, get_post, list_posts, update_post, cancel_post, delete_post, get_post_metrics, list_replies, get_analytics, get_usage, create_upgrade_link, list_events, disconnect_account, get_workspace, set_owner_email, list_webhooks, create_webhook, delete_webhook, list_keys, create_key and revoke_key.Why use a hosted server instead of one per network?Running your own MCP server for a network usually means registering your own developer app with that network, keeping its client secret on your machine, and running a separate server per platform. A hosted server needs one key and one connection, and the account owner approves access on the network's own screen through a connect link.It also applies the same rules on every network before anything goes out: length counted the way each network counts it, duplicate text on the same account within 24 hours, image limits, and a per-account daily cap. Those checks are ordinary code with no AI calls, and a dry run returns each problem with a fix the agent can act on.Which networks work today?Eight networks are live: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn (personal profiles and Company Pages), Mastodon (any server), Telegram (channels and groups, through a bot), Discord and Slack (a channel, through its webhook) and Nostr (your own key and relays). Instagram, Threads and Facebook are built and waiting on Meta's review; YouTube, TikTok and Reddit are built and waiting on theirs; Pinterest is planned. The list_platforms tool returns the current status and what each network supports (threads, polls, documents, delete, metrics, reading replies), so an agent never has to guess.Keeping a human in the loopFor X and LinkedIn, the account owner approves access on the network's own page: the agent sends a connect link and calls wait_for_connection to pick up as soon as they finish. Bluesky, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord and Slack connect with an app password, token or webhook URL, so an agent can connect them itself with connect_account when the owner hands over those credentials (never a main password). A Nostr key is the whole account, so the owner should paste it into a connect link themselves. For posting, the safest pattern is to have the agent call create_post with dry_run: true, show you the preview, and publish only after you confirm. Passing an idempotency_key means a retried tool call never posts twice.An agent with a posting tool can publish something wrong faster than a person can read it. The server gives you five controls; use the ones that fit.Dry run first. dry_run: true runs every preflight check and returns the exact text each account would get, without publishing or consuming an idempotency key. The checks are plain code with no AI calls and no cost.Ask for approval. Have the agent create the post with approval: "required": it is held as pending_approval and you get a link showing the exact text for each network, with Approve and Reject buttons. Nothing goes out until you approve, and a rejection note goes back to the agent. You can also leave your client's tool approval prompt on for create_post.Limit the key. Give an agent its own API key with only the scopes it needs, a list of accounts it may post to, a daily post cap, or require_approval so every post it creates waits for you.Send an idempotency key. If the agent retries after a timeout with the same key and the same body, it gets the original post back instead of a second one.Rely on the caps. Each account has a fair-use cap per rolling 24 hours: 100 on X, 300 on Bluesky and Mastodon, 50 on LinkedIn, 500 on Telegram (daily_cap_reached). Identical text to the same account within 24 hours is blocked with duplicate_content.Every tool and its inputsThe server exposes thirty tools. None of them is tied to one network: the same create_post call can target accounts on several networks at once, with a different text per network through platform_options. Inputs below are the real schema fields. The LinkedIn, X and Bluesky pages describe what each tool returns for that network.list_platforms (no input): each platform's id, name, whether it's available on this server, and its limits: maxChars, maxImages, supportsVideo, video (count, size and mixing rules), dailyPostCap.list_accounts (platform?, external_ref?): connected accounts with id, platform, handle, display_name, status (active or needs_reauth) and connected_at. The ids go into create_post.create_connect_link (platforms?, external_ref?, redirect_url?, expires_in?): a hosted URL the account owner opens, plus its id. expires_in is 300 seconds to 30 days and defaults to 7 days. Required for X and LinkedIn, where the owner approves on the network's own page.wait_for_connection (id, wait_seconds 0 to 120, default 45, until: all or any): waits while the owner uses a connect link and returns status (connected, partially_connected, waiting or expired), the connected accounts and pending_platforms. Call it again while the status is waiting.connect_account (platform, credentials, external_ref?): connects a Bluesky (identifier, app_password), Mastodon (instance, access_token), Telegram (bot_token, chat_id), Discord (webhook_url), Slack (webhook_url) or Nostr (nsec, relays?) account directly, no link needed. X and LinkedIn return requires_owner_approval.create_post: accounts (1 to 100 account ids), text (up to 10,000 characters before per-platform limits), media (up to 20 items of {url, type?: image|video|document, alt?, title?, thumbnail?}; a document is a PDF, PowerPoint or Word file posted to LinkedIn as a document carousel, alone in its post; a video's title and thumbnail are used by LinkedIn, Facebook and as the Instagram Reel cover), first_comment (up to 1,250 characters, posted as a comment by the same LinkedIn profile or Page right after the post goes out, for example to hold a link; its id comes back as first_comment_id on the target. If the comment is refused, the post stays published and the target's error is first_comment_failed. Other networks skip it with a first_comment_not_supported warning; use thread on X, Bluesky, Mastodon and Telegram), poll ({question?, options, duration_minutes?, multiple?} on X, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram and Threads (2 to 4 options of 25 characters; Threads sets the open time), never with media: X takes 2 to 4 options of 25 characters for 5 minutes to 7 days; LinkedIn 2 to 4 options of 30 characters plus a question of up to 140 (defaults to the text), open 1, 3, 7 or 14 days (rounded); Mastodon 2 to 4 options of 50 characters for up to 30 days, multiple allowed; Telegram up to 10 options with a question, sent right after the text when both are given. Default open time is 1 day; other networks reject polls with poll_not_supported), platform_options (per-network settings: a text override, for example {"x": {"text": "..."}}, plus x.reply_settings (following, mentionedUsers, subscribers, verified), bluesky.langs (e.g. ["en"]), mastodon.visibility (public, unlisted, private, direct), mastodon.spoiler_text (content warning), mastodon.sensitive, mastodon.language, telegram.disable_notification (silent), telegram.protect_content (no forwarding or saving), instagram.format (post or story), Reel settings instagram.share_to_feed, instagram.cover_url, instagram.thumb_offset (ms) and instagram.audio_name, instagram.collaborators (up to 3 usernames), linkedin.visibility (PUBLIC, CONNECTIONS, LOGGED_IN), linkedin_page.visibility (PUBLIC, LOGGED_IN) and threads.reply_control (everyone, accounts_you_follow, mentioned_only, parent_post_author_only, followers_only). Unknown networks or settings are rejected, so typos don't pass silently), auto_thread (split over-long text into a thread where the network has them), repeat ({every, interval?, count} for a dated series), scheduled_at ("best" picks the hour that has worked best for these accounts; or ISO-8601 with offset, up to 365 days ahead), dry_run (default false), wait (default true on the MCP server, so the call returns per-account results), idempotency_key (up to 255 characters) and metadata (any JSON object you want back on the post).get_post (id): the post with one target per account: status, url, external_post_id, attempts, next_attempt_at, published_at, verified and error (code, message, fix, retryable).list_posts (status?, limit 1 to 100, default 20, before? cursor): recent posts, newest first, with has_more and next_cursor.wait_for_approval (id, wait_seconds 0 to 120, default 45): waits while a post created with approval: "required" is pending_approval, then returns it. approval.status is approved (publishing or scheduled) or rejected (canceled, with the reviewer's approval.note).update_post (id, plus any of text, media, link, thread, poll, first_comment, platform_options, scheduled_at, dry_run): edits a post that hasn't started publishing. Fields left out stay; scheduled_at: null publishes now. Checked like a new post; an approved post goes back for approval if its content changes. A published post returns post_not_editable.cancel_post (id): cancels a scheduled or pending-approval post that hasn't started publishing. A post that is already publishing returns post_not_cancelable.get_post_metrics (id): likes, reposts, replies, quotes, views and more for each published copy, plus totals, read from the network and cached for 15 minutes. X, Bluesky, Mastodon and LinkedIn Pages; X bills $0.005 per read.create_posts (posts: 1 to 50 items with the same fields as create_post, dry_run?): a week or month of content in one call. Each item is checked and created by itself; results come back per item.list_replies (id): what people replied under each published copy of a post, with ids to answer. Answer one with create_post using reply_to (the post) and reply_to_comment (the reply's id). Bluesky, Mastodon and X today (X bills $0.005 per reply returned).list_events (after?, types?, limit, wait_seconds): what happened since you last looked (posts published or failed, approvals, accounts needing reconnection), oldest first, with a last_id to pass as after next time. For agents that can't receive webhooks.disconnect_account (id): removes a connected account and deletes its stored credentials.get_workspace (no input) and set_owner_email (email): the workspace's plan and owner email, and setting that email once so the owner can sign in and pay for a plan.delete_post (id, account_ids?): deletes it everywhere it went out: published copies are deleted from X, Bluesky, Mastodon, LinkedIn, Telegram and Facebook (threads included) and copies not yet published are canceled. account_ids limits it to some accounts. Each target comes back deleted, or with the network's error (also listed in warnings); calling it again retries those. Instagram and Threads return delete_not_supported for now.upload_media (data_base64, content_type): stores an image or short video up to 4 MB and returns a public url for create_post media. For agents whose files don't have a public URL.create_media_upload (content_type, size_bytes?): a one-time signed upload_url (valid 2 hours, up to 200 MB) to PUT a larger file to, plus the url it will have.get_analytics (days?, from?, to?, account_id?, platform?, timezone?, limit?): totals and engagement per account, the top posts and the best posting hours over a period, from metrics already read. Free; it never calls a network.get_usage (no input): active accounts this month, posts, plan, estimated cost and X API fees (x_api_fees: used, included, billable), plus the scopes and limits of the key in use.create_upgrade_link (plan: hobby, pro, growth or scale): a payment link for the workspace owner. The agent can't pay; it hands over the url, and the plan changes when the owner pays by card.list_webhooks (no input), create_webhook (url, events?) and delete_webhook (id): manage webhook endpoints. create_webhook returns the signing secret once.list_keys (no input), create_key (name, scopes?, account_ids?, require_approval?, daily_post_limit?) and revoke_key (id): manage API keys, including limited keys for other agents. create_key returns the key once.PromptsThe server also offers four prompts, which clients such as Claude show as ready-made commands. Each frames a request and leaves the work to the tools: post_everywhere (one message to every connected account, adjusted per network, dry-run first), plan_week (draft a week of posts on a topic and schedule them once you approve), answer_replies (read the replies under a post and draft answers for you to approve) and whats_new (failed posts, approvals waiting and accounts that need reconnecting since last time).Not using MCP?The same tools come as packages for agent frameworks, defined once so they behave the same everywhere. Python: pip install socialsforai includes tools for LangChain and LangGraph (socialsforai.integrations.langchain), CrewAI (.crewai) and the OpenAI Agents SDK (.openai_agents). JavaScript: npm install @socialsforai/ai-sdk gives the Vercel AI SDK socialsTools(). Each returns errors to the model with their fix, and sends an idempotency key with every publish. See the docs.Set up in Claude Code, Cursor or Claude DesktopClaude Code adds remote servers with claude mcp add --transport http and takes request headers with --header, per its MCP docs. Export your key first so it never lands in shell history as plain text, then run the command below.The default scope is local (this project, only you). Add --scope user to load the server in every project. Avoid --scope project with a raw key: that scope writes .mcp.json in the project root, which is meant to be committed. Run claude mcp list to confirm the server shows as connected, or /mcp inside a session. Tools appear as mcp__socials__create_post and so on. Cursor and Claude Desktop follow in the next two sections; other clients are on the agent guides.bashexport SOCIALS_API_KEY=sk_... claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY"Cursor configurationCursor reads .cursor/mcp.json in a project or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for every project, and supports Streamable HTTP servers with url and headers. Cursor resolves ${env:NAME} inside headers, so the key can stay in your environment. Cursor asks for approval before running MCP tools by default; keep that on for create_post. More in the Cursor guide.json{ "mcpServers": { "socials": { "url": "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${env:SOCIALS_API_KEY}" } } } }Claude Desktop configurationClaude Desktop launches local servers from claude_desktop_config.json (on macOS in ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/, on Windows in %APPDATA%\Claude\). mcp-remote bridges that to our HTTP server and forwards your key with --header. Its README notes that some clients, Claude Desktop on Windows among them, don't escape spaces inside args, so the header is written without a space after the colon and the Bearer sk_... value sits in env. Restart Claude Desktop after saving. More in the Claude Desktop guide.json{ "mcpServers": { "socials": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp", "--header", "Authorization:${AUTH_HEADER}"], "env": { "AUTH_HEADER": "Bearer sk_..." } } } }Troubleshooting by error codeEvery error carries a stable code, a message and a fix written for the agent to act on. Tool errors come back as an MCP error result whose text is the same JSON body the REST API returns. This is the full list of codes that behave the same on every network; the LinkedIn, X and Bluesky pages add the causes specific to each.HTTP 401 when the client connects: the Authorization header is missing or the key is wrong. The server checks the bearer key before any tool runs. On the REST API the same problem returns missing_api_key or invalid_api_key. Check the header spelling (Authorization: Bearer sk_...) and that the environment variable is set in the process that launches the client.account_not_found (404): an id in accounts doesn't belong to this workspace, often because the agent invented one. The fix tells it to call list_accounts.preflight_failed (422): the post would fail at least one check, and nothing was published. The issues array lists every problem with code, field and fix. Repeat the call with dry_run: true until ok is true.text_too_long, too_many_media, too_many_videos, mixed_media, empty_post: per-network content checks inside preflight_failed. Each issue names the account and, for text, the platform_options field to set a shorter version in.account_needs_reauth: the account's token expired or was revoked. Call create_connect_link with that platform and send the URL to the account owner. The account keeps its id when reconnected.duplicate_content: the same text went to the same account in the last 24 hours. Vary the text, or set a per-platform version in platform_options.daily_cap_reached: the account hit our fair-use cap for the rolling 24 hours. Pass scheduled_at to post later.scheduled_in_past or scheduled_too_far: scheduled_at is more than 5 minutes ago or more than 365 days ahead. Omit it to publish now.idempotency_key_reused (409): the key was already used with a different body. Use a new key for a different post; reuse a key only to retry the identical request.post_not_cancelable (409): cancel_post was called on a post that already started publishing. Use delete_post instead to remove the published copies.platform_unavailable (400) from create_connect_link, or platform_not_configured in a dry run: that network isn't live on this server. list_platforms shows which are.connect_link_expired (410): the link is past its expires_in. Create a new one.invalid_media_url, media_fetch_failed or media_too_large: we couldn't download an image from a public http(s) URL, or it's over that network's size limit. Host the file publicly and pass its URL.platform_rate_limited or platform_unavailable on a target: the network said no for now. These are retryable; we try again after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours, six attempts in total, then mark the target failed. Poll with get_post instead of posting again.platform_rejected: the network refused the post after preflight passed. Its message is included; adjust the post and send it with a new idempotency key.plan_limit_active_accounts or plan_limit_posts: the Free plan's 3 active accounts or 100 posts a month is used up. Both are hard limits on Free only.QuestionsWhat people askIs there a free social media MCP server?+Yes. SocialsForAI's Free plan covers 3 active accounts and 100 posts a month, with the MCP server included. Paid plans add accounts and unlimited posts; every plan includes the MCP server, the REST API and webhooks.Which MCP clients does it work with?+Any client that supports remote MCP servers over Streamable HTTP with a custom Authorization header, such as Claude Code and Cursor. Clients that only run local servers can connect through mcp-remote, which forwards the header. Setup guides are on the agent pages.Does the agent see my social media passwords?+No. Account owners approve access on the network's own OAuth screen, or with a Bluesky app password, Mastodon access token or Telegram bot token, from a hosted connect link. Credentials are stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never returned by the API or the MCP server.Can an agent spam my accounts with this?+Each account has a fair-use cap per rolling 24 hours (100 on X, 300 on Bluesky and Mastodon, 50 on LinkedIn, 500 on Telegram), identical text on the same account within 24 hours is blocked, and every post can go through a dry run first. You can also revoke the API key at any time.Get an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/mcp/bluesky.body_text: Bluesky MCP Server: Post from Claude, Cursor, AgentsSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyBluesky MCP serverA Bluesky MCP server that's live today.Connect a Bluesky account with an app password, add one server to your agent, and post with links and hashtags that actually render as links.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026A Bluesky MCP server exposes Bluesky posting as tools an AI agent can call over the Model Context Protocol. SocialsForAI's is hosted at https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp and live today; clients connect over Streamable HTTP with a bearer API key. It connects accounts with a Bluesky app password (never the main password), counts the 300-grapheme limit, builds link, mention and hashtag facets automatically, uploads up to 4 images, and verifies each post by reading it back.Bluesky: live. Posting to Bluesky works on the API today.What a Bluesky MCP server doesBluesky's API is open, so posting from a script is easy. Posting correctly takes more: logging in with an app password, keeping the session alive, counting graphemes rather than characters, uploading images as blobs, and adding facets so links and mentions are clickable. Our server handles all of it and gives the agent thirty tools.When the agent calls create_post, we log in to the account's PDS (bsky.social by default, or a custom PDS URL the owner entered), run the text through the atproto SDK's facet detection, upload images, create the record, and then fetch it back with getPosts to set verified. More on the raw API is in our Bluesky API guide, and the protocol side is on the MCP server overview.The tools that matter for BlueskyInputs for all thirty tools are on the hub, under every tool and its inputs. This is what they return or do for a Bluesky account, one of the eight networks you can run end to end today.list_platforms: Bluesky's row has available: true, maxChars: 300 (graphemes), maxImages: 4, supportsVideo: true (1 video) and dailyPostCap: 300. Over REST, GET /v1/platforms also shows connect: "credentials", meaning a form rather than an OAuth redirect.create_connect_link with platforms: ["bluesky"]: returns a link to a hosted page with three fields: handle or email, app password, and an optional PDS URL. It works on the hosted server now.list_accounts with platform: "bluesky": handle is the account's handle from its session (for example you.bsky.social) and display_name comes from the Bluesky profile when it can be read.create_post: text is checked against 300 graphemes and 3,000 UTF-8 bytes. Write links, @handles and #tags as plain text; facets are added at publish time. Images are fetched from your URLs, refused above 2,000,000 bytes, uploaded as blobs, and embedded with your alt text.get_post: a Bluesky target's url is https://bsky.app/profile/<handle>/post/<rkey> and external_post_id is the record's at:// URI. verified: true means we read the record back with getPosts after creating it.A worked session: dry run, fix, publishYou ask the agent to announce a launch on Bluesky and LinkedIn. The shared draft is long enough for LinkedIn but 318 graphemes for Bluesky, so the dry run fails with text_too_long and points at platform_options.bluesky.text. The agent writes a short Bluesky version, keeps the long one for LinkedIn, and publishes after you approve.The result is partially_published: Bluesky succeeded and LinkedIn failed with account_needs_reauth. Each account gets its own target, so one bad account never hides another's result. The agent's next step is in the fix field. Ids here are illustrative; the shapes are the server's real responses, trimmed with ....text// 1. Dry run the draft create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP"], "text": "<318-grapheme thread opener>", "dry_run": true }) → { "object": "preflight", "ok": false, "issues": [{ "account_id": "acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP", "platform": "bluesky", "severity": "error", "code": "text_too_long", "field": "platform_options.bluesky.text", "message": "Text is 318 characters; Bluesky allows 300.", "fix": "Shorten it by 18+ characters, or set platform_options.bluesky.text to a shorter version." }], "preview": [{ "account_id": "acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP", "platform": "bluesky", "text": "<318-grapheme thread opener>" }] } // 2. Publish a shorter Bluesky version (after the human approves) create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP", "acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX"], "text": "<long version for LinkedIn>", "platform_options": { "bluesky": { "text": "Webhooks shipped. Docs: https://example.com/docs #devtools" } }, "idempotency_key": "webhooks-launch-1" }) → { "id": "post_Zt6Mw1Qe8Rn4Yb2C", "object": "post", "status": "partially_published", "targets": [ { "account_id": "acc_Bs2rTq8Lm5Wn1KdP", "platform": "bluesky", "status": "published", "url": "https://bsky.app/profile/you.bsky.social/post/<rkey>", "external_post_id": "at://did:plc:<did>/app.bsky.feed.post/<rkey>", "attempts": 1, "verified": true, "error": null, ... }, { "account_id": "acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "platform": "linkedin", "status": "failed", "attempts": 1, "error": { "code": "account_needs_reauth", "message": "LinkedIn access token expired (they last 60 days).", "fix": "Reconnect the LinkedIn account with a new connect link.", "retryable": false }, ... } ], ... }Bluesky rules the server handlesFrom Bluesky's lexicons and docs, and our Bluesky provider:Length: the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon sets maxGraphemes: 300 (and 3,000 bytes). A grapheme is what a reader sees as one character, so an emoji with skin tone counts once. We count graphemes the same way.Facets: Bluesky doesn't use markup. Links, mentions and hashtags are facets that point at UTF-8 byte ranges in the text, per Bluesky's rich text guide; without them a URL shows as plain text. We run the SDK's detectFacets on every post, so the agent writes plain text and links work.Images: the lexicon allows up to 4 images per post, each up to 2,000,000 bytes (formerly 1 MB). We fetch the URL you pass and reject larger files with media_too_large. Pass alt text; it goes into the image embed.Video: 1 MP4 per post, up to 100 MB through our API, uploaded through Bluesky's video service and not mixed with images. Bluesky-hosted accounts need a verified email to upload video, and Bluesky sets daily video upload limits.App passwords: atproto's own docs say password logins should use app passwords only, since they're designed for programmatic access. The connect page asks for an app password and never the main one. Revoke it in Bluesky's settings and our access ends.Self-hosted PDS: enter the PDS URL on the connect page. Leave it blank for bsky.social.Volume: our fair-use cap is 300 posts per Bluesky account per rolling 24 hours.Before an agent posts to Bluesky for youBluesky charges no API fee and our 300-a-day cap is higher than on X or LinkedIn, so the guardrails here are mostly yours to set. These are the ones that matter on Bluesky.One app password per connection. Create a dedicated app password for this account, so revoking it in Bluesky's settings cuts off our access without touching your other apps. The next publish then fails with account_needs_reauth. Disconnecting the account through our API deletes the stored credentials on our side too.Read the mentions in the preview. Because facets are added automatically, an @handle in the agent's draft becomes a real mention linked to that account, and a URL becomes a live link. Check both in the dry-run text before you approve.Three hundred a day is generous. At our cap of 300 posts per account per rolling 24 hours, the duplicate check (duplicate_content for identical text within 24 hours) and your approval prompt do more of the work than the cap does.Approve the publish, not only the draft. Have the agent run create_post with dry_run: true first, then leave your client's tool approval on so the real call needs a click.Key every publish. Send an idempotency_key; a retried call with the same key and body returns the existing post, so a timeout never leaves two copies in your feed.Practice failures in the sandbox. The sandbox platform's fake account fails on purpose when the text contains [fail:retryable], [fail:permanent] or [fail:auth], so you can see how the agent reacts before it touches your real account.Set up for Bluesky: add the server, then an app passwordThe server is the same for every network. Register it in your client; the Claude Code command is below, and the Cursor and Claude Desktop entries are in client setup.Bluesky connects with a form instead of OAuth. Ask the agent to call create_connect_link with platforms: ["bluesky"] and open the URL yourself. Enter your handle (a leading @ is stripped) or account email, and an app password from Settings, Privacy and security, App passwords, at bsky.app. Leave the PDS URL blank unless your account lives on your own server. We log in, keep the session, and on later posts resume it; if the session can't be resumed we log in again with the app password. The app password is stored encrypted with AES-256-GCM and never returned by any tool.bashexport SOCIALS_API_KEY=sk_... claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY"Bluesky errors and their fixesThese are the Bluesky-specific codes. The ones every network shares, such as the 401 at connect time, preflight_failed and idempotency_key_reused, are covered once in troubleshooting by error code.account_needs_reauth on Bluesky: the app password was revoked or the login failed. The fix says to create a new app password at bsky.app/settings/app-passwords and reconnect with a connect link.invalid_credentials on the connect page: the handle or app password is empty. Use the full handle (yourname.bsky.social) and paste the app password with its dashes.media_too_large: an image is over 2 MB. Compress or resize it and pass a new URL.text_too_long under 300 graphemes: the text is over 3,000 UTF-8 bytes, which happens with many emoji or non-Latin scripts. Shorten it or set platform_options.bluesky.text.platform_rejected: Bluesky answered 400 and its message is in the error. It isn't retried, so fix the post and send it with a new key.platform_rate_limited or platform_unavailable: Bluesky answered 429 or failed for another reason. Both are retried automatically; poll get_post.Status: liveBluesky posting is live on the hosted server today: text, links, mentions, hashtags, up to 4 images with alt text or 1 MP4 video up to 100 MB, scheduling, and read-back verification. X, LinkedIn (profiles and Company Pages), Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live too; see the X MCP server and LinkedIn MCP server pages for how they behave.Connect Bluesky to your agent in five steps01Make a keySign up or send POST /v1/workspaces. Free covers 3 accounts that post in a month and 100 posts, which is plenty to try Bluesky end to end.02Create a Bluesky app passwordIn Bluesky, open Settings, Privacy and security, App passwords, and create one for this connection. Keep the dashes when you copy it.03Add the server and ask for a linkRegister the hosted URL in your client, then ask the agent for a Bluesky connect link.04Enter handle and app passwordOn the connect page, type your handle or email, paste the app password, and fill in a PDS URL only if you host your own. The agent never sees these fields.05Dry run and publishHave the agent dry run under 300 graphemes, approve the post, and open the bsky.app URL from the result to see the links rendered.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Claude Code: connect to MCP servers (code.claude.com) · Cursor: Model Context Protocol (cursor.com) · mcp-remote README (GitHub) · Bluesky lexicons: app.bsky.feed.post, app.bsky.embed.images (atproto) · Bluesky docs: links, mentions and rich text · atproto password sessions: use app passwords (GitHub)QuestionsWhat developers askWhy use a hosted Bluesky MCP server instead of the SDK?+The SDK is fine for one script. A hosted server adds connect links, encrypted credentials, preflight checks, retries, receipts and the same tools for X, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr.Do I give the agent my Bluesky password?+No. The account owner enters an app password on our connect page, not in the chat. The agent only sees an account id.Will links in my agent's Bluesky posts be clickable?+Yes. We detect links, mentions and hashtags and add facets automatically. Without facets Bluesky shows a URL as plain text.Does the Bluesky MCP server work with self-hosted PDS accounts?+Yes. Enter the PDS URL on the connect page.Can I try it without a real Bluesky account?+Yes. Connect the sandbox platform. Putting [fail:retryable], [fail:permanent] or [fail:auth] in the text simulates failures.Can I log in with my email instead of my handle?+Yes. The connect page accepts a handle or the account's email in the first field, with the app password in the second.How much does it cost?+Bluesky has no API fee. Our Free plan is enough to start; see pricing for paid plans, which are priced per account that posted in the month.Keep readingAll MCP setup guidesBluesky API guideClaude Desktop setupSocial media APIGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/mcp/linkedin.body_text: LinkedIn MCP Server: Post from Claude, Cursor, AgentsSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyLinkedIn MCP serverA LinkedIn MCP server your agent can't embarrass you with.Hosted, so there's nothing to run. The agent drafts, dry runs against LinkedIn's rules, waits for your yes, and publishes to your profile.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026A LinkedIn MCP server exposes LinkedIn posting as tools an AI agent can call over the Model Context Protocol. SocialsForAI hosts one at https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp (Streamable HTTP, bearer API key). It posts to personal LinkedIn profiles through LinkedIn's Posts API, checks the 3,000-character limit before anything is sent, escapes LinkedIn's reserved characters, and returns the post URL for each account. Company Pages aren't supported.LinkedIn: live. Posting to LinkedIn works on the API today.What a LinkedIn MCP server doesTo let Claude or Cursor post to LinkedIn, something has to hold an OAuth token with the w_member_social permission, format text the way LinkedIn's API expects, upload images, and report back. Our server does that work and exposes it as thirty tools. The agent never sees the token; it sees account ids like acc_Li4n....Under the hood, create_post sends POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts with the Linkedin-Version and X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0 headers LinkedIn requires, uploads images through LinkedIn's Images API first, and reads the new post's id from the x-restli-id response header. You don't need your own LinkedIn developer app. For the raw API details see our LinkedIn API guide; for the protocol side see the MCP server overview.The tools that matter for LinkedInAll thirty tools work the same on every network, and their full inputs are listed once in every tool and its inputs. Here is what five of them say or do when the account is a LinkedIn profile.list_platforms: the LinkedIn row carries maxChars: 3000, maxImages: 20, supportsVideo: true, video: {maxCount: 1, mixWithImages: false} and dailyPostCap: 50. Its available flag is false on the hosted server until our production LinkedIn app is configured, so an agent that reads it first won't offer LinkedIn before it works.list_accounts with platform: "linkedin": LinkedIn's userinfo endpoint gives us your member id, name and picture but no public handle, so handle comes back empty and display_name is the name on your profile. Tell the agent to pick the account by display_name or by id.create_post: write plain text up to 3,000 characters, counted per grapheme. The dry-run preview shows your text unescaped; the backslashes LinkedIn's format needs are added only in the request to LinkedIn. One image becomes a single-image post and two to twenty become a MultiImage post, each with the alt you passed as its alt text.get_post: a LinkedIn target's url is https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:share:<id> and external_post_id is the URN itself. verified stays false, because reading the post back needs r_member_social; the 201 from LinkedIn is the confirmation.cancel_post: scheduled LinkedIn posts are held on our side, so you can cancel any time before publishing starts. After that, delete_post removes it from LinkedIn.A worked session: dry run, fix, publishHere is what the agent sees when you ask it to repost a job ad that went out yesterday. The dry run catches the repeat before LinkedIn does. The agent rewrites, dry runs again, shows you the new text, and publishes once you approve. The publish call returns the post with one target per account. verified stays false on LinkedIn: reading a post back needs r_member_social, which LinkedIn has closed, so LinkedIn's 201 with a post id in x-restli-id is the confirmation. Ids and timestamps here are illustrative, and the shapes are the server's real responses, trimmed with ....Notice the parentheses and brackets in the text. LinkedIn's "little" text format treats them as markup, so we send them escaped and the post reads as written.text// 1. Dry run the draft (the same text went out yesterday) create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX"], "text": "We're hiring a staff engineer (remote, US). Details: ...", "dry_run": true }) → { "object": "preflight", "ok": false, "issues": [{ "account_id": "acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "platform": "linkedin", "severity": "error", "code": "duplicate_content", "message": "The same text was already posted to acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX in the last 24 hours; platforms reject or penalize duplicates.", "fix": "Vary the text for this account (platform_options) or wait 24 hours." }], "preview": [{ "account_id": "acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "platform": "linkedin", "text": "We're hiring a staff engineer (remote, US). Details: ..." }] } // 2. Rewrite, dry run again → { "object": "preflight", "ok": true, "issues": [], ... } // 3. Publish (after the human approves) create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX"], "text": "Still hiring: staff engineer [remote, US]. What the first 90 days look like: ...", "idempotency_key": "staff-eng-li-2" }) → { "id": "post_Hq7Tn2Wd5Ks9Lp3R", "object": "post", "status": "published", "targets": [{ "account_id": "acc_Li4nKd8Qp2Zr7TmX", "platform": "linkedin", "status": "published", "url": "https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:share:<id>", "external_post_id": "urn:li:share:<id>", "attempts": 1, "verified": false, "error": null, ... }], ... }LinkedIn rules the server handlesThese come from LinkedIn's own documentation and from how our LinkedIn provider is written. The agent doesn't have to know them; the dry run tells it when it breaks one.Length: LinkedIn Help says posts can be up to 3,000 characters. Preflight counts the final text for each account and returns text_too_long with the overage.Reserved characters: LinkedIn's Posts API stores commentary in the little text format, where | { } @ [ ] ( ) < > # \ * _ ~ are reserved and must be escaped with a backslash to show as plain text. We escape all of them except #, so hashtags still work. Without escaping, a post with "(remote)" or "@team" can be cut off or misparsed.Images: up to 20 per post, 20 MB each, uploaded through LinkedIn's Images API. More than one image becomes a MultiImage post, which LinkedIn supports for organic posts. Organic carousels aren't supported by LinkedIn.Video: 1 MP4 per post, up to 200 MB through our API (LinkedIn allows 3 seconds to 30 minutes), on personal profiles. A video can't share a post with images; preflight returns mixed_media, and a second video returns too_many_videos.Posting volume: LinkedIn says it may limit how many posts a member can make in a period without publishing a number. Our fair-use cap is 50 posts per LinkedIn account per rolling 24 hours.Tokens: LinkedIn member tokens last 60 days, and refresh tokens need partner access we don't have. When a token expires the account moves to needs_reauth and the agent gets account_needs_reauth with a fix.Before an agent posts to LinkedIn for youA LinkedIn post goes out under your own name, with PUBLIC visibility and main-feed distribution, to the people you work with and the ones who might hire you. That audience is less forgiving of a stray draft than most, so set the agent up to ask first.Make the preview the default. Tell the agent that every LinkedIn post starts as create_post with dry_run: true, and that it shows you the preview text before the real call. The dry run is plain code with no AI calls and no cost, and it doesn't use up the idempotency key.Keep the publish behind a click. Leave your client's approval prompt on for create_post. A published LinkedIn post can't be pulled back through our API; only scheduled ones can be canceled.Fifty a day is a ceiling, not a target. Our cap is 50 posts per profile per rolling 24 hours (daily_cap_reached), and LinkedIn may limit members sooner without saying where. A person posting a few times a week is far below either.Personal profile only. If you ask the agent to post as your company, the right answer is that it can't: Company Pages need w_organization_social, which we don't have. It should not fall back to your own profile.Plan for the 60-day token. When it runs out, publishing stops with account_needs_reauth and the account.needs_reauth webhook fires. Subscribe to it if you want a message the day it happens rather than when the agent next tries.Retry with the same key. If the agent times out mid-publish and calls again with the same idempotency_key and body, it gets the first post back instead of a second copy.Set up for LinkedIn: add the server, then approve on LinkedInAdd the server once. In Claude Code the command below registers it for this project; the configs for Cursor and Claude Desktop, and notes on scope, are in client setup.Then connect the profile. Ask the agent to call create_connect_link with platforms: ["linkedin"]. The link sends you to LinkedIn's authorization page at linkedin.com/oauth/v2/authorization, asking for openid profile w_member_social. After you allow it, we exchange the code for a token, read your member id from LinkedIn's userinfo endpoint, and store the token encrypted with AES-256-GCM. If the link was created with a redirect_url, you land there with ?account_id=...&platform=linkedin&status=connected.bashexport SOCIALS_API_KEY=sk_... claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY"LinkedIn errors and their fixesThese are the codes you'll see on LinkedIn targets specifically. Codes that work the same on every network, such as a 401 at connect time, account_not_found or idempotency_key_reused, are in the full troubleshooting list.account_needs_reauth on LinkedIn usually means the 60-day token ran out. Ask the agent for create_connect_link with platforms: ["linkedin"] and approve again on LinkedIn's OAuth screen. The account keeps its id.platform_rejected with a LinkedIn message such as FIELD_LENGTH_TOO_LONG: LinkedIn refused the request after preflight passed. The fix field says to adjust the post and retry with a new idempotency key.platform_rate_limited: LinkedIn answered 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS. It's retryable, so we try again on our schedule; check back with get_post rather than sending the post again.too_many_media or media_too_large: more than 20 images, or one over 20 MB. Drop images or compress them and pass new URLs.duplicate_content: the same text reached this profile in the last 24 hours, or LinkedIn's own response called it a duplicate. Rewrite it; for a repost, change the opening line.platform_unavailable from create_connect_link, or platform_not_configured in a dry run: LinkedIn isn't enabled on the server you're calling. On the hosted server it's live; list_platforms shows the current status.Status: what works todayLinkedIn posting to personal profiles is live on the hosted server: OAuth with openid profile w_member_social, text, images, escaping, and a receipt that reports verified: false because w_member_social can't read posts back and LinkedIn keeps r_member_social closed. Company Pages need w_organization_social and LinkedIn's approval, which we don't have, so they aren't supported. X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live too; see the X MCP server and Bluesky MCP server.Connect LinkedIn to your agent in five steps01Create a workspace keySign up or call POST /v1/workspaces. The key starts with sk_ and the workspace starts on Free, which has room for a LinkedIn profile and two more accounts.02Register the serverAdd the hosted URL to your MCP client with the key as a bearer header. The Claude Code command is below; Cursor and Claude Desktop configs are on the MCP hub.03Approve LinkedIn's consent screenAsk for a LinkedIn connect link. https://socialsforai.com/mcp/x.body_text: X (Twitter) MCP Server for Claude, Cursor and AgentsSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyX (Twitter) MCP serverAn X MCP server that counts like X and warns before the expensive post.Your agent drafts and posts to X through one hosted server. It counts characters the way X does, flags the $0.20 link post, and caps volume per account.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026An X MCP server exposes posting to X (formerly Twitter) as tools an AI agent can call over the Model Context Protocol. Ours lives at https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp, speaks Streamable HTTP and takes a bearer API key. It posts through X's API v2 with OAuth 2.0, counts text with X's weighted rules (280, links 23, emoji 2), warns when a post contains a link because X charges $0.200 for it versus $0.015, and returns each post's URL.X: live. Posting to X works on the API today.What an X MCP server doesPosting to X from an agent takes an X developer app, an OAuth 2.0 flow with PKCE, token refresh, a character counter that matches X's, image uploads, and per-post API fees. Our server holds the app and the tokens and gives the agent thirty tools. The agent asks for an account id, drafts, dry runs, and calls create_post.create_post sends POST https://api.x.com/2/tweets; images go first to X's media upload endpoint. Access tokens refresh automatically through the offline.access scope, so an X account rarely needs reconnecting. X's per-post fees are covered on our X API pricing page; the shared protocol setup is on the MCP server overview.The tools that matter for XThe thirty tools and their inputs are documented once, in every tool and its inputs. For an X account, these five carry the details worth knowing.list_platforms: X's entry is maxChars: 280, maxImages: 4, supportsVideo: true with 1 video per post, dailyPostCap: 100. The 280 is a weighted count, not a string length. available is true: our production X app is configured, so X connect links work today.list_accounts with platform: "x": handle is the X username we read from GET /2/users/me when the account connected, and display_name is the profile name. The handle is what goes into the post URL.create_post: put the X wording in platform_options.x.text and the longer version in text; the weighted 280 applies to whichever text X receives. Up to 4 images, each downloaded from its URL, refused over 5 MB, and uploaded to POST /2/media/upload before the post is created.get_post: an X target's url is https://x.com/<handle>/status/<id> and external_post_id is the id X returned. Right after publishing we fetch the post with GET /2/tweets/<id>; a successful read sets verified: true, and a 403 on that read leaves it false without failing the post. X's pricing lists post reads at $0.005 per resource, so that check is one read in X's terms.get_usage: active accounts, posts, plan, an estimated plan cost, and X API fees so far this month (x_api_fees: used, included, billable). Before posting, a dry run warns with x_link_cost when the X text has a link.A worked session: dry run, fix, publishYou ask the agent to announce a launch on X with a link. The dry run returns one error and one warning. The error is length: X's weighted count is 301, over 280. The warning is cost: a post with a URL is billed at $0.200 instead of $0.015. The agent drops the link from the X version (a reply with the link would be billed at $0.200 too), shows you the new text, and publishes with an idempotency key once you approve.Warnings don't block a publish. If you want the link anyway, say so and the agent can send it as is. Ids here are illustrative; the shapes are the server's real responses, trimmed with .... To try the flow without posting, run the same session against the sandbox platform.text// 1. Find the account list_accounts({ "platform": "x" }) → [{ "id": "acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB", "object": "account", "platform": "x", "handle": "yourhandle", "status": "active", ... }] // 2. Dry run the draft create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB"], "text": "<301-character draft with a link>", "dry_run": true }) → { "object": "preflight", "ok": false, "issues": [ { "account_id": "acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB", "platform": "x", "severity": "error", "code": "text_too_long", "field": "platform_options.x.text", "message": "Text is 301 characters; X allows 280.", "fix": "Shorten it by 21+ characters, or set platform_options.x.text to a shorter version." }, { "account_id": "acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB", "platform": "x", "severity": "warning", "code": "x_link_cost", "message": "Posts with a URL cost $0.200 through the X API instead of $0.015 (docs.x.com pricing).", "fix": "Remove the link, or send a link-free version for X in platform_options.x.text. A link in a reply is also billed at the with-URL rate." } ], "preview": [{ "account_id": "acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB", "platform": "x", "text": "<301-character draft with a link>" }] } // 3. Publish the fixed version (after the human approves) create_post({ "accounts": ["acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB"], "text": "Webhooks are live: signed events for every post and account change.", "idempotency_key": "webhooks-launch-x" }) → { "id": "post_Vb3kR8sLq2Xn0TfY", "object": "post", "status": "published", "targets": [{ "account_id": "acc_x7Qm2pLr9sTn4VwB", "platform": "x", "status": "published", "url": "https://x.com/yourhandle/status/<id>", "external_post_id": "<id>", "attempts": 1, "verified": true, "error": null, ... }], ... }X rules the server handlesFrom X's developer docs and our X provider:Length: X allows 280 characters by weight. Per X's counting guide, every URL counts as 23 characters regardless of length, each emoji counts 2 (including joined sequences), CJK characters count 2, and text is NFC-normalized first. Our counter follows the same rules, so text_too_long matches what X would say.Link cost: X's pricing page lists Post create at $0.015 per request and Post create with a URL at $0.200, and notes prices are subject to change. A link in an X post triggers the x_link_cost warning before you spend it.Fees: we pass X API fees through at cost, with an included monthly credit ($0.50 Free per verified owner, $2 Hobby, $5 Pro, $15 Growth, $40 Scale). On Free, X posts past the credit fail preflight with x_credit_exhausted; on paid plans the fees are billed at cost at the end of the period.Images: up to 4 per post, 5 MB each. Video: 1 MP4 or MOV per post, up to 200 MB through our API, not mixed with images (mixed_media).Volume: our fair-use cap is 100 posts per X account per rolling 24 hours, plus the 24-hour duplicate check. Bursts and repeats are what get automated accounts limited.Per-network text: X is usually the shortest limit in a multi-network post, so set platform_options.x.text and keep the long version for LinkedIn.Before an agent posts to X for youOn X every post is a metered API request, so the human check is partly about wording and partly about money. The numbers below come from X's pricing page and our caps.Know what a runaway loop costs. At our cap of 100 posts per account per day, link-free posts come to $1.50 in X fees and posts that all carry a link come to $20.00. The cap (daily_cap_reached) is what stops the loop; your approval prompt is what stops the first one.Treat x_link_cost as a question. The warning doesn't block anything, so instruct the agent to stop and ask you whenever a dry run returns it, rather than publishing on its own judgment.Don't move the link into a reply to save money. A reply with a URL is billed at the same $0.200 rate.Review before every publish. Keep your client's tool approval on for create_post, and have the agent show you the dry-run preview of the X text specifically, since it's often a shorter rewrite of the shared draft.Retries are safe with a key. A timed-out create_post resent with the same idempotency_key and body returns the original post, so X isn't billed twice for one announcement.Repeats are blocked. Identical text to the same X account within 24 hours fails preflight with duplicate_content.Set up for X: add the server, then authorize on XRegister the server in your client first. The Claude Code version is below; Cursor and Claude Desktop take a JSON entry each, shown in client setup.Connecting an X account is an OAuth 2.0 authorization with PKCE (S256). The agent calls create_connect_link with platforms: ["x"]; you open the link and are sent to x.com/i/oauth2/authorize, which asks for tweet.read tweet.write users.read media.write offline.access. We exchange the code, read your handle, and keep the tokens encrypted. Before each publish we refresh the access token if it expires within a minute, and if X still answers 401 we refresh once and retry the post. If the refresh is refused, or X rejects the new token too, the account moves to needs_reauth.bashexport SOCIALS_API_KEY=sk_... claude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY"X errors and their fixesThe codes below are the ones with an X-specific cause. For the codes every network shares, including a 401 when the client connects, account_not_found and idempotency_key_reused, see troubleshooting by error code.x_link_cost (warning): the text contains a link. Remove it, give X a link-free version in platform_options.x.text, or publish anyway knowing X bills $0.200 for that request. Moving the link to a reply doesn't help: a reply with a URL is billed at $0.200 too.text_too_long on X while the text looks short: links count 23 and emoji count 2. Ask the agent to set platform_options.x.text instead of shortening the shared text.account_needs_reauth on X: the refresh token was revoked, for example because the owner removed the app in X's settings. Create a new connect link for x.too_many_media or media_too_large: a fifth image, or one over 5 MB. X's limits are tighter than LinkedIn's, so a shared media list may need trimming for the X account.platform_rate_limited: X answered 429. We retry on our backoff schedule; poll get_post instead of calling create_post again.duplicate_content after preflight passed: X's own response called the post a duplicate. Change the wording for that account.platform_unavailable when creating an X connect link, or platform_not_configured in a dry run: X isn't enabled on the server you're calling. On the hosted server it's live; list_platforms shows the current status.Status: what works todayX posting is live on the hosted server: OAuth 2.0 with PKCE and the scopes tweet.read tweet.write users.read media.write offline.access, text, images, video (1 per post, up to 200 MB), refresh, read-back verification. Bluesky, LinkedIn (profiles and Company Pages), Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live too; see the Bluesky MCP server and LinkedIn MCP server.Connect X to your agent in five steps01Get a keyCreate a workspace at /signup or with POST /v1/workspaces. You get an sk_ key on the Free plan.02Point your client at the serverRegister the hosted URL with an Authorization: Bearer header. The Claude Code command is on this page; the other clients are on the MCP hub.03Check that X is availableAsk the agent to call list_platforms. The X row should say available: true. If it says false, the server you're calling doesn't have X enabled and the next step will be refused.04Authorize on XAsk for a connect link for x. Open it, sign in to the X account that should post, and authorize the app on X's OAuth screen.05Dry run, read the cost warning, publishDry run the draft. Fix any length error, decide whether the link is worth $0.200, then approve the publish and keep the x.com status URL it returns.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Claude Code: connect to MCP servers (code.claude.com) · Cursor: Model Context Protocol (cursor.com) · mcp-remote README (GitHub) · X API pricing (docs.x.com) · Counting characters (docs.x.com)QuestionsWhat developers askDo I have to run an X MCP server myself?+No. Ours is hosted. You add one URL and an API key to your client; we hold the X app, refresh tokens and count characters the way X does.Does using the X MCP server cost X API fees?+Yes. X charges per post: $0.015, or $0.200 with a link, per its pricing page. We pass that through at cost, with a small included credit on paid plans.Do I need an X developer account?+No. The account owner approves our app on X's OAuth screen from a connect link.Can an agent spam X with this?+We cap each X account at 100 posts per rolling 24 hours and block identical text to the same account within 24 hours.Why does X say my 250-character post is too long?+X counts by weight: every URL is 23, every emoji 2, CJK characters 2. A dry run shows the weighted count before you post.Can the agent schedule tweets?+Yes. Pass scheduled_at up to 365 days ahead. The post stays scheduled until then and can be canceled with cancel_post.Will I have to reconnect my X account often?+Rarely. The offline.access scope gives us a refresh token, and we refresh before publishing when the access token is close to expiring. You reconnect only if the refresh token is revoked.Keep readingAll MCP setup guidesX API pricingCursor setupLinkedIn MCP serverGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/privacy.body_text: Privacy policy | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyPrivacy policyDraft, last updated 2026-11-01SocialsForAI is a product of Codehorts LLC (“we”, “us”), 1421 B St, Eureka, CA 95501, USA. Codehorts LLC operates socialsforai.com and the SocialsForAI API and MCP server, and is responsible for this privacy policy. Questions and requests: lee@socialsforai.com.SocialsForAI publishes posts to social networks on behalf of our customers and the people who connect their accounts to them. This policy explains what we collect, why, who we share it with, how long we keep it, and the choices you have.What we collectWebsite visitors: our public pages use Google Analytics to measure visits. It sets cookies and tells Google which pages you view, how you arrived, and details like your browser, device and approximate location. It doesn't run on the dashboard pages you sign in to.Workspace owners: your email address, used to send sign-in links and service messages, and whether you've verified it. Signing in sets one first-party cookie, sfa_session, a random token that lasts 30 days or until you sign out. We store only a hash of it.API keys: a short prefix and a one-way hash of each key, its name and when it was last used. We can't recover a key's full value.Connected social accounts: the network's account or page id, handle, display name and profile image URL, and the access credentials the network issues (OAuth tokens, or the app password, access token or bot token you provide). Credentials are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.Posts: the text, media links, per-network options, schedule and any metadata our customer sends, and the result on each network (post id, link, status, errors, attempts, and the network's API fee where it applies).Uploaded media: images and videos uploaded to us are stored in a private storage bucket and served only through unguessable links.Webhooks: the endpoint URLs customers register and a record of each delivery attempt.Billing: for paid plans, your Stripe customer id and subscription status. Card details are entered on Stripe's pages and stay with Stripe; we never see or store them.Connected AI apps: when an MCP client signs in, we store its name and callback address.Security records: to limit abuse we store a salted hash of the network address that requests a signup or a sign-in email (never the address itself) and delete it after a day. Our hosting provider records standard request logs, which include IP addresses.What we receive from social networksWhen someone connects an account, the network gives us what's needed to identify it and post on its behalf: for example, from LinkedIn a member's id, name and photo, or for a Company Page, the page's id and name and the member's role on it. We use network APIs only to publish the posts our customers send, to upload their media, and to confirm a post went live. We don't read feeds, messages, comments, followers or connections, and we don't combine network data across customers.How we use informationTo provide the service: publishing and scheduling posts, retrying failed deliveries, sending webhooks, and showing results in the dashboard and API.To bill for paid plans, including active-account overage and network API fees passed through at cost.To secure the service and prevent abuse, including rate limits and fair-use caps.To send sign-in links and messages about your account or the service.We don't sell personal information, show ads, or use customer content or network data to train AI models.Who we share it withWe use these providers to run the service. They process data on our behalf, under their own security and privacy commitments:Vercel: hosting, request logs (United States).Supabase: database (United States, AWS us-east-1).Amazon Web Services: storage for uploaded media (United States, us-east-1).Stripe: payments and invoices.Resend: sign-in and service email.Google (Tag Manager and Analytics): measuring visits to our public website.The social networks you publish to receive the posts and media you send them, under their own policies. We may also disclose information if required by law, to protect our rights or users, or as part of a sale or reorganization of our business.How long we keep itDisconnecting an account deletes its stored credentials immediately.Deleting a workspace deletes its connected accounts and their credentials, posts, API keys, webhooks and delivery records immediately. A workspace with an active plan needs that plan cancelled first, in Billing → Manage billing.Uploaded media files are deleted automatically 400 days after upload.Sign-in links expire after 15 minutes; sign-in and signup security records are deleted after a day.Our database provider keeps backups for a limited period, after which deleted data is gone from them too.Billing records are kept by Stripe and by us as long as tax and accounting rules require.Your choicesDisconnect any account from the dashboard or the API, or revoke our access in the network's own settings.Revoke API keys and connected AI apps on the dashboard's API keys page.Delete a workspace on its Settings page.Email lee@socialsforai.com to access, correct or delete your personal information, including your sign-in email, or with any privacy question. We'll respond within 30 days. If you connected your account through one of our customers' apps, you can also contact them.SecurityTraffic is encrypted in transit. Network credentials are encrypted at rest; API keys and session tokens are stored only as hashes; uploaded media sits in a private bucket; and each internal service key has only the permissions it needs. No system is perfectly secure, and we'll notify affected customers of a breach as the law requires.ChildrenSocialsForAI is a service for businesses and developers and isn't directed to children under 16.ChangesWe'll update this page when our practices change and show the date above. For material changes we'll notify workspace owners by email.
