https://socialsforai.com/schedule-linked.body_text: Schedule LinkedIn Posts with an API or AI Agent | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keySchedule LinkedIn posts with an APISchedule LinkedIn posts from code, a cron job or an agent.LinkedIn's own scheduler is built for one person in a browser. This guide is for software that decides what goes out and when, including what LinkedIn's API can and can't do on its own.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To schedule a LinkedIn post through SocialsForAI, send POST /v1/posts with scheduled_at set to an ISO-8601 time up to 365 days ahead. The post is held, then published to every listed account when it's due. Cancel it any time before publishing starts with DELETE /v1/posts/:id; a webhook reports the result.LinkedIn: live. Posting to LinkedIn works on the API today.Can you schedule LinkedIn posts through the LinkedIn API?Not directly. LinkedIn's Posts API documentation says PUBLISHED is the only lifecycleState accepted when creating a post, so there is no field for a future publish time. Scheduling has to happen on your side: store the post, then call the API at the right moment.That is the part we run for you. You send the post once with scheduled_at; we store it, and our delivery worker, which runs every minute, publishes it through POST https://api.linkedin.com/rest/posts when it's due. Reserved characters in LinkedIn's "little" text format, such as ( ) [ ] @ *, are escaped for you, and hashtags are left intact. The LinkedIn API page covers the underlying API in more detail.A worked example: schedule a hiring postThis schedules a post for 14:00 UTC on November 10. The timestamp must carry a time zone, either Z or an offset like -05:00; a bare local time is rejected as a validation error.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: hiring-staff-eng-2026-11" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_linkedin_maria"], "text": "Hiring: staff engineer, platform team. Remote in US time zones. Details and the full job description are on our careers page.", "scheduled_at": "2026-11-10T14:00:00Z", "metadata": { "campaign": "hiring-q4" } }'What does a scheduled post look like?The response is a 201 with status: "scheduled" (the text is shortened here). The target is pending with zero attempts, and next_attempt_at is the scheduled time. Your metadata comes back on the post and on every webhook, which is the easiest way to match results to rows in your own database.json{ "id": "post_7HcN2qLx9VbE0sTa", "object": "post", "status": "scheduled", "text": "Hiring: staff engineer, platform team. Remote in US time zones. ...", "media": [], "platform_options": {}, "scheduled_at": "2026-11-10T14:00:00.000Z", "created_at": "2026-11-01T18:20:03.511Z", "completed_at": null, "metadata": { "campaign": "hiring-q4" }, "targets": [ { "id": "tgt_Lr5mW0aYp3Qe8KdZ", "account_id": "acc_linkedin_maria", "platform": "linkedin", "status": "pending", "url": null, "external_post_id": null, "attempts": 0, "next_attempt_at": "2026-11-10T14:00:00.000Z", "published_at": null, "verified": false, "error": null } ] }What happens when the scheduled time arrives?Within about a minute of scheduled_at, the post moves to publishing, then published. The target gets LinkedIn's post URN (from the x-restli-id header LinkedIn returns with its 201) and a https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/... URL, and a post.published webhook fires with the full post.Before publishing, we check the account is still connected. Everything else, such as length and duplicates, was checked when you created the post. If LinkedIn returns 429 or a 5xx, the attempt is retried after 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m and 2h, six attempts in all, before the target is marked failed and post.failed fires.In TypeScript, the webhook handler verifies the Socials-Signature header (HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp and raw body) before trusting the event:typescriptimport { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto"; export async function POST(req: Request) { const raw = await req.text(); const sig = req.headers.get("Socials-Signature") ?? ""; // t=<unix>,v1=<hex> const { t, v1 } = Object.fromEntries(sig.split(",").map((p) => p.split("="))); const expected = createHmac("sha256", process.env.SOCIALS_WEBHOOK_SECRET!).update(`${t}.${raw}`).digest("hex"); const ok = !!v1 && v1.length === expected.length && timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(v1), Buffer.from(expected)); if (!ok) return new Response("bad signature", { status: 400 }); const event = JSON.parse(raw); // { type: "post.published", data: { post } } if (event.type === "post.failed") console.error(event.data.post.targets[0].error); return new Response("ok"); }How do I edit or cancel a scheduled LinkedIn post?There is no edit endpoint. Cancel the post with DELETE /v1/posts/:id and create a new one. Canceling works while no target has started publishing; once it's out, the same call deletes the published copy from LinkedIn instead.When you recreate the post, use a new idempotency key. Sending the old key with a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused. A canceled post fires post.canceled.Why would a scheduled LinkedIn post fail?The most common cause is an expired token. LinkedIn access tokens last 60 days, and without LinkedIn partner access there is no refresh token. A post scheduled 90 days after the profile was connected is sent with an expired token; LinkedIn rejects it, the account moves to needs_reauth, and the target fails with account_needs_reauth, which doesn't retry.Plan for it: every account carries connected_at, so send the profile owner a fresh connect link before 60 days pass, and listen for the account.needs_reauth webhook to catch the ones you miss. The other failures are covered in the troubleshooting list below.text_too_long: over 3,000 characters. Shorten it; see the LinkedIn character limit page.scheduled_in_past: scheduled_at is more than 5 minutes in the past. Pass a future time, or omit it to publish now.scheduled_too_far: more than 365 days ahead.duplicate_content: the same text is already published or queued on this account from the last 24 hours. This counts when the post was created, not when it publishes, so two identical posts created today for different weeks still collide.daily_cap_reached: 50 posts created for this LinkedIn account in 24 hours, scheduled ones included. Load long queues a few days at a time.too_many_media: more than 20 images. Images are uploaded through LinkedIn's Images API, up to 20 MB each.When is LinkedIn's own scheduler the better choice?If one person writes and schedules their own posts by hand, use LinkedIn's built-in scheduler. LinkedIn Help says you can schedule a post between 10 minutes and 3 months ahead, on desktop or mobile, and edit, reschedule or delete it from the Scheduled posts page. Event and job posts can't be scheduled there.We have no calendar or composer. We're the better fit when software decides what to post: an app posting for its users, an agency system posting for many clients, or an AI agent running through our LinkedIn MCP server. We also support up to 365 days ahead and the same call reaches X and Bluesky; see crossposting. We post to personal profiles only for now, not company pages.How to schedule a LinkedIn post with the APIFive calls, most of them one-time setup.01Get an API keyPOST https://socialsforai.com/v1/workspaces returns an api_key (sk_...). Store it; it is shown once.02Connect the LinkedIn profilePOST /v1/connect-links with platforms set to linkedin. The person whose profile it is opens the url, signs in to LinkedIn and approves posting (the w_member_social permission). You get an account id (acc_...).03Check the post with a dry runSend the post with dry_run: true and your scheduled_at. You get back ok: true, or a list of issues such as text_too_long or scheduled_in_past, each with a fix. Nothing is stored.04Schedule itSend the same body without dry_run. The response is 201 with status scheduled. Keep the post id.05Get told when it publishesRegister a webhook for post.published and post.failed with POST /v1/webhooks, or poll GET /v1/posts/:id. To change your mind, DELETE /v1/posts/:id before the scheduled time.Sources, read 2026-11-01: LinkedIn Posts API (Microsoft Learn) · LinkedIn Help: post limits · LinkedIn Help: Schedule postsQuestionsWhat developers askHow far ahead can I schedule a LinkedIn post?+Through our API, up to 365 days ahead; anything later fails preflight with scheduled_too_far. LinkedIn's own scheduler allows 10 minutes to 3 months, per LinkedIn Help. Because LinkedIn tokens last 60 days without partner access, posts scheduled further out need the profile owner to reconnect before they come due.Can I edit a scheduled LinkedIn post?+Not in place. Cancel it with DELETE /v1/posts/:id and create a new post with a new idempotency key. Canceling works until the post starts publishing; after that the same call deletes the published post from LinkedIn.Can I schedule posts to a LinkedIn company page?+Not yet. We post to personal profiles using LinkedIn's w_member_social permission. Posting as a company page uses w_organization_social, which LinkedIn restricts to members with an admin or content role on that page, and we haven't built it. For pages today, LinkedIn's own Page scheduler is the option.Does the LinkedIn API support scheduled posts natively?+No. LinkedIn's Posts API documentation says PUBLISHED is the only lifecycleState accepted when a post is created, so there is no future publish time field. Any tool that schedules LinkedIn posts through the API stores the post and calls LinkedIn at the scheduled time, which is what our delivery worker does every minute.How do I know a scheduled LinkedIn post went out?+Register a webhook for post.published and post.failed. The published event includes the post with LinkedIn's URN and URL on each target. Each request carries a Socials-Signature header, an HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp and raw body, so you can verify it came from us. Polling GET /v1/posts/:id works too.Can an AI agent schedule LinkedIn posts?+Yes. Connect our MCP server to Claude Code, Cursor or another MCP client, and the agent gets a create_post tool that accepts the same scheduled_at field. It can also call list_posts and cancel_post. The agent never sees LinkedIn credentials; it works with account ids.Keep readingLinkedIn APILinkedIn MCP serverLinkedIn character limitLinkedIn post previewSchedule tweetsGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/schedule-tweets.body_text: Schedule Tweets with an API (X Scheduling for Developers)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keySchedule tweets with an APISchedule posts on X without a scheduler app.Pass a time. We hold the post, publish it through X's API when it's due, retry if X is down, and tell your webhook when it's live.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To schedule a post on X (Twitter) programmatically, send it to POST /v1/posts with scheduled_at set to an ISO-8601 time up to 365 days ahead. It's checked against X's 280-character weighted limit when you create it, held until the time, then published through X's API. X's per-post fee applies only when it actually goes out.X: live. Posting to X works on the API today.How does scheduling a tweet through the API work?X's API creates posts immediately; there is no future publish time on POST /2/tweets. A scheduler stores the post and calls X at the right moment. With us, that's one field: add scheduled_at to the request and we store the post with status scheduled.Our delivery worker runs every minute. When the time comes, it checks the X account is still connected, refreshes the OAuth token if it's close to expiring, uploads any images, creates the post on X and reads it back to confirm it exists. The result goes to your webhook and to GET /v1/posts/:id.If X is unavailable or rate-limits the request, the attempt is retried after 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m and 2h. After six attempts the target is failed with the last error. A post scheduled for 09:00 during an X outage can therefore go out late; check attempts and published_at on the target to see when it actually went out.A worked example: schedule a launch postThis schedules one X post with a link for 9:00 New York time. The text is 131 characters as JavaScript counts them but 120 weighted characters as X counts them, because the 34-character URL counts as 23.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-v2-4-x" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_x_company"], "text": "v2.4 is out: cancel scheduled posts from the API, 24h webhook retries, custom Bluesky PDS hosts. https://example.com/changelog/v2-4", "scheduled_at": "2026-11-10T09:00:00-05:00" }'What comes back when you schedule a tweet?A 201 with status: "scheduled" and the time normalized to UTC (trimmed here to the relevant fields). Because the text contains a link, the response also carries an x_link_cost warning. It doesn't block the post; it tells you this post will be billed by X at the with-URL rate, $0.200 instead of $0.015.json{ "id": "post_c8Wq1NfZ4yHs6TbA", "object": "post", "status": "scheduled", "scheduled_at": "2026-11-10T14:00:00.000Z", "targets": [ { "id": "tgt_P0xEo7Jr2mLa9VuK", "account_id": "acc_x_company", "platform": "x", "status": "pending", "attempts": 0, "next_attempt_at": "2026-11-10T14:00:00.000Z", "url": null, "error": null } ], "warnings": [ { "account_id": "acc_x_company", "platform": "x", "severity": "warning", "code": "x_link_cost", "message": "Posts with a URL cost $0.200 through the X API instead of $0.015 (docs.x.com pricing).", "fix": "Remove the link, or send a link-free version for X in platform_options.x.text. A link in a reply is also billed at the with-URL rate." } ] }How do I schedule a batch of tweets?Send one request per post, each with its own scheduled_at and idempotency key. Here is a week of daily posts from a Python list. If the script dies halfway and you rerun it, the keys make the already-created posts come back as replays instead of duplicates.Two limits shape batch loads. The fair-use cap of 100 posts per X account counts posts created for that account in the last 24 hours, scheduled ones included, so loading a month of hourly posts in one go stops at 100 with daily_cap_reached; load a few days at a time. And on the Free plan, every created post counts toward the 100-posts-a-month limit when it's created.pythonimport os, requests from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone API = "https://socialsforai.com" headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SOCIALS_API_KEY']}"} start = datetime(2026, 11, 10, 14, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc) for day, text in enumerate(daily_tips): # 7 different strings when = (start + timedelta(days=day)).isoformat() r = requests.post(f"{API}/v1/posts", headers={**headers, "Idempotency-Key": f"tips-{when}"}, json={"accounts": ["acc_x_company"], "text": text, "scheduled_at": when}) if r.status_code == 422: for issue in r.json()["error"]["issues"]: print(day, issue["code"], issue["fix"]) else: r.raise_for_status()Common mistakes when scheduling tweetsMost scheduling bugs are about time zones, duplicates and counting.Timestamps without a time zone. 2026-11-10T09:00:00 is rejected with a 400 validation_error. Add Z for UTC or an offset like -05:00.Times slightly in the past. A scheduled_at up to 5 minutes ago publishes immediately; more than 5 minutes ago fails with scheduled_in_past. Clock skew on your server is the usual cause.Recycled text. Two posts with identical text for the same account, created within 24 hours of each other, fail with duplicate_content, even if they're scheduled a week apart.Counting with len() or .length. X weights characters. Check with the X character counter or dry_run, and read how the weights work on the X character limit page.Editing by resending. There is no edit. Cancel and recreate with a new idempotency key; the old key with a new body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused.How do I troubleshoot a scheduled tweet that didn't post?Call GET /v1/posts/:id and read the target's status, attempts, next_attempt_at and error. The error.code tells you what happened.Status pending with attempts above 0 and a next_attempt_at: a retryable failure (platform_rate_limited, platform_unavailable). It's waiting for the next retry; do nothing.account_needs_reauth: X refused the token and it couldn't be refreshed. Send the account owner a new connect link, then recreate the post.duplicate_content from X: X itself rejected the text as a duplicate. Change the text and create a new post.platform_rejected: X refused the post for another reason; its response is in the message.Status canceled: someone called DELETE /v1/posts/:id. Nothing was sent to X and nothing was charged.Should you use X's own scheduler instead?If a person schedules their own posts by hand, yes. X's own scheduling tools show the post as it will look, with no API work. Paying for an API makes no sense for that workflow.An API is the better fit when software decides what goes out: a product that posts for its users, a pipeline that announces releases, a Twitter bot, or an agent using our X MCP server. It's also the only way to schedule the same announcement to X, Bluesky and LinkedIn in one call; see crossposting. X's per-post fees still apply; see X API pricing.How to schedule tweets with an API01Get a key and connect XPOST https://socialsforai.com/v1/workspaces for an API key, then POST /v1/connect-links with platforms set to x. The account owner opens the link and approves on X. You get an account id.02Write the post and check itSend it with dry_run: true. Preflight counts the text the way X does (URLs 23, emoji and CJK 2) and returns text_too_long with the overage if it doesn't fit.03Add scheduled_atSet scheduled_at to a UTC time like 2026-11-10T14:00:00Z, or a local time with an offset like 2026-11-10T09:00:00-05:00. Up to 365 days ahead.04Send it with an idempotency keyPOST /v1/posts with an Idempotency-Key header. The response is 201 with status scheduled. A network retry with the same key returns the same post instead of a second one.05Track or cancel itA post.published or post.failed webhook fires when it's done. Before then, DELETE /v1/posts/:id cancels it and nothing is sent to X.Sources, read 2026-11-01: X API pricing (docs.x.com) · Counting characters (docs.x.com) · X API rate limits (docs.x.com)QuestionsWhat developers askIs a scheduled post charged if I cancel it?+No. Nothing is sent to X until the scheduled time, so a post canceled with DELETE /v1/posts/:id before then never reaches X and X charges nothing. Once it has published, the same call deletes it from X instead, and X charges $0.010 for the delete.How far in advance can I schedule tweets with the API?+Up to 365 days. A scheduled_at further out fails preflight with scheduled_too_far, and one more than 5 minutes in the past fails with scheduled_in_past. X OAuth tokens refresh automatically, so a post scheduled months ahead doesn't need the account to reconnect, unless the owner revokes access.How accurate is the scheduled time?+Our delivery worker runs every minute, so a post normally goes out within about a minute after its scheduled_at. If X returns a rate limit or server error, the attempt is retried after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours, so an outage can delay a post. The target's attempts and published_at fields show what happened.Can I schedule a tweet with images?+Yes. Add up to 4 images in the media array as public https URLs, at most 5 MB each, with optional alt text. The images are fetched and uploaded to X when the post publishes, not when you schedule it, so keep the URLs reachable until the scheduled time. A scheduled video works the same way: 1 per post, up to 200 MB.How many tweets can I schedule per day?+Our fair-use cap is 100 posts per X account in a rolling 24 hours, counted when posts are created, scheduled ones included. X's own rate-limit docs list POST /2/tweets at 100 requests per 15 minutes per user. For long queues, create posts a few days at a time.Can I schedule a thread?+Not as a thread. The API creates standalone posts and has no reply-to field yet, so you can schedule several posts a minute apart, but they won't be linked as replies on X. Each post in such a sequence needs its own distinct text, or the later ones fail preflight with duplicate_content.Keep readingHow to make an X botX API pricingX character counterSchedule LinkedIn postsX MCP serverGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

Choose Connect, sign in with your email in the window that opens, pick or create a workspace, and approve.Custom connectors are available on Claude plans that support them.02Claude CodeAdd the server, then sign in from inside a session: run /mcp, pick socials, and choose Authenticate.terminalclaude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcpOr install the plugin, which adds the server and the agent skill together:claude code/plugin marketplace add SocialsForAi/socialsforai /plugin install socialsforai@socialsforai03CursorInstall with one click, then choose Connect next to socials in Cursor's MCP settings to sign in.Add to Cursor04VS CodeInstall with one click; VS Code asks you to sign in the first time the agent uses a tool.Add to VS Code05Any agent with a shellAgents that can make web requests (Claude Code, Codex, scripts) can sign up on their own through the REST API. https://socialsforai.com/social-media-ap.body_text: Social Media API for Developers and AI Agents (2026)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keySocial media APIOne API for every feed your agent posts to.Connect an account once, then publish with a single request. X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live today. Every response says which accounts published, which are retrying, and why.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026A social media API lets software publish posts to social networks without a person pressing "post". A unified social media API like SocialsForAI wraps each network's own API (X API v2, LinkedIn's Posts API, Bluesky's AT Protocol) behind one endpoint, one connect flow for account owners and one error format, so an app or AI agent writes one integration instead of one per network.What we check before a post goes out, per networkNetworkText limitImagesVideoFair-use cap per accountStatusBluesky300 graphemes4, up to 2 MB each1 MP4, up to 100 MB300 posts / 24hLiveX280 weighted characters (URLs count 23)4, up to 5 MB each1 MP4 or MOV, up to 200 MB100 posts / 24hLiveLinkedIn3,000 charactersUp to 20, up to 20 MB each1 MP4, up to 200 MB50 posts / 24hLive, personal profiles onlyMastodon500 characters (URLs count 23), any server4, up to 16 MB each1, up to 99 MB300 posts / 24hLiveTelegram4,096 characters; 1,024 as a caption with mediaUp to 10, up to 10 MB eachUp to 10 photos and videos combined, 50 MB per video500 posts / 24hLive, channels and groups via your botLimits are the ones our preflight enforces (src/providers). Platform limits come from each network's docs, read 2026-11-01. On X, Bluesky, LinkedIn and Mastodon a video can't share a post with images; Mastodon servers may set lower size limits.What is a social media API?A social media API is an HTTP interface that lets code create posts, upload media or read data on a social network. The phrase covers two different products, and search results mix them up.Posting APIs act for an account that has granted permission: they publish, schedule and delete. Data APIs read public profiles and posts, often by scraping, and sell the results per request. This page is about posting. If you need follower counts or competitor posts, a data API is the tool, and we don't sell one.Posting APIs come in two shapes. First-party APIs belong to the network: the X API, LinkedIn's Posts API, Bluesky's AT Protocol, Meta's Instagram Graph API, TikTok's Content Posting API. Unified APIs (us, Ayrshare, Postiz's public API and others) sit in front of several first-party APIs and give you one request format for all of them.What does one API call do?One POST /v1/posts checks the post against every target network's limits, publishes to each account in parallel, reads the post back where the network allows it, and returns one receipt. You send text, optional media URLs and a list of account ids.The checks run before anything leaves our servers: length (weighted for X, graphemes for Bluesky), image count, empty posts, the same text on the same account in the last 24 hours, and per-account fair-use caps. They are plain code with no AI calls, so a dry_run: true request costs nothing and posts nothing.Send an Idempotency-Key header. If your request times out and you retry with the same key and body, you get the original post back with Idempotent-Replayed: true instead of a second post. The same key with a different body returns 409 idempotency_key_reused.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-0412" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_bluesky", "acc_linkedin", "acc_x"], "text": "We just shipped webhooks.", "wait": true }'What does the response look like?Every post has one target per account, and each target carries its own status, URL, attempt count and error. The post's overall status is published, partially_published, failed, scheduled, publishing or canceled, derived from its targets.In the response below, Bluesky published and was verified by reading the post back. LinkedIn failed because its 60-day token expired; the error says so and says what to do. With wait: true the call returns after delivery; without it you get 201 straight away and a post.published, post.partially_published or post.failed webhook later.jsonHTTP/1.1 201 Created (trimmed: media, metadata, target ids and some target fields omitted) { "id": "post_9fQ2mXc4LpZr8TwA", "object": "post", "status": "partially_published", "text": "We just shipped webhooks.", "scheduled_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-01T15:04:05.000Z", "completed_at": "2026-11-01T15:04:07.000Z", "targets": [ { "account_id": "acc_bluesky", "platform": "bluesky", "status": "published", "url": "https://bsky.app/profile/acme.bsky.social/post/3m4xq7k2c2s2a", "attempts": 1, "verified": true, "error": null }, { "account_id": "acc_linkedin", "platform": "linkedin", "status": "failed", "url": null, "attempts": 1, "verified": false, "error": { "code": "account_needs_reauth", "message": "LinkedIn access token expired (they last 60 days).", "fix": "Reconnect the LinkedIn account with a new connect link.", "retryable": false } } ] }What errors come back, and how do you fix them?Errors that we can predict come back before publishing as a 422 preflight_failed, listing every issue with the account, the field and a fix sentence. Nothing is published when any account fails preflight, so you never get half a launch because one network's text was too long.Errors from the network itself land on the target. Retryable ones (platform_rate_limited, platform_unavailable, media_fetch_failed on a 5xx) retry after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours, six attempts in all, then the target becomes failed. Permanent ones stop at once.text_too_long: shorten it, or set platform_options.x.text (or .bluesky, .linkedin) to a per-network version.too_many_media: X and Bluesky take 4 images, LinkedIn 20.duplicate_content: same text, same account, last 24 hours. Vary it or wait.daily_cap_reached: schedule it with scheduled_at instead.account_needs_reauth: send the owner a new connect link; an account.needs_reauth webhook fires when this happens.too_many_videos and mixed_media: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn and Mastodon take 1 video per post and no images alongside it. Send the video as its own post.plan_limit_active_accounts and plan_limit_posts: Free plan limits (3 active accounts, 100 posts a month).jsonHTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity { "error": { "code": "preflight_failed", "message": "The post would fail on 1 check(s). Nothing was published.", "fix": "Fix the issues below, or send dry_run: true to iterate without publishing.", "issues": [ { "account_id": "acc_x", "platform": "x", "severity": "error", "code": "text_too_long", "field": "platform_options.x.text", "message": "Text is 312 characters; X allows 280.", "fix": "Shorten it by 32+ characters, or set platform_options.x.text to a shorter version." } ] } }Should you use a network's own API or a unified API?Use the network's own API when you post to one network, from accounts you control, and need features a unified layer doesn't expose. That is a real and common case, and the first-party route is cheaper and has fewer moving parts.Use a unified API when you post to two or more networks, or post for other people. Posting for other people is where first-party work grows: each network wants its own developer app, its own review (LinkedIn's Community Management API, Meta's App Review, TikTok's audit) and its own token refresh rules.Go first-party for one Bluesky bot. The AT Protocol has no app review and no fee; our Bluesky API guide shows the raw calls.Go first-party for quote posts, DMs, reading timelines or replying to other people's posts. We don't do those.Go unified when an AI agent posts. Structured code and fix fields, idempotency keys and an MCP server save you writing that layer.Go unified when end users connect their own accounts and you don't want to hold their tokens or build reconnect flows.How do accounts get connected?The account owner opens a hosted connect link: OAuth for X and LinkedIn, an app password for Bluesky, the server URL and an access token for Mastodon, and a bot token plus channel or group for Telegram. You never see their password, and stored credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM and deleted on disconnect.Tag the link with external_ref (your client id or user id) and every account it creates carries it. Links expire after 7 days by default, configurable from 5 minutes to 30 days. Set redirect_url and the owner lands back in your app with account_id, platform and status=connected in the query string.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/connect-links \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "platforms": ["bluesky", "linkedin"], "external_ref": "client_42", "redirect_url": "https://yourapp.example/connected" }' # 201 → { "id": "cl_...", "object": "connect_link", "url": "...", "expires_at": "..." }How much does a social media API cost?First-party posting is cheap or free in money: Bluesky charges nothing, LinkedIn publishes no per-call price, and X charges $0.015 per post and $0.200 per post with a link. The cost is engineering and review time. See X API pricing and LinkedIn API pricing for the detail.We charge per active account, meaning one that published that month. Free covers 3 active accounts and 100 posts a month; Hobby is $9 for 5; Pro is $29 for 25; Growth is $79 for 100. Posts are unlimited on paid plans and X's fees pass through at cost. Paid plans start from the dashboard's Billing page and cancel any time. Full table on pricing.Other unified APIs price differently: Ayrshare starts at $149 a month for one profile, Postiz at $29 for 5 channels (read on their pricing pages). The comparisons are at vs Ayrshare and vs Postiz.Can an AI agent use the API directly?Yes. The same operations are exposed as an MCP server over Streamable HTTP at /api/mcp, with tools for listing platforms and accounts, creating connect links, creating, reading and canceling posts, and checking usage. create_post waits for delivery by default so the agent sees the result in the same turn.An agent can even get its own key: POST /v1/workspaces returns a Free-plan API key without a browser. Setup for Claude Code is one command.bashclaude mcp add --transport http socials https://socialsforai.com/api/mcp \ --header "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY"From zero to a published post01Get a keyPOST /v1/workspaces returns a Free-plan API key. Store it; it isn't shown again. Agents can do this step themselves.02Send a connect linkPOST /v1/connect-links returns a URL. The account owner opens it, approves access, and the account appears in GET /v1/accounts.03Dry-run the postPOST /v1/posts with dry_run set to true returns every issue with a fix and a per-account preview of the text, and publishes nothing.04PublishSend it for real with wait set to true and an Idempotency-Key header. Retrying with the same key never posts twice.05Listen for webhooksRegister an endpoint with POST /v1/webhooks. Payloads are signed with HMAC-SHA256 in the Socials-Signature header, and failed deliveries retry on a schedule from 1 minute to 24 hours.Sources, read 2026-11-01: X API pricing (docs.x.com) · Counting characters (docs.x.com) · LinkedIn Posts API (Microsoft Learn) · app.bsky.feed.post lexicon (atproto)QuestionsWhat developers askWhat is the best social media API for developers?+It depends on the networks and who owns the accounts. For one network and your own account, that network's API is simplest. For several networks, or for accounts your users own, a unified API saves building OAuth, token refresh and error handling per network. Compare pricing models too: per profile, per channel or per active account.Which networks can I post to with SocialsForAI?+X, Bluesky, LinkedIn personal profiles and Company Pages, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live. Instagram, Threads, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest and Reddit are coming and need platform review or are not built yet. Video posts on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram and Discord. GET /v1/platforms reports live status from the server's configuration.Is there a free social media API?+Bluesky's API is free to use for posting. LinkedIn doesn't charge per call for member posts. X charges per request with no free posting tier on its pricing page. Our Free plan covers 3 active accounts and 100 posts a month with every feature, so you can build and test without paying.Do I need my own developer app on each network?+Not with a unified API. Account owners connect through our apps with a connect link, and you hold one API key. If you go first-party instead, you register an app on each network and pass each network's review before posting for anyone outside your own team.Is there a dashboard?+No, on purpose. Everything runs through the REST API, the MCP server and webhooks. If you want a calendar and a drag-and-drop composer for a social media team, a scheduler like Postiz or Buffer is the better fit, and our comparison pages say so.What happens if a post fails on one network?+The other accounts still publish. The post comes back partially_published, the failed account carries an error with a code, a message and a fix, and transient errors retry on their own at 30 seconds, 2, 10 and 30 minutes and 2 hours before the target is marked failed.Keep readingMCP server for social mediaCrosspost to X, Bluesky and LinkedInX API pricingLinkedIn APIBluesky APICompare social media APIsGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/tiktok-api.body_text: TikTok Posting API (2026): Audit, Limits, Example | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyTikTok posting APITikTok lets apps post privately until they pass an audit.TikTok posting isn't live on our API yet. This is a guide to TikTok's own Content Posting API: the two posting modes, the audit, media rules and limits.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026TikTok's Content Posting API lets an app post videos and photo posts to a creator's account after the creator authorizes the video.publish scope, or send drafts to their inbox with video.upload. Until the app passes TikTok's audit, everything it posts is restricted to private viewing, and at most 5 users can post through it in a 24-hour window.TikTok: coming soon. Built; private posts only until TikTok's review. Everything else on this page describes the API as it works today.TikTok posting modesModeScopeWhat happensLimit to knowDirect Post (video)video.publishPosts to the profile with the privacy level the user picksPrivate-only until the app is auditedUpload to inbox (video)video.uploadCreator gets an inbox notification and finishes the post in TikTokAt most 5 pending shares per 24 hoursPhoto postvideo.publish (DIRECT_POST) or video.upload (MEDIA_UPLOAD)Up to 35 images, posted or sent to the creator to finishImages must be pulled from a verified URLFrom TikTok for Developers: Direct Post, Upload and Photo Post references, read 2026-11-01.TikTok media requirementsItemRequirementVideo formatsMP4 (recommended), WebM, MOVVideo codecsH.264 (recommended), H.265, VP8, VP9Video size and lengthUp to 4 GB; up to 10 minutes via the API, or less if the creator's max duration is lowerVideo frame and resolution23 to 60 fps; 360 to 4096 px on each sideUpload chunks5 MB to 64 MB each (last may be larger), 1 to 1,000 chunks, sent in orderPhotosJPEG or WebP, up to 1080p, 20 MB each, up to 35 per postVideo captionUp to 2,200 UTF-16 runesPhoto title and description90 and 4,000 UTF-16 runesFrom TikTok's media transfer guide and Content Posting API references.Does SocialsForAI support TikTok yet?No. TikTok posting isn't available on our API yet: it needs TikTok's audit, which our app hasn't been through. Video posting already works on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram and Discord, so the audit is what's missing. It goes live here only after approval and a public post going through end to end.X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live today; the social media API page has the details, and pricing shows how accounts are billed once a network is live. The rest of this page is about TikTok's own API, so you can judge whether to build on it directly.What does it take to post with the TikTok API?Register an app on TikTok for Developers, add the Content Posting API product, enable the Direct Post configuration, and get the video.publish scope approved. Each creator then authorizes your app for that scope, which gives you their user access token and open id.Before every post, TikTok requires a Query Creator Info call. It returns details such as the privacy levels the creator can use and their maximum video duration (the example in TikTok's docs shows 300 seconds), and your upload screen must use those values.What does the TikTok audit change?Unaudited apps can call the API, but TikTok restricts all their content to private viewing. Its sharing guidelines add that an unaudited client can let at most 5 users post in a 24-hour window, those accounts must be private, and posts must use SELF_ONLY visibility. Posting otherwise returns unaudited_client_can_only_post_to_private_accounts.That's why an unaudited app is fine for testing and useless for publishing for anyone else. Meta's equivalent gate for Instagram is App Review, covered in our Instagram API guide. To lift it, the client must pass TikTok's audit, and TikTok's content sharing guidelines describe the posting experience it expects:Show the creator's nickname on the upload screen.Offer the privacy levels from Query Creator Info with no default selected.Leave Comment, Duet and Stitch toggles off by default, and grey out ones the creator has disabled.Include a commercial content disclosure, off by default, with Your brand and Branded content options; branded content can't be private.Show a preview, let the user edit preset titles and hashtags, and only upload after they consent.Don't add promotional watermarks or logos to creators' content.How does a TikTok Direct Post request work?Call POST https://open.tiktokapis.com/v2/post/publish/video/init/ with a post_info object (caption, privacy_level and interaction settings) and a source_info object. With FILE_UPLOAD you declare the size and chunking and get back an upload_url, which expires after one hour; with PULL_FROM_URL TikTok fetches the file itself.The response carries a publish_id. Processing is asynchronous, so poll the post status endpoint or use webhooks, and tell the user it may take a few minutes to appear on their profile. If an AI agent drives the upload, the consent and preview rules above still apply; our MCP server doesn't offer TikTok yet.bashcurl -X POST https://open.tiktokapis.com/v2/post/publish/video/init/ \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $TIKTOK_USER_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=UTF-8" \ -d '{ "post_info": { "title": "Shipping day #buildinpublic", "privacy_level": "SELF_ONLY", "disable_comment": false, "disable_duet": false, "disable_stitch": false }, "source_info": { "source": "PULL_FROM_URL", "video_url": "https://media.example.com/launch.mp4" } }' # 200 → { "data": { "publish_id": "..." }, "error": { "code": "ok" } }Why does PULL_FROM_URL need domain verification?TikTok only pulls media from URLs it knows you own. Verify a domain by adding a signature string to its DNS records, and every path under it and its subdomains counts as yours; or verify a URL prefix. Pulling from an unverified URL returns url_ownership_unverified.The URL must be HTTPS, its host must be a domain rather than an IP address, and it must not redirect. Photo posts only accept PULL_FROM_URL, so photo posting needs this set up from day one.What are the TikTok API posting limits?Each user access token can make 6 requests per minute to the posting endpoints; going over returns 429 rate_limit_exceeded. Each creator also has a daily post cap that varies by creator and is typically around 15 posts a day, per TikTok's sharing guidelines, returned as spam_risk_too_many_posts.On top of that, each API client has a 24-hour cap on how many creators can actively post through it (reached_active_user_cap), and inbox uploads allow at most 5 pending shares per 24 hours (spam_risk_too_many_pending_share).What TikTok API errors should you plan for?The Direct Post reference lists these. Most of them mean show the user a message, not retry:401 access_token_invalid or scope_not_authorized: refresh the token or ask the creator to grant video.publish.403 privacy_level_option_mismatch: the privacy level isn't one Query Creator Info returned.403 spam_risk_user_banned_from_posting: the creator can't post right now; nothing to retry.400 invalid_param: read the error message for the field at fault, such as chunk sizes that don't match video_size.5xx: TikTok server or network error; retry later.Sources, read 2026-11-01: TikTok Content Posting API: get started (TikTok for Developers) · TikTok Direct Post API reference · TikTok Upload (inbox) API reference · TikTok Photo Post API reference · TikTok content sharing guidelines · TikTok media transfer guideQuestionsWhat developers askWhy can't unaudited TikTok apps post publicly?+TikTok restricts all content from unaudited Content Posting API clients to private viewing. Its guidelines also limit an unaudited client to 5 posting users per 24 hours, all with private accounts. Passing TikTok's audit lifts the restriction; TikTok's content sharing guidelines describe the posting experience it expects.Is the TikTok Content Posting API free?+TikTok's developer docs for the Content Posting API describe scopes, audits and rate limits but no per-call price. The constraints are access and volume: an audit before public posting, 6 requests per minute per user token, and a per-creator daily post cap that is typically around 15.What's the difference between Direct Post and upload to inbox?+Direct Post, with the video.publish scope, publishes to the creator's profile with the privacy level they choose. Upload, with video.upload, sends the video to the creator's TikTok inbox and they finish editing and posting in the app. Inbox uploads allow at most 5 pending shares per 24 hours.Can I post photos with the TikTok API?+Yes. The photo post endpoint takes up to 35 JPEG or WebP images, each up to 1080p and 20 MB, in DIRECT_POST or MEDIA_UPLOAD mode. Photos must use PULL_FROM_URL, so the image host needs a verified domain or URL prefix.How long can a video posted by API be?+TikTok's media transfer guide says the longest video you can send through the upload endpoint is 10 minutes, up to 4 GB. The creator's own maximum, returned by Query Creator Info, can be lower, and your app must check the video against it before posting.When will TikTok work on your API?+After our app passes TikTok's audit, which hasn't happened yet. Video posting is already built and live on X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon and Telegram. This page will show the change, TikTok will appear in the platforms endpoint, and we mark TikTok live only after a public post goes through end to end.Keep readingInstagram posting APISocial media APIMCP server for social mediaPricingGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/tools/bluesky-c.body_text: Bluesky Character Counter: 300 Graphemes (Free)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyBluesky character counter300 graphemes. Count them properly.Bluesky counts what you see as one character, not code units. Bytes matter too.Your postFamily update 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 counts as one grapheme on Bluesky.Graphemes: 50 / 300 (250 left)Bytes: 74 / 3,000 (2,926 left)The short answerA Bluesky character counter measures a post against Bluesky's two limits from the app.bsky.feed.post lexicon: 300 graphemes and 3,000 UTF-8 bytes. A grapheme is one character as a reader sees it, so a family emoji built from seven code points counts once. This counter shows both numbers live, because emoji-heavy posts can hit the byte limit first.Graphemes, code points, UTF-16 and bytesText has at least four lengths, and different tools report different ones. A grapheme is what a reader sees as one character. A code point is one Unicode character number. JavaScript's .length counts UTF-16 code units, where characters outside the basic range take two. Bytes are the size of the text in UTF-8, the encoding Bluesky stores. These numbers come from running the counter's own functions:"hello": 5 graphemes, 5 code points, 5 UTF-16 units, 5 bytes."café" typed as one é: 4 graphemes, 4 code points, 4 units, 5 bytes."café" typed as e plus a combining accent: still 4 graphemes, but 5 code points, 5 units, 6 bytes."👍🏽" (thumbs-up with skin tone): 1 grapheme, 2 code points, 4 units, 8 bytes."👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" (family): 1 grapheme, 7 code points, 11 units, 25 bytes."🇺🇸" (a flag): 1 grapheme, 2 code points, 4 units, 8 bytes."日本語": 3 graphemes, 3 code points, 3 units, 9 bytes."𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱" (Unicode bold): 4 graphemes, 4 code points, 8 units, 16 bytes.Two limits: 300 graphemes and 3,000 bytesThe post record's text field in Bluesky's app.bsky.feed.post lexicon has maxGraphemes: 300 and maxLength: 3000, where the length is in bytes. A post has to satisfy both. For most writing, the grapheme limit is the one you hit: 300 plain Latin letters are 300 bytes, and 300 Japanese characters are 900 bytes, both well under 3,000.Emoji are where bytes catch up. A family emoji is 1 grapheme but 25 bytes, so 120 of them reach 3,000 bytes while using only 120 of the 300 graphemes. Three hundred of them would be 7,500 bytes. If a post is mostly emoji or flags, watch the byte meter rather than the grapheme one.Bluesky's 300 is higher than X's 280, and the units differ. The sample in the box, "Family update 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 counts as one grapheme on Bluesky.", is 50 graphemes and 74 bytes here, and weighs 51 in the X character counter. More on the rules in our Bluesky character limit guide.Links, mentions and hashtags are facetsA Bluesky post stores links, @mentions and hashtags separately from the text, as facets. Each facet points at a slice of the text by byte offsets. The facet lexicon puts it directly: indices count "bytes of the UTF-8 encoded text", and languages like JavaScript that index strings by UTF-16 or code points need to convert before working with facets. An off-by-a-few offset is the classic bug in hand-written Bluesky clients when the text contains emoji or accented letters.Unlike X, Bluesky doesn't give links a fixed weight. A URL you put in the text counts its full length, as written, toward 300 graphemes: "https://example.com/docs/webhooks" is 33 graphemes on Bluesky and 23 on X. Long tracking links are expensive here, so trim query strings you don't need.When you post through our Bluesky API, facets are detected automatically from the text with the official @atproto/api library (RichText.detectFacets), so links, mentions and hashtags come out clickable without you computing byte offsets.Alt text for imagesBluesky posts can carry up to 4 images, each up to 2,000,000 bytes, per the app.bsky.embed.images lexicon. Every image object has a required alt field, described there as "Alt text description of the image, for accessibility". The lexicon requires the field but allows it to be an empty string, so an image can be posted with no description at all.Write one anyway. Alt text is what screen reader users get in place of the image, and it doesn't count toward the 300 graphemes of the post text. In our API, pass it as alt on each media item; if you leave it out we send an empty string, which is valid but tells a screen reader user nothing.json{ "accounts": ["acc_..."], "text": "New docs for webhooks are up.", "media": [{ "url": "https://example.com/webhooks-diagram.png", "alt": "Diagram: a post is published, then a signed webhook is sent to your server." }] }What happens over the limit through our APIBluesky is one of the eight networks live on our API. Before anything is sent, our preflight check counts the text in graphemes, the same function this counter uses. Over 300, the request fails with HTTP 422, preflight_failed, and a text_too_long issue that says how much to cut. Nothing is published to any account in the request. Send dry_run: true to run the checks without posting.The check covers both limits. A post under 300 graphemes but over 3,000 bytes, which takes a lot of emoji, also fails with text_too_long, and the message gives the byte count. The byte meter above shows the same number as you type.json{ "error": { "code": "preflight_failed", "message": "The post would fail on 1 check(s). Nothing was published.", "fix": "Fix the issues below, or send dry_run: true to iterate without publishing.", "issues": [{ "account_id": "acc_...", "platform": "bluesky", "severity": "error", "code": "text_too_long", "field": "platform_options.bluesky.text", "message": "Text is 312 characters; Bluesky allows 300.", "fix": "Shorten it by 12+ characters, or set platform_options.bluesky.text to a shorter version." }] } }Posting the same text to Bluesky, X and LinkedInThe same draft lands differently on each network: 300 graphemes on Bluesky, 280 weighted characters on X, 3,000 characters on LinkedIn. A post that fits Bluesky with a long link may be over on X once its emoji double, or under on X because its link shrinks to 23. Use platform_options to give a network its own version of the text when one draft can't fit all three. Our cross-posting guide walks through it, and the docs list every field.QuestionsAbout this toolWhat's the Bluesky character limit?+300 graphemes and 3,000 UTF-8 bytes, from the text field of Bluesky's app.bsky.feed.post lexicon. A post must satisfy both. Ordinary writing hits the 300 grapheme limit long before 3,000 bytes; posts packed with emoji can hit the byte limit first, which is why this counter shows both numbers.What's a grapheme?+A grapheme is one character as a reader sees it, even when it is built from several Unicode code points. "👍🏽" is two code points but one grapheme, and the family emoji "👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" is seven code points but one grapheme. Bluesky's 300 limit counts graphemes, so each of those counts once.Why does an emoji count as one character on Bluesky but two on X?+The networks count differently. Bluesky counts graphemes, so any emoji, however complex, is 1. X uses weighted characters and its docs say every emoji counts 2. The same family emoji is 1 grapheme on Bluesky, 2 on X, and 25 bytes toward Bluesky's separate 3,000-byte limit.Do links count toward Bluesky's 300 characters?+Yes, at their full length. Bluesky doesn't shorten links to a fixed weight the way X does with t.co. "https://example.com/docs/webhooks" counts 33 graphemes on Bluesky and 23 on X. The link itself is stored as a facet, a byte range over the text, which makes it clickable.Does alt text count toward the 300 limit?+No. Alt text is stored on each image in the app.bsky.embed.images record, separately from the post text, so it doesn't use any of the 300 graphemes. The lexicon requires an alt field on every image but allows an empty string. Write a real description; it is what screen reader users get instead of the image.What happens if I post more than 300 graphemes through the API?+Our API rejects it before posting, with HTTP 422 preflight_failed and a text_too_long issue that names the length, the limit and how much to cut. Nothing is published. The check covers both limits, so a post under 300 graphemes but over 3,000 bytes is caught the same way.Posting from code or an agent? https://socialsforai.com/tools/linkedin-.body_text: LinkedIn Post Preview: See the "See More" Cut (Free)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyLinkedIn post previewSee where LinkedIn will cut your post off.Paste a draft to see roughly what shows before "…see more" and how close you are to 3,000 characters.DraftMost posts lose the reader before "see more". Put the point in the first line. Here's what we changed…Characters: 103 / 3,000 (2,897 left)Approximate feed viewYour NameYour headline · NowMost posts lose the reader before "see more". Put the point in the first line. Here's what we changed…An estimate: about 210 characters or 3 lines. LinkedIn's real cut varies by device.The short answerLinkedIn shows the first lines of a post in the feed and hides the rest behind "…see more". A post preview tool approximates that cut so you can check that the opening carries the point. The real cut depends on the device, screen width and line breaks; this preview estimates it at about 210 characters or 3 lines, whichever comes first.How this preview estimates the cutThe preview runs a short rule in your browser. It splits your draft on line breaks and takes lines from the top until it has three lines or 210 characters, whichever comes first. If that leaves any of your text out, it shows the opening followed by "…see more". Click it to expand the full post, the way you would in the feed.A few details of that rule are worth knowing, because they change what you see:A blank line is a line. A one-line hook followed by an empty line uses two of the three lines, so only one more line shows.A long paragraph with no line breaks is cut at 210 characters, even mid-word.The 210 is measured in UTF-16 code units, so a Unicode bold or italic letter from the LinkedIn text formatter uses two of them. A styled opening reaches the cut sooner.The character meter under the draft counts graphemes against 3,000, separately from the preview.Why the real cut varies by deviceLinkedIn doesn't publish a fixed cut-off point in its Help pages that we could find, and it would be hard to: the feed truncates by rendered lines, and how many words fit on a line depends on screen width, font size, the app versus the browser, and the length of each word. A line that fits in one row on a laptop can wrap to two on a phone, which pushes later lines below the fold.Treat 210 characters and three lines as a planning number, not a guarantee. The check that matters is the published post on your own phone, ideally before many people have seen it.Three drafts, three cutsThe same information, laid out three ways, run through this preview's rule. The text is about our retry schedule, which is real: failed posts retry after 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes, 30 minutes and 2 hours.Short paragraphs with blank lines between them (179 characters): the preview shows the first sentence, the blank line and the schedule line, 120 characters in all. The third paragraph is hidden. The point is visible, but the blank line cost a whole line.The same sentences on consecutive lines with no blank lines (214 characters): three full lines show, 177 characters, and only the fourth line is hidden. More fits, at the cost of a denser block.One long paragraph (252 characters) that opens with "We spent a while thinking about how retries should work": the cut lands at 210 characters, in the middle of the word "roughly", before the reader learns there are five retries. The opening is spent on preamble.Writing the opening linesThese are editing habits, not rules backed by data. LinkedIn's ranking isn't public and we have no engagement numbers of our own. What the preview does show you is which words a reader gets before deciding whether to tap.Put the news or the claim in the first sentence. "Our API now retries failed posts five times" tells the reader what the post is about; "We spent a while thinking about" doesn't.Finish the first sentence before the cut. A sentence that breaks mid-thought at "see more" reads as a teaser, and some readers won't tap.Name the specific thing: the product, the number, the result. Specifics survive truncation better than setup.Spend blank lines on purpose. One after the hook makes it stand out; two in the first three lines leaves almost nothing visible.If you bold anything, bold the hook or a short label, not the whole opening. Styled letters use more of the 210-character estimate and some screen readers skip them.Don't hold the link or the call to action until the end if it is the point of the post. Many readers only see the opening.Formatting checklist before you postRun through this with the draft in the preview:The first line makes sense on its own, without anything below the cut.No more than one blank line in the first three lines.Hashtags, names and keywords are in plain text, not Unicode bold.Lists use line breaks, one item per line, so they scan on a phone.The total is under 3,000 characters, with room to spare if the post uses a lot of styled text.Any link is one you have opened from the draft, and it is placed where readers will reach it.You have opened the published post on a phone to check the real cut.The 3,000 character limitLinkedIn Help (read Nov 1, 2026) says a post can be up to 3,000 characters. That is a lot of room compared with the opening: this preview's 210-character estimate is 7 percent of it. Length is rarely the problem. The opening is.The meter in this tool counts graphemes, the characters you see, which is the same way our API counts LinkedIn text before posting. A draft over 3,000 is rejected by our API's preflight check with text_too_long and the exact number to cut, before anything is sent to LinkedIn. Details, including how styled letters and emoji count, are in our LinkedIn character limit guide.Previewing posts that you publish from codeIf posts go out from a script, an app or an AI agent, the opening still matters, and nobody is looking at a composer. Our API's dry_run option runs the same preflight checks (length, media, duplicates, daily caps) and returns the issues without publishing, so a pipeline can catch a too-long draft before it reaches LinkedIn. LinkedIn posting to personal profiles is live; see the LinkedIn API page for how it works and Schedule LinkedIn posts for timing posts with scheduled_at.QuestionsAbout this toolWhere does LinkedIn cut off a post?+In the feed, LinkedIn shows the first few lines and hides the rest behind "…see more". The exact point depends on screen width, the app or browser, and your line breaks, and LinkedIn doesn't publish a fixed number. This tool estimates about 210 characters or three lines. Check the published post on your phone before relying on it.Do blank lines count toward what shows before "see more"?+In this preview, yes: a blank line uses one of the three lines. In the real feed, empty lines also take vertical space, so a hook followed by two blank lines leaves little room for anything else. One blank line after the opening sentence is usually enough to set it apart.What's the LinkedIn post character limit?+3,000 characters, per LinkedIn Help (read Nov 1, 2026). The meter in this tool counts graphemes, the characters you see, against that limit. Unicode bold and italic letters count as one character each here but take more space in storage, so leave a margin if a heavily styled post is close to 3,000.Why does my preview look different from LinkedIn on my phone?+This preview applies a fixed rule (210 characters or three lines), while LinkedIn truncates by rendered lines. On a narrow phone screen, a long line wraps to two, so fewer of your lines fit above the cut. On a wide desktop feed, more words fit. The preview is a planning aid, not a pixel-accurate copy of the feed.Does bold text change where the post gets cut?+It can. In this preview's estimate, each Unicode bold letter counts as two characters toward the 210, so a fully bold opening reaches the cut sooner. Bold a short label or a single hook line rather than the whole first paragraph.Does this preview save or upload my draft?+No. The preview runs in your browser, and the draft you paste stays on your device. Nothing is sent to our servers or to LinkedIn, and the text is gone when you close the tab. To publish, copy the text into LinkedIn or send it through an API.Posting from code or an agent? https://socialsforai.com/tools/linkedin-.body_text: LinkedIn Text Formatter: Bold & Italic Text (Free)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyLinkedIn text formatterBold, italic and monospace text for LinkedIn posts.Select words, pick a style, copy. Free, runs in your browser, nothing is sent anywhere.Your post. Select words to style them; with nothing selected, the whole post changes.Shipped: webhooks for every post. Three things we learned building them…𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱𝘐𝘵𝘢𝘭𝘪𝘤𝘽𝙤𝙡𝙙 𝙞𝙩𝙖𝙡𝙞𝙘𝙼𝚘𝚗𝚘U̲n̲d̲e̲r̲l̲i̲n̲e̲S̶t̶r̶i̶k̶e̶ClearCharacters: 73 / 3,000 (2,927 left)Copy textThe short answerLinkedIn's post format has no bold or italic markup. A LinkedIn text formatter swaps ordinary letters for look-alike characters from Unicode's Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols block, which display as bold, italic or monospace wherever plain text shows. Use it for a few words at most: several screen readers skip or spell out those characters, and they are different characters from the plain words.How the formatter makes bold and italicThere is no hidden formatting code in the text you copy. Each styled letter is a separate Unicode character that happens to be drawn bold or slanted. Unicode added these in the Mathematical Alphanumeric Symbols block (U+1D400 to U+1D7FF) so math notation could tell a bold variable from an italic one. The Unicode 18.0 code chart, read Nov 1, 2026, says it plainly: the block is "to be used for mathematical variables where style variations are important semantically. For general text, use standard Latin and Greek letters with markup."Social posts have no markup, so people borrow the math letters anyway. Here is exactly what each button does:Bold uses Mathematical Sans-Serif Bold (capital A is U+1D5D4), plus sans-serif bold digits.Italic uses Mathematical Sans-Serif Italic (capital A is U+1D608). Letters only.Bold italic uses Mathematical Sans-Serif Bold Italic (capital A is U+1D63C). Letters only.Mono uses Mathematical Monospace (capital A is U+1D670), plus monospace digits.Underline and Strike keep your letters and add a combining mark after each character: U+0332 (combining low line) or U+0336 (combining long stroke overlay). Spaces and line breaks are skipped.Clear maps every styled character back to plain A to Z, a to z and 0 to 9 and removes the underline and strike marks, so you can switch styles without retyping.What converts and what stays plainOnly the 26 basic Latin letters (both cases) and, for bold and mono, the digits 0 to 9 change. Everything else passes through untouched. Bold turns "Café déjà vu, 3 ideas" into 𝗖𝗮𝗳é 𝗱é𝗷à 𝘃𝘂, 𝟯 𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗮𝘀: the é and à stay regular weight in the middle of bold words.No italic digits. Unicode defines digit sets only for bold, double-struck, sans-serif, sans-serif bold and monospace. There are no sans-serif italic or bold italic digits, so "Hello 2026" in italic comes out as 𝘏𝘦𝘭𝘭𝘰 2026.No accented letters. The block has no styled é, ñ, ü or ø, so names and words in many languages end up half styled. If that looks wrong, pick a different word to emphasize.No punctuation, symbols or emoji. Colons, commas, # and @ stay as they are in bold, italic and mono. Underline and strike do mark punctuation and digits, since they add a mark rather than swap the letter.Greek has bold and italic forms in the same block, but this tool converts Latin letters and digits only.Accessibility: what screen readers do with styled lettersThis is the main reason to keep styled text short. Accessibility consultant Adrian Roselli tested fake bold and italic with default settings (his post was updated Sep 29, 2025; we read it Nov 1, 2026). NVDA with Firefox, VoiceOver on macOS and iPadOS, and Narrator with Edge did not announce the styled text. JAWS with Chrome announced each letter individually, with its case and style. Only TalkBack with Chrome read it as ordinary words.Scope for Business, writing for the UK disability charity Scope, says these characters are "inaccessible to screen reader users" and gives the example of a letter announced as "mathematical sans-serif script t". It also notes fancy characters are harder to read for people with dyslexia or low vision. Its advice is to use standard text when you want a wide audience to understand the message.So the safe pattern is decoration on words the post doesn't depend on. If a screen reader drops your bold label, the sentence after it should still make sense. If the bold words carry the whole point, write them in plain text.Search, hashtags and copy-pasteA bold 𝘄𝗲𝗯𝗵𝗼𝗼𝗸𝘀 is a different string of characters from the word webhooks. The Unicode chart lists a compatibility mapping from each styled letter back to its plain letter, and software that applies that normalization (NFKC) can fold them together. Plenty of software doesn't. LinkedIn doesn't document how its search treats these characters, so don't count on styled words being found by people searching for them.The practical rules follow from that. Leave keywords, product names and your own name in plain text. Don't select hashtags: the # stays a #, but the letters after it become different characters, so the tag no longer matches the plain one. The same goes for anything a reader might copy into another tool, such as a command, a URL or an email address.When to use each styleA rule of thumb: one styled element per paragraph at most, and never a whole paragraph.Bold for a short label at the start of a line ("What changed:", "Key takeaway:") or a single hook line at the top of the post.Italic for one word of stress, a title, or a short aside. Remember it skips digits.Bold italic rarely. It is heavier to read than bold and adds nothing bold can't do.Mono for short technical strings that should look like code, such as an endpoint name. Keep the real, copyable version in plain text if readers need to use it.Strikethrough for a visible correction, like an old price or version number next to the new one.Underline almost never. Readers expect underlined text to be a link, and the combining marks render unevenly across fonts.Copy-paste examplesThese were generated with the buttons above, so they match what the tool produces. A bolded label followed by plain text keeps the sentence readable when the label is skipped. If you're unsure where LinkedIn will cut the post, paste the result into the LinkedIn post preview.text𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗱: failed posts now retry five times before we mark them failed. 𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝘁𝗮𝗸𝗲𝗮𝘄𝗮𝘆: check the webhook, not the dashboard. The endpoint is 𝙿𝙾𝚂𝚃 /𝚟𝟷/𝚙𝚘𝚜𝚝𝚜 (plain: POST /v1/posts). This is 𝘯𝘰𝘵 a scheduling app. 𝗕𝗲𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗲: v̶2̶ 𝗔𝗳𝘁𝗲𝗿: v3Line breaks, spacing and the 3,000 character limitThe formatter keeps your line breaks and spaces exactly as typed, and underline and strike skip them, so paragraph spacing survives the copy. Blank lines between short paragraphs make a post easier to scan than any amount of bold. Check the pasted result in LinkedIn's composer before you publish, since that is the rendering readers see.LinkedIn Help (read Nov 1, 2026) says posts can be up to 3,000 characters. The counter under the tool counts graphemes, the characters you see, which is also how our API counts LinkedIn posts. Styled letters are heavier underneath: "Hello 2026" in bold is 10 graphemes but 19 UTF-16 code units and 37 UTF-8 bytes. LinkedIn doesn't say which unit its limit uses, so leave some room if a heavily styled post sits near 3,000. More on the limit in our LinkedIn character limit guide.Posting formatted text through the LinkedIn APIThe LinkedIn Posts API takes post text in its "little" text format. Microsoft's documentation for it (read Nov 1, 2026) lists four elements: plain text, mentions, hashtags and a hashtag template. There is no bold or italic element, so Unicode styling is also the only way to emphasize words in a post created through the API.Styled letters are ordinary text to the API and pass through unchanged. What does need care is the reserved character set: little text requires characters like ( ) [ ] { } < > @ * _ ~ | and \ to be escaped with a backslash, even when they aren't part of a mention. Our LinkedIn API integration escapes them for you and leaves hashtags intact. For the text below, the commentary we send is:json// you send: "𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗱: failed posts retry (5 times) #api" { "commentary": "𝗪𝗵𝗮𝘁 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗻𝗴𝗲𝗱: failed posts retry \\(5 times\\) #api" }QuestionsAbout this toolHow do I bold text on LinkedIn?+LinkedIn's post format has no bold or italic markup. Type your post in the formatter above, select the words, press Bold and copy the result into LinkedIn. The letters are swapped for Unicode sans-serif bold characters, which display bold anywhere plain text shows. Keep it to a label or one line, because some screen readers skip those characters.Why didn't my numbers or accented letters turn italic?+Unicode has no italic or bold italic digits, and no styled versions of accented letters like é or ñ. The formatter only changes the 26 basic Latin letters, plus digits in bold and monospace. Everything else, including punctuation, emoji and accented letters, is copied as it was, so a word like café ends up partly styled.Is Unicode bold text bad for accessibility?+Used heavily, yes. In Adrian Roselli's tests, NVDA, VoiceOver and Narrator didn't announce styled text, and JAWS read it letter by letter with each letter's style. Only TalkBack read it as words. Style a few words that the post doesn't depend on, and never a whole paragraph or anything a reader needs to understand.Will people find my styled words in LinkedIn search?+Don't rely on it. Styled letters are different Unicode characters from plain letters. Some software folds them back to plain text, but LinkedIn doesn't document whether its search does. Keep keywords, product names, hashtags and your own name in plain text, and use styling only on words you don't need anyone to search for.Do formatted characters count more toward LinkedIn's 3,000 limit?+Each styled letter is one visible character, but it takes two UTF-16 code units and four UTF-8 bytes. Bold "Hello 2026" is 10 characters, 19 code units and 37 bytes. LinkedIn Help states the 3,000 limit without naming the unit, so if a heavily styled post is close to the limit, leave a margin.Can I post bold text to LinkedIn through an API?+Yes, as Unicode characters. The Posts API's little text format has elements for text, mentions and hashtags but none for bold or italic, so styled characters are the only option. They pass through unchanged. Reserved characters like parentheses and @ must be backslash-escaped; our API does that automatically.Does this tool store or send my text?+No. The formatter runs entirely in your browser. The conversion is a lookup from plain letters to Unicode code points done by JavaScript on the page, and nothing you type is sent to our servers or saved. Closing the tab discards the text.Posting from code or an agent? SocialsForAI runs the same checks before every post.
