https://socialsforai.com/tools/twitter-c.body_text: Twitter (X) Character Counter: Counts Like X (Free)Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyTwitter (X) character counterCount characters the way X counts them.Links count 23, emoji and CJK count 2. A plain character count gets X wrong; this doesn't.Your postShipping webhooks today 🚀 Docs: https://example.com/docs/webhooksX weighted count: 56 / 280 (224 left)Plain length 65 · links 1 (×23)This post has a link. Through the X API, posts with a URL cost $0.200 instead of $0.015 (docs.x.com pricing).The short answerAn X (Twitter) character counter measures a draft against X's 280-character limit using X's own weighting: every URL counts as 23 characters, every emoji as 2, and Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters as 2, per X's developer docs. That is why a plain character count disagrees with X. This counter applies those weights live as you type.How X counts charactersX doesn't count characters one for one. Its developer page "Counting characters" (read Nov 1, 2026) says posts can contain up to 280 characters and gives each character a weight:Latin letters, punctuation and common symbols weigh 1, so 280 of them fit.Every URL counts as 23, whatever its real length, because X wraps links in its t.co shortener.All emoji count as 2, "regardless of complexity". A skin-tone thumbs-up and a four-person family emoji are both 2.Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters weigh 2, so a post fits 140 of them.Other Unicode characters default to a weight of 2.Text is normalized to Unicode NFC before counting, so an accented letter counts once whether it was typed as one character or as a letter plus an accent mark.Worked examplesEach number below was computed with the same function this counter and our API use, xWeightedLength in our codebase. Compare the weighted count with the plain length a generic counter would show.The sample in the box, "Shipping webhooks today 🚀 Docs: https://example.com/docs/webhooks": 65 characters plain, 56 weighted. The 33-character URL counts 23 and the rocket counts 2."Docs: https://example.com" and "Docs: " followed by a 95-character tracking URL both weigh 29. Long links cost nothing extra."こんにちは" (five Japanese characters) weighs 10."Hello 👋" weighs 8: six for the letters and space, two for the emoji."👨‍👩‍👧‍👦" is seven code points joined into one family emoji, and it weighs 2.280 plain letters weigh exactly 280, the limit.Characters that count more than you expectMost surprises come from characters outside the weight-1 ranges. Our counter gives weight 1 to code points U+0000 to U+10FF (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Arabic, Hebrew and more) and to the space, dash, quote and prime ranges of General Punctuation. Everything else weighs 2, following X's rule that other Unicode defaults to 2:Unicode bold and italic letters. "𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱" weighs 8, while "Bold" weighs 4. A bolded sentence from the LinkedIn text formatter, "Shipped: webhooks for every post.", goes from 33 characters to a weight of 60.The single ellipsis character. "Wait…" weighs 6, while "Wait..." with three periods weighs 7. The ellipsis character weighs 2.Curly quotes and the em dash weigh 1. "“Quoted” — dash" weighs 15, the same as its plain length.Underlined or struck-through text made with combining marks counts each marked letter as 2.What doesn't count toward 280The same X page says two things are free. Media attached through official clients counts as 0 characters, so images don't eat into the text. And auto-populated @mentions at the start of a reply don't count; mentions you type into the text yourself count like any other characters.This counter measures the text you paste. It doesn't know whether your post will be a reply, so if you paste the auto-added @handles of a reply, it counts them. Leave them out to match what X will count. This page covers the standard 280-character limit that X's developer docs describe; we haven't verified the separate rules for longer posts on paid X accounts, so the counter doesn't model them.Links: 23 characters, and a different price through the APIA link always counts 23 in the text. Through the X API it also changes the price. X's pricing page (read Nov 1, 2026) lists post creation at $0.015 per request and $0.200 for a post that contains a URL. X notes that prices are subject to change.At 10 posts a day for 30 days, that is $4.50 a month without links and $60.00 a month if every post has one. The counter shows a warning when your draft contains a link, and our API returns the warning x_link_cost on the created post for the same reason. Our X API pricing page has the full cost breakdown.Where this counter can differ from XWe'd rather tell you the edge cases than claim a perfect match:Only text starting with http:// or https:// is treated as a URL. If you type a bare domain like example.com, X may still turn it into a link and count it as 23. Include the scheme to be certain of the count.A trailing period, comma or closing parenthesis right after a URL is counted as ordinary text, not as part of the link, so a sentence that ends in a link counts the way it reads.Counting before you post from codeOur API counts X posts with the same function before anything is sent. A draft over 280 weighted characters fails preflight with text_too_long, a message like "Text is 312 characters; X allows 280." and the exact number to cut. When one post goes to several networks, set platform_options.x.text to a shorter version for X and keep the full text for Bluesky and LinkedIn; see cross-posting. X posting is live. The rules are on our X character limit page.QuestionsAbout this toolWhat's the X (Twitter) character limit?+280 characters for a standard post, per X's developer page "Counting characters" (read Nov 1, 2026). Characters are weighted: Latin letters and common punctuation count 1, while emoji and Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count 2, and every link counts 23. So 280 letters fit, but only 140 CJK characters.Why does my count differ from other character counters?+Most counters count characters or code points one for one. X weights them: a URL counts 23 no matter how long it is, every emoji counts 2, and Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count 2. The sample in this tool is 65 characters plain but 56 the way X counts it, because its 33-character link counts 23.How many characters does a link use on X?+23, always. X wraps every URL in its t.co shortener, so a short link and a 95-character tracking link both count 23 toward the 280 limit. Through the X API, a post containing a URL also costs $0.200 instead of $0.015, per X's pricing page read Nov 1, 2026.Do emoji count as two characters on X?+Yes. X's docs say all emoji count as 2 regardless of complexity. A single smiley, a thumbs-up with a skin tone and a family emoji built from seven code points each count 2. In this counter, "Hello 👋" shows a weighted count of 8: six for the letters and space, two for the emoji.Do images, videos or reply mentions count toward 280?+Media attached through official clients counts 0, per X's docs. Auto-populated @mentions at the start of a reply don't count either. Mentions you type into the text yourself do count. This counter measures only the text you paste, so leave out the auto-added reply handles to match what X counts.Does Unicode bold text use more characters on X?+Yes, double. X weighs characters outside its common Latin ranges as 2, and Unicode bold and italic letters fall outside them. "Bold" weighs 4 and its bold version weighs 8. A 33-character sentence set in Unicode bold weighs 60, so styled text eats into the 280 limit twice as fast as plain text.Posting from code or an agent? SocialsForAI runs the same checks before every post. https://socialsforai.com/twitter-bot.body_text: How to Make a Twitter (X) Bot in 2026: Code, Cost, LimitsSkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyHow to make a Twitter (X) botAn X bot in 2026 is a script, an API key and a budget.The code is the easy part. The parts that bite are OAuth, X's per-post pricing, rate limits, and not getting the account limited for duplicates or bursts.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026To make a Twitter (X) bot you need an X account for the bot, a way to authorize posting (your own X developer app with OAuth 2.0, or a posting API that handles OAuth for you), and code that creates posts on a schedule or in response to events. X charges $0.015 per post created and $0.200 per post containing a link.X: live. Posting to X works on the API today.X API fees for a bot, per 30-day monthPosts per dayPosts per monthWithout links ($0.015)Every post has a link ($0.200)130$0.45$6.00390$1.35$18.005150$2.25$30.0024 (hourly)720$10.80$144.00100 (our per-account cap)3,000$45.00$600.00X's fees only, computed from docs.x.com pricing, read 2026-11-01. X notes prices are subject to change.What do you need to build a Twitter bot?You need four things: an X account for the bot, permission to post as it, code that decides what to post, and something that runs that code on time.Permission is the hard part. Posting as an account through X's API v2 means an OAuth 2.0 flow with PKCE, token storage, and refreshing tokens before they expire, or the bot stops working. Our X connector requests the scopes tweet.read tweet.write users.read media.write offline.access, stores the tokens encrypted (AES-256-GCM) and refreshes them automatically, so your code only ever sees an account id.The code that decides what to post can be anything: a script that reads an RSS feed, a build pipeline that announces releases, or an AI agent. If the agent runs in Claude Code or Cursor, our X MCP server gives it a create_post tool and you write no HTTP code at all. For no-code workflows, see n8n.How much does it cost to run an X bot?X bills API usage per request. Its developer pricing page lists Post: Create at $0.015 per request and Post: Create with a URL at $0.200 per request, with no subscription or minimum spend. A bot that posts links pays about 13 times more per post than one that doesn't.The table below is that math over a 30-day month. It covers X's fees only. On our side, the Free plan includes 100 posts a month and 3 active accounts, which covers a bot posting three times a day; see pricing for the paid plans and the X credit they include. Our X API pricing page has the full breakdown.One more line item: X charges $0.005 per post returned by a read. We read each X post back once after publishing to confirm it exists, and if your bot reads mentions or timelines, those reads are billed by X at the same rate.A worked example: a build-status botHere is the full round trip for a bot that announces passing builds. First the request. The Idempotency-Key is the build number, so if your CI job retries the step, the second call returns the first post instead of creating another.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: build-1482" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_x_bot"], "text": "Build 1482 passed. 412 tests, 0 failures. Deploying to production now.", "wait": true }'What does the response look like?With wait: true the call returns after X has answered. The post is published, the target has X's post id and URL, and verified is true because we read the post back. The text is 70 weighted characters, well under 280, and has no link, so X's fee for it is $0.015.If the same request is sent again with the same key, you get this same body back with the header Idempotent-Replayed: true. Reusing the key with different text returns 409 idempotency_key_reused.json{ "id": "post_Qm3v9XcR1aZ0bL7e", "object": "post", "status": "published", "text": "Build 1482 passed. 412 tests, 0 failures. Deploying to production now.", "media": [], "platform_options": {}, "scheduled_at": null, "created_at": "2026-11-01T15:02:11.204Z", "completed_at": "2026-11-01T15:02:12.918Z", "metadata": {}, "targets": [ { "id": "tgt_k2Hs8PZq0nV4wYcT", "account_id": "acc_x_bot", "platform": "x", "status": "published", "url": "https://x.com/buildbot/status/1852039912345678901", "external_post_id": "1852039912345678901", "attempts": 1, "next_attempt_at": null, "published_at": "2026-11-01T15:02:12.611Z", "verified": true, "error": null } ] }How do I post from TypeScript or Python?The same call in TypeScript with fetch, run from a cron job, a serverless function or a CI step. It throws on any non-2xx status so your scheduler marks the run as failed and you see the error code in the logs.typescriptconst res = await fetch("https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.SOCIALS_API_KEY}`, "Content-Type": "application/json", "Idempotency-Key": `build-${buildNumber}`, }, body: JSON.stringify({ accounts: [process.env.X_BOT_ACCOUNT_ID], text: `Build ${buildNumber} passed. ${tests} tests, 0 failures.`, wait: true, }), }); const body = await res.json(); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`${body.error.code}: ${body.error.fix ?? body.error.message}`); console.log(body.targets[0].url);And the same bot in Python?The Python version with requests. On a 422 it prints each preflight issue's code and fix, which is usually all you need to correct a template.pythonimport os, requests API = "https://socialsforai.com" r = requests.post(f"{API}/v1/posts", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['SOCIALS_API_KEY']}", "Idempotency-Key": f"build-{build_number}"}, json={"accounts": [os.environ["X_BOT_ACCOUNT_ID"]], "text": f"Build {build_number} passed. {tests} tests, 0 failures.", "wait": True}) if r.status_code == 422: for issue in r.json()["error"]["issues"]: print(issue["code"], "->", issue.get("fix")) r.raise_for_status() print(r.json()["targets"][0]["url"])What gets an X bot limited?Repeating yourself and posting in bursts are the two patterns that get automated accounts in trouble, and both are checked before anything reaches X.Duplicate text. If the same account already has the same text published or queued in the last 24 hours, preflight returns duplicate_content. Add a variable part (a build number, a date, a count) to every template.Bursts. X's rate-limit docs list POST /2/tweets at 100 requests per 15 minutes per user and 10,000 per 24 hours per app. Our fair-use cap is stricter: 100 posts per X account per rolling 24 hours, returned as daily_cap_reached. Spread posts out with scheduled_at instead of firing them together.Links in every post. Each one costs $0.200 at X's rates, and our preflight attaches an x_link_cost warning (it doesn't block). Moving the link into a reply doesn't lower the bill: the reply is itself a post with a URL, so the pair costs $0.215. If cost matters, post without the link or give X its own link-free text in platform_options.x.text.X's own automation rules. X publishes rules for automated accounts in its Help Center. Read the current version before launch; we don't paraphrase them here because they change.Common mistakes when building a Twitter botThese are the common failures, with the fix for each.Counting characters with text.length. X counts URLs as 23, emoji as 2 and CJK characters as 2. A 260-character JavaScript string can be over the limit. Use our X character counter or dry_run, which apply X's weights. Details on the X character limit page.Posting the same template every hour. The second identical post within 24 hours fails with duplicate_content.Retrying without an idempotency key. A timeout on your side doesn't mean the post failed. Without a key, the retry can publish a second copy.Scheduling with a local timestamp. scheduled_at must include Z or an offset like -05:00; 2026-11-10T14:00:00 without one is rejected with a 400 validation_error.Mixing a video with images. An X post takes 1 video (MP4 or MOV, up to 200 MB through our API) or up to 4 images, not both; preflight returns mixed_media. Send the video as its own post.How do I fix X bot errors?Every error carries a stable code, a message and a fix. Preflight errors come back as a 422 preflight_failed with an issues array, and nothing is published. Errors from X itself land on the target after publishing starts.text_too_long: the message gives the weighted count, for example "Text is 283 characters; X allows 280." Shorten it, or set platform_options.x.text to a shorter version.duplicate_content: same text on the same account within 24 hours. Vary the text.daily_cap_reached: 100 posts on this account in 24 hours. Schedule the rest later.account_needs_reauth: the token couldn't be refreshed. Create a new connect link for the bot account and approve it again. An account.needs_reauth webhook fires when this happens.platform_rate_limited or platform_unavailable: X returned 429 or a 5xx. These retry on their own after 30s, 2m, 10m, 30m and 2h (6 attempts), then the target is failed.platform_rejected: X refused the post for another reason. The message includes X's response; adjust the post and send it with a new idempotency key.How to make an X bot, step by stepThis is the path through our API. The same steps apply if you build on X's API directly; you take on OAuth, token refresh and retries yourself.01Create a separate X account for the botUse a dedicated account, not your personal one. If the bot misbehaves, the limits land on that account, and you can revoke its access without touching anything else.02Get an API keySend POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/workspaces with a name. The response contains an api_key starting with sk_. It is shown once, so store it in your secrets manager or .env file right away.03Connect the bot's X accountSend POST /v1/connect-links with platforms set to x. Open the returned url in a browser where you are signed in as the bot account and approve. The account id (acc_...) appears in GET /v1/accounts and on the account.connected webhook.04Dry-run the first postSend POST /v1/posts with dry_run: true. Nothing is published. The response lists every issue, such as text_too_long or duplicate_content, with the exact fix.05Publish from a cron job or eventDrop dry_run and call the same endpoint from your scheduler, a GitHub Action, an n8n workflow or an agent. Add an Idempotency-Key header so a retried request never posts twice.06Listen for resultsRegister a webhook for post.published and post.failed, or poll GET /v1/posts/:id. Failed targets carry an error code, a message and a fix.Sources, read 2026-11-01: X API pricing (docs.x.com) · Counting characters (docs.x.com) · X API rate limits (docs.x.com)QuestionsWhat developers askAre bots allowed on X?+X permits automated accounts under its automation rules, which it publishes in the X Help Center. Read the current rules before you launch, because they decide what gets an account limited. Separately, our API blocks two common problems before they reach X: identical text on the same account within 24 hours, and more than 100 posts per account in 24 hours.How much does an X bot cost to run?+At X's published rates, a bot posting 5 times a day without links pays about $2.25 a month in X fees (150 posts at $0.015). If every post has a link, the same bot pays $30 a month, because X charges $0.200 per post with a URL. Our Free plan covers 100 posts a month on top of that.Do I need my own X developer account?+Not through our API. We handle the OAuth 2.0 flow, token refresh and the X developer app, and your code only needs our API key and the bot's account id. If you build directly on X's API instead, you need a developer account, an app with the tweet.write scope, and your own token storage and refresh logic.Can an X bot post images?+Yes. Pass up to 4 images in the media array, each a public https URL of at most 5 MB, with optional alt text. We download each file and upload it to X's media endpoint before creating the post. Video works too: 1 MP4 or MOV per post, up to 200 MB, uploaded in chunks, and not mixed with images (mixed_media).Can I test an X bot without posting publicly?+Yes, two ways. Send dry_run: true and you get every preflight issue without publishing anything. Or connect the sandbox platform, a fake account that accepts posts; putting [fail:retryable], [fail:permanent] or [fail:auth] in the text simulates each failure type so you can test your error handling.Is X posting live on SocialsForAI today?+Yes. The X connector is live and handles OAuth, media upload, retries and read-back verification as described here. Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr are live too, and the same bot code posts there by adding their account ids to the accounts list.Keep readingX API pricingSchedule tweetsX MCP serverX character limitCrosspost to X, Bluesky and LinkedInGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

API, MCP and docs onlySelf-hostingNoNoAI content generationNot listed on the pages readNone. Your agent or app writes the postVideo postingYes (videos on paid plans)Yes: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram (no TikTok, YouTube or Instagram yet)Ayrshare column read on ayrshare.com/pricing and ayrshare.com/docs on 2026-11-01.What Ayrshare isAyrshare is a REST social media API for posting, analytics and comments across 14 networks: Bluesky, Facebook, Google Business, Instagram, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Reddit, Snapchat, Telegram, Threads, TikTok, WhatsApp, X and YouTube. The MCP server runs at https://mcp.blotato.com/mcp over Streamable HTTP and works in Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, Cursor, Codex and others. The request and response shapes are in the docs; our social media API overview explains the model.How to decideThe question is who writes the post. In MCP clients, swap the server URL for ours and use create_post, which waits for the result by default. Its site says it's "built for one person marketing a business", as opposed to team tools like Buffer and Hootsuite. It supports multiple accounts per platform, carousels, bulk video scheduling, analytics (in beta) and founder support.For developers it has a REST API with an API key from the dashboard, and an MCP server at one URL that most clients join over OAuth. Its MCP page lists 16 tools covering scheduling, analytics, accounts, post results and media.Post Bridge pricing, plan by planRead on post-bridge.com/pricing on 2026-11-01. There's a yearly toggle advertising "2 months free", but the page doesn't list the yearly prices.Marketer: $39/mo. 15 connected accounts, unlimited posts, API included, MCP agent connect, multiple accounts per platform, scheduling, carousels, bulk video, analytics (beta).Operator: $99/mo. 99 accounts included, $1 each after, no account limit, everything in Marketer plus team invites.Free: not shown as a plan. The FAQ says free users get 5 posts; account limits for free users aren't listed.The Post Bridge APIThe agents page says API access is "included on every plan" and the key is "only for the REST API and URL-only clients"; MCP uses OAuth instead. It shows POST /v1/social-accounts/connect-link, which returns a link the account owner opens to approve the connection, and describes creating a post with a scheduled_at timestamp and reading per-account results back. We couldn't read a full REST reference: the API reference page rendered no content when fetched, so endpoint paths beyond these aren't listed here.Where Post Bridge is the better choicePost Bridge posts to ten networks today, including TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Threads, Pinterest, Facebook and Google Business. We have X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr live, with the others coming. If you need any of those networks now, use Post Bridge.It also has the app. If you sometimes want to drag a post on a calendar or bulk-schedule a folder of videos, that's a real feature we don't have and don't plan to build.Where we differPrice at small and mid counts. Post Bridge starts at $39 for up to 15 accounts. We're $0 for 3 active accounts on Free, $9 for 5, $19 for 10 and $29 for 15. Between 16 and 98 accounts Post Bridge jumps to $99, while we're $29 at 25 and $54 at 50. At 100 accounts the two are close: $100 against our $79. See pricing.Idle accounts. Post Bridge counts connected accounts. We count accounts that published that month. For client work or an app whose users post now and then, that gap grows with the account count.API behavior. We run preflight checks before sending (length, media count, duplicates, daily caps, account status) and return each problem with a fix, retry retryable failures on a fixed schedule, and accept idempotency keys so a retried request doesn't double-post. How Post Bridge handles these isn't documented on the pages we read, so we don't compare them. Our full contract is in the docs, and the MCP server uses the same calls.How to decideA short way to pick, using only the prices and features above. If you want a scheduler with AI generation or self-hosting instead, see Postiz.You open the app most days to schedule or bulk-upload video: Post Bridge.You need TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Threads or Pinterest this month: Post Bridge.You call the API from code or an agent and never open a dashboard: us, starting on Free.You have 16 to 98 accounts: Post Bridge is $99; we're $29 to $79 depending on how many posted.You have about 100 accounts that all post every month: the price is close, so pick on network coverage and API behavior.Moving from Post BridgeSocial accounts map to our accounts. POST /v1/social-accounts/connect-link maps to POST /v1/connect-links, which takes an external_ref (your client or user id) and a redirect_url; links expire after 7 days by default. A post to several social accounts is one POST /v1/posts with several ids in accounts, and scheduled_at keeps its name and takes ISO-8601. Media goes in as public URLs in media. Accounts need reconnecting, since OAuth grants don't move between apps.bash# A scheduled post to two accounts, retry-safe with an idempotency key curl -X POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-2026-11-03" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_bluesky", "acc_linkedin"], "text": "We shipped v2. Notes: https://example.com/v2", "media": [{ "url": "https://example.com/v2.png", "type": "image", "alt": "v2 screenshot" }], "scheduled_at": "2026-11-03T15:00:00Z" }'Pick Post Bridge ifOne person who wants a scheduler app, bulk video scheduling, or TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, Threads or Pinterest today.Pick SocialsForAI ifDevelopers and agents that only use the API, with 25 or fewer active accounts or many accounts that post irregularly, and who can work with the eight networks live today: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Post Bridge pricing · Post Bridge homepage · Post Bridge MCP · Post Bridge for agentsQuestionsWhat developers askHow much does Post Bridge cost?+Marketer is $39/mo for 15 connected accounts and Operator is $99/mo for 99 accounts, then $1 per account, both with unlimited posts, per Post Bridge's pricing page read 2026-11-01.Is Post Bridge free?+There's a 7-day free trial on both plans. The pricing page doesn't show a free plan, though its FAQ says free users get 5 posts.Does Post Bridge have an API?+Yes. The pricing page lists API included and MCP agent connect on Marketer, and the agents page says API access is included on every plan.Does Post Bridge limit posts?+Paid plans have unlimited posts, per its FAQ. Free users get 5 posts.What are the best Post Bridge alternatives?+For an API-only option billed per active account with a free plan, SocialsForAI. At 100 accounts the two cost about the same. We're only the API.If you use Postiz through its API, MCP or CLI and never open the calendar, you're paying for a product you don't use. If you do use the calendar, Postiz is probably the better fit.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Pick Postiz if you want a calendar UI, AI images and video, 30+ channels live today, or a self-hosted open-source install; hosted plans are $29/mo for 5 channels up to $99/mo for 100, with the API, MCP server and CLI on every plan (pricing page, read 2026-11-01). Pick SocialsForAI if you only call the API, want to pay only for accounts that posted that month, and can work with the eight networks live today: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr.Monthly cost by number of channelsAccountsPostizSocialsForAI3$29$0 (Free, 100 posts/mo)5$29$9 (Hobby)15$49$29 (Pro)25$49$29 (Pro)100$99$79 (Growth)Postiz's prices read on its pricing page on 2026-11-01, monthly billing. Paid plans are billed monthly through Stripe and cancel any time.Postiz vs SocialsForAI, feature by featurePostizSocialsForAIPlatforms you can post to today30+ channels: X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Bluesky, Reddit, Pinterest, Mastodon and more5 live: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn (profiles), Mastodon, Telegram; others comingAPI and MCPPublic API, webhooks, hosted MCP server and CLI on every planREST API and hosted MCP server on every plan, including FreePricing unitChannel (connected account), in plan tiersActive account (published that month)Free tierNo hosted free plan; 7-day trial. Self-hosted edition is free to runYes: 3 active accounts, 100 posts/moPost limitUnlimited posts on every planUnlimited on paid plans, with per-network daily fair-use capsClient or end-user accountsCustomer groups; OAuth2 for apps acting for other Postiz usersConnect links tagged with external_ref; idle accounts cost nothingWeb UIYes: calendar, editor, analytics, team rolesNone. API, MCP and docs onlySelf-hostingYes, AGPL-3.0, DockerNoAI content generationYes: AI copilot, images, videos, clipping (allowances by plan)None. Your agent or app writes the postVideo postingYesYes: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram (no TikTok, YouTube or Instagram yet)Postiz column read on postiz.com, postiz.com/pricing and docs.postiz.com on 2026-11-01.What Postiz isPostiz calls itself "the agentic social media scheduler": agents or people plan, generate and schedule posts, and a human reviews them in a visual calendar before they publish. Its homepage names three audiences: AI-first marketers prompting Claude or ChatGPT, developers building on its OAuth2, SDK and public API, and automation teams using n8n or Make.The codebase is open source under AGPL-3.0 and on GitHub. You can self-host it with Docker for free, but you run the server, updates and backups, and you get your own app approvals from each social network. The pricing FAQ says the hosted platform is where agent features ship first and self-hosting is a secondary option.Postiz pricing, plan by planAll prices below were read on postiz.com/pricing on 2026-11-01. Every plan has unlimited posts, a 7-day free trial, and the MCP server, CLI, API and webhooks. Annual billing saves about 20% and isn't refundable.Standard: $29/mo ($23/mo yearly). 5 channels, no team members, no AI images, 3 AI videos and 60 clipping minutes a month.Team: $39/mo ($31 yearly). 10 channels, unlimited team members, 100 AI images, 10 AI videos, 120 clipping minutes.Pro: $49/mo ($39 yearly). 30 channels, 300 AI images, 30 AI videos, 300 clipping minutes.Ultimate: $99/mo ($79 yearly). 100 channels, 500 AI images, 60 AI videos, 600 clipping minutes.On every plan: picture editor, AI copilot, comments, repeated posts, RSS auto-post, analytics, customer groups, calendar views, signatures.The Postiz API and MCP serverThe public API lives at https://api.postiz.com/public/v1. You send the key from your settings in the Authorization header with no Bearer prefix, or an OAuth2 token starting pos_ when your app acts for other Postiz users. A connected account is a "channel" in the UI and an "integration" in the API: GET /integrations lists them, POST /upload takes images as multipart form data, and POST /posts creates a post with type (now or schedule), a date, and a posts array with one entry per integration.The create-post endpoint is limited to 90 requests an hour (100 on cloud). The docs say the limit is one global value per instance, doesn't vary by plan, and self-hosters can change it with API_LIMIT. Agents can also connect through the hosted MCP server (API key or OAuth token as a Bearer token), the Postiz CLI, or an installable skill.Where Postiz is the better choicePlatform coverage is the biggest gap. Postiz posts to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Threads, Facebook, Pinterest and more today. We have eight networks live: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn (profiles and Company Pages), Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr. The rest are coming. If you need those networks this month, use Postiz.Postiz also has a calendar where a person approves what an agent drafted, AI media generation, team roles, and a self-hosted edition you can run on your own servers. We have none of these. If a human reviews every post in a UI, that review step is the product, and Postiz has it. For a simpler scheduler app, Post Bridge is the other option.Where we differPricing unit. Postiz charges by connected channels in tiers. We charge by accounts that published that month, so ten client accounts that sit idle in October cost nothing. At 3 accounts we're $0 on Free; at 25 we're $29 against Postiz's $49; at 100 Postiz's $99 is close to our $79. The full math is on pricing.Preflight and receipts. Every post runs plain-code checks before it's sent (length per network, media count, duplicates in the last 24 hours, daily caps, accounts flagged for reconnection) and fails with a 422 that lists each issue with a fix. Each target account gets its own status, URL, attempt count and error, and retryable failures retry on a fixed schedule (30s, 2m, 10m, 30m, 2h). Idempotency keys are accepted on every create.Agents. Our MCP server is on the Free plan too, so you can wire it into Claude Code before paying anything. For X, we warn when a post contains a link, because X charges more for those (see X API pricing).Moving from PostizThe endpoints differ, but the concepts map one to one. A Postiz integration is one of our accounts: GET /public/v1/integrations becomes GET /v1/accounts. A Postiz post with several entries in posts becomes one POST /v1/posts with several ids in accounts; per-network text goes in platform_options. type: "now" is the default when you omit scheduled_at. Instead of uploading to /upload first, pass public image URLs in media. Customer groups map to external_ref on connect links, and GET /v1/accounts?external_ref=client_42 lists one client's accounts.Your users reconnect their accounts through our connect links, since OAuth grants don't transfer between apps. Notes: https://example.com/v2", "media": [{ "url": "https://example.com/v2.png", "type": "image", "alt": "v2 screenshot" }], "scheduled_at": "2026-11-03T15:00:00Z" }'Pick Postiz ifTeams that review posts in a calendar, want AI image and video generation, need Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or 30+ channels today, or want to self-host the open-source edition.Pick SocialsForAI ifDevelopers and agents that only call the API, start on a free plan, and have many accounts that don't all post every month. Publishing goes through POST /api/upload for videos, photos, text and documents, usually as multipart form data. We only bill the ones that posted.Zernio (formerly Late) is a unified API for social posting, messaging, ads, SMS and more. We do publishing only, and price on accounts that published.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Pick Zernio if you need one API for publishing to a dozen networks today plus inbox, comments, ads, SMS or WhatsApp; it bills per connected account: 2 free, $6 each for accounts 3–10, $3 for 11–100 and $1 beyond, with unlimited posts (pricing page, read 2026-11-01). Pick SocialsForAI if you only publish and many connected accounts sit idle in a given month, since we bill only accounts that posted. SocialsForAI counts accounts that published that month; connected but idle accounts are free. Paid plans are billed monthly through Stripe and cancel any time.Zernio vs SocialsForAI, feature by featureZernioSocialsForAIPlatforms you can post to today12 listed for posting: X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Reddit, Bluesky, Threads, Google Business, Snapchat (closed beta)5 live: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn (profiles), Mastodon, Telegram; others comingAPI and MCPREST API, SDKs in 8 languages, hosted MCP server, CLIREST API and hosted MCP server on every plan, including FreePricing unitConnected account (ad accounts count too)Active account (published that month)Free tierYes: 2 connected accounts, no cardYes: 3 active accounts, 100 posts/moPost limitUnlimited posts; 25 posts/hour per account velocity limitUnlimited on paid plans, with per-network daily fair-use capsClient or end-user accountsProfiles group accounts per customer; connect URL per platformConnect links tagged with external_ref; idle accounts cost nothingWeb UINot described on the pages readNone. API, MCP and docs onlySelf-hostingNoNoAI content generationNot listedNone. Your agent or app writes the postVideo postingYes (video media items)Yes: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram (no TikTok, YouTube or Instagram yet)Zernio column read on zernio.com/pricing and docs.zernio.com on 2026-11-01.What Zernio isZernio is the renamed Late (getlate.dev). Its docs describe one POST /v1/posts call that publishes to 16 platforms, and an API that covers 37 platforms in total across posting, messaging, comments and reviews, ads, telephony, blogs and commerce. Its platforms page lists 12 networks under social posting. It has official SDKs for Node.js, Python, Go, Ruby, Java, PHP, .NET and Rust, a hosted MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor, a CLI and webhooks.Of the products on our comparison pages, Zernio is the closest to us in shape: an API first, priced per account, built for apps whose users connect their own accounts. The difference is scope and what "account" means on the bill.Zernio pricing, tier by tierRead on zernio.com/pricing on 2026-11-01. There are no plans or seats; the rate stays $1 per account past 2,000 accounts, and Enterprise custom terms are available from there. Every feature is included.Accounts 1–2: free, no card. Accounts 3–10: $6/mo each. 11–100: $3 each. 101 and up: $1 each, no cap. The page shows 10 accounts at $48; by the same rate card, 100 accounts are $318 and 1,000 are $1,218.Unlimited posts, threads, first comments and queue access on every account.Messaging: received messages free; first 10,000 sent a month free, then $1 per 10,000.X API passed through at X's rates with no markup: posts $0.015, posts with a URL $0.200, reads $0.005.SMS from $0.008 per outbound US segment, plus 10DLC fees. Managed ads metered per active ad, first 500 free.The Zernio APIRequests go to https://zernio.com/api/v1 with Authorization: Bearer and a key starting sk_. The quickstart has three steps: create a profile (POST /v1/profiles, one per brand or per user of your app), get a connect URL with GET /v1/connect/{platform}?profileId=..., then POST /v1/posts with content, scheduledFor, timezone and a platforms array of entries with a platform and an accountId.The create-post docs list an optional Idempotency-Key header (retries with the same key within 24 hours return the original post), a dryRun flag that applies to TikTok only, and 429 causes including a velocity limit of 25 posts per hour per account and daily platform limits.Where Zernio is the better choiceCoverage and breadth. Zernio publishes to X, Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Reddit, Threads and Google Business today. We publish to X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr, and the rest are coming. Zernio also has a unified inbox, comment and review management, managed ads, SMS, WhatsApp and iMessage, and SDKs in eight languages. If your product needs any of that, Zernio covers more than we do.Connected vs active, with numbersZernio bills every connected account each month. We bill accounts that published that month. If every account posts, the two are close: at 25 accounts Zernio is $93 and we're $29; at 100, $318 against $79.The gap opens when users connect and then post occasionally. Take an app with 1,000 connected accounts where 200 post in a given month: Zernio's rate card puts 1,000 accounts at $1,218; we'd bill the 200 active ones, $154 on Growth. The pricing page has a calculator.Both pass X API costs through at cost. Ours comes with an included X credit on paid plans, and preflight warns with x_link_cost when a post contains a link, because X charges $0.200 for those against $0.015 for plain posts (see X API pricing).How to decideBoth are APIs, so the choice comes down to scope and billing. For per-profile pricing instead of per-account, compare Ayrshare and Upload-Post.You need messaging, comments, ads, SMS or an SDK in Go, Ruby, Java, PHP, .NET or Rust: Zernio.You need Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, Reddit or Google Business publishing now: Zernio.You publish only, and a large share of connected accounts don't post in a given month: us, because idle accounts are free.You want dry runs on every network, not only TikTok, and preflight errors that carry a fix: us.Moving from ZernioWe have no profile object. Tag connect links with external_ref instead (the profile id or your customer id), and filter with GET /v1/accounts?external_ref=.... GET /v1/connect/{platform} becomes POST /v1/connect-links, which returns a hosted URL valid for 7 days by default. A platforms array of {platform, accountId} becomes a flat accounts array of ids; content becomes text; mediaItems becomes media; scheduledFor plus timezone becomes one ISO-8601 scheduled_at with an offset. Idempotency-Key works the same way, and our dry_run runs preflight on every network, not only TikTok. Full field list in the docs.bash# Zernio's platforms[].accountId becomes a flat accounts array curl -X POST https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_KEY" \ -H "Idempotency-Key: launch-2026-11-03" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_bluesky", "acc_linkedin"], "text": "We shipped v2. Notes: https://example.com/v2", "media": [{ "url": "https://example.com/v2.png", "type": "image", "alt": "v2 screenshot" }], "scheduled_at": "2026-11-03T15:00:00Z" }'Pick Zernio ifProducts that need publishing to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and other networks today, or messaging, comments, ads, SMS and SDKs in one API.Pick SocialsForAI ifPublishing-only apps with many connected accounts that don't all post every month, on the eight networks live today: X, Bluesky, LinkedIn, Mastodon, Telegram, Discord, Slack and Nostr.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Zernio pricing · Zernio docs · Zernio quickstart · Zernio create post · Zernio platformsQuestionsWhat developers askHow much does Zernio cost?+Two connected accounts are free, then $6/mo each for accounts 3 to 10, $3 for 11 to 100 and $1 from 101. By its rate card that is $48 for 10 accounts, $318 for 100 and $1,218 for 1,000. Read on its pricing page 2026-11-01.Is Zernio free?+Up to 2 connected accounts, with no card required and unlimited posts on them.Does Zernio have an API?+Zernio is an API. Requests go to https://zernio.com/api/v1 with a Bearer key, and it has SDKs in eight languages, a hosted MCP server and a CLI.Is Zernio the same as Late?+Yes. Zernio is the rebranded Late (getlate.dev).What are the best Zernio alternatives?+For publishing-only billing per active account, SocialsForAI. For enterprise-scale posting across 14 networks, Ayrshare. For a video-heavy posting API with per-profile pricing, Upload-Post.Does Zernio charge for X API calls?+It passes X's rates through with no markup: $0.015 per post, $0.200 per post with a URL. SocialsForAI also passes X fees through at cost, with an included credit on paid plans.Keep readingAyrshare alternativeUpload-Post alternativeX API pricingAll comparisonsGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/x-api-pricing.body_text: X API Pricing 2026: Cost per Post, Links, Reads | SocialsForAISkip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyX API pricing (2026)What posting through the X API costs now.X moved the API to pay-per-use credits. Posting is cheap until you add a link, and then it isn't. Every number below comes from X's own pricing page.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026The X API charges per request with no subscription: $0.015 to create a post, $0.200 to create a post that contains a URL, and $0.005 per post read, according to X's developer pricing page. You buy credits upfront. Pay-per-use plans are capped at 3 million post reads per monthly billing cycle; higher volume needs an Enterprise plan.X: live. Posting to X works on the API today.X API cost calculator (X's published rates)Posts per day: 10Posts with a link: 50%Posts / month300X API cost / month$32.25Same posts, no links$4.50X API pay-per-use rates that matter for postingRequestPriceNoteCreate a post$0.015 per requestText, images, repliesCreate a post with a URL$0.200 per requestAny post containing a linkRead a post$0.005 per resourceCapped at 3M reads per billing cycleOwned read$0.001 per resourceYour app reading its own posts, bookmarks, followers, likes, listsRead a user$0.010 per resourceProfile lookupsCreate a DM$0.015 per requestDM Interaction: CreateRead on docs.x.com on 2026-11-01. X says prices are subject to change; the developer console shows your current rates. Re-reading the same resource within one UTC day isn't billed again.Monthly X API posting cost by volume (30-day month)Posts per dayPosts per monthNo linksHalf have linksEvery post has a link130$0.45$3.23$6.005150$2.25$16.13$30.0010300$4.50$32.25$60.0020600$9.00$64.50$120.001003,000$45.00$322.50$600.00Computed from $0.015 per post and $0.200 per post with a URL. Excludes reads: reading each post back once adds up to $0.005 per post.How much does the X API cost per post?A plain post costs $0.015, so 1,000 posts cost $15. A post with a link costs $0.200, so 1,000 linked posts cost $200. Those two lines are the whole posting bill for most bots and agents; media metadata, reads and deletes are priced separately and only apply if you call them.X bills against credits you buy in advance. There's no monthly subscription and no minimum spend, and X's page says prices are subject to change, so treat the table above as a snapshot and check the developer console before you commit to a budget.Is there a free X API tier in 2026?X's pricing page doesn't describe a free tier. It describes pay-per-use credits, with two incentives for new payers: $20 in API credits after you save a card and make a first purchase, and a match of your first auto-recharge up to $50.At $0.015 a post, the $20 incentive covers about 1,333 plain posts or 100 linked posts. For a hobby bot posting a few times a day without links, that's months of posting; our X bot guide walks through building one.Why does a post with a link cost 13 times more?X lists "Post: Create (with URL)" as its own request type at $0.200, about 13.3 times the $0.015 plain rate. The pricing page doesn't define what counts as a URL; our preflight treats any http:// or https:// in the text as a link and warns with x_link_cost.A common tip is to move the link into a reply. By X's price list that doesn't save money through the API: the reply is itself a post with a URL, so the pair costs $0.215, a little more than the single linked post. The savings only come from leaving the link off X.With a unified API you can do that per network. Set platform_options.x.text to a version without the link, and Bluesky and LinkedIn still get the full text. At 20 posts a day, that one field is the difference between $9 and $120 a month.bashcurl https://socialsforai.com/v1/posts \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $SOCIALS_API_KEY" \ -d '{ "accounts": ["acc_x", "acc_bluesky", "acc_linkedin"], "text": "Release notes for v2.3: https://example.com/changelog", "platform_options": { "x": { "text": "v2.3 is out. Notes are on our site." } } }'How do X API credits, spending limits and billing cycles work?You load credits, X draws them down per request, and when the balance goes negative requests are blocked until you top up. Auto-recharge tops up at a threshold you set, at most once per 5-minute window.You can set a spending limit per billing cycle. Once it's reached, X blocks API requests until the next cycle, which is the cheapest insurance against a runaway loop that posts the same link a thousand times.Read cap: pay-per-use plans stop at 3 million post reads per monthly cycle; above that X asks you to request an Enterprise plan.Deduplication: re-requesting a billed resource within the same UTC day isn't charged again. X calls this a soft guarantee.xAI credits: link your xAI team and X returns 10% of cumulative spend from $200, 15% from $500 and 20% from $1,000 in xAI API credits, reset each cycle.Owned reads: your app reading its own posts, bookmarks, followers, likes and lists costs $0.001 per resource instead of $0.005.What are the X API rate limits for posting?Creating posts is limited to 100 requests per 15 minutes per user and 10,000 per 24 hours per app, according to X's rate limit table. Deleting is 50 per 15 minutes per user. Looking up a post is 900 per 15 minutes per user and 450 per app.Media upload (POST /2/media/upload) allows 500 per 15 minutes per user. Over a limit, X returns HTTP 429 with error code 88, "Rate limit exceeded", and documents x-rate-limit-remaining and x-rate-limit-reset headers for pacing.Through us, a 429 becomes platform_rate_limited and retries on our backoff schedule. We also cap each X account at 100 posts per 24 hours as a fair-use limit, which returns daily_cap_reached before anything is sent.What does a raw X API post request look like?Posting needs an OAuth 2.0 user-context token with tweet.read, tweet.write and users.read, per X's create-post reference; we also request media.write for image uploads and offline.access for refresh tokens. You send JSON to POST https://api.x.com/2/tweets; the response's data object carries the new post's id and text.A post takes up to 4 photos, 1 animated GIF or 1 video, uploaded first to get media ids. Quote posts need an Enterprise plan, per X's create-post reference, so they aren't available on pay-per-use.bashcurl -X POST https://api.x.com/2/tweets \ -H "Authorization: Bearer $X_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "text": "Hello from the X API" }' # 201 → { "data": { "id": "...", "text": "Hello from the X API" } }How does SocialsForAI bill X usage?SocialsForAI passes X's per-request charges through at cost, with a monthly X credit included: $0.50 on Free (per verified owner, shared across their Free workspaces), $2 on Hobby, $5 on Pro, $15 on Growth and $40 on Scale. On Free, X posts past the credit fail preflight with x_credit_exhausted; paid plans are billed for the rest at renewal. Worked example: 20 plain posts a day to one X account is $9.00 of X fees a month; on Pro the $5 credit covers part of it, leaving $4.00 on top of the $29 plan.After publishing we read each X post back once to confirm it exists, which is at most one $0.005 read per post. Those reads are part of the X fees passed through at cost. Plan details are on pricing.When a post bound for X has a link, the 201 response carries the warning below so an agent can decide whether the link is worth $0.185 extra. Agents get the same warning through the X MCP server.json"warnings": [ { "account_id": "acc_x", "platform": "x", "severity": "warning", "code": "x_link_cost", "message": "Posts with a URL cost $0.200 through the X API instead of $0.015 (docs.x.com pricing).", "fix": "Remove the link, or send a link-free version for X in platform_options.x.text. A link in a reply is also billed at the with-URL rate." } ]How do you cut an X API bill?Most of the bill is links, so most of the savings are too. In rough order of impact:Drop the link on X only, with platform_options.x.text. Keep it on networks where links are free.Set a spending limit in the X developer console so a bug can't drain your credits.Don't read what you don't need. Reads are $0.005 each; owned reads are $0.001.Use dry_run: true to test. Our preflight never calls X, so testing costs nothing.Fit posts in 280 weighted characters the first time with the X character counter; the X character limit page explains why a URL always counts as 23.Sources, read 2026-11-01: X API pricing (docs.x.com) · Counting characters (docs.x.com) · X API rate limits (docs.x.com) · X API: Create Post reference (docs.x.com)QuestionsWhat developers askHow much does the X API cost per month?+There is no monthly fee. You pay per request from prepaid credits: $0.015 per post, $0.200 per post with a link, $0.005 per post read. Posting 10 times a day without links is about $4.50 a month; with a link in every post it's $60. Set a spending limit to cap it.Is there still a free X API tier?+X's pricing page describes pay-per-use credits with no subscriptions or minimum spend and doesn't list a free posting tier. New payers get $20 in credits after saving a card and making a first purchase, plus a match of the first auto-recharge up to $50.Does a link in a reply also cost $0.20?+Yes, by X's price list. X prices by request type, and creating any post containing a URL is listed at $0.200. A reply with a link is still a post with a URL, so moving the link into a reply costs $0.215 for the pair rather than saving money.Can I cap my X API spend?+Yes. X lets you set a maximum spend per billing cycle in the developer console. Once it's reached, API requests are blocked until the next cycle. Requests are also blocked if your credit balance goes negative, until you add credits to cover it.What is the X API rate limit for posting?+X's rate limit table lists 100 create-post requests per 15 minutes per user and 10,000 per 24 hours per app. Exceeding it returns HTTP 429 with error code 88. Through our API, a 429 retries automatically, and each account has a 100-posts-per-day fair-use cap.Do reads cost anything when I only post?+Only if you read. Publishing doesn't require reading your timeline. Through us, each X post is read back once to confirm it went out, which costs at most one $0.005 post read, and re-reading the same post within a UTC day isn't billed again.Keep readingX character limitHow to make an X botX MCP serverSocial media APIPricingGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →

https://socialsforai.com/x-character-lim.body_text: X (Twitter) Character Limit: 280, URLs = 23, Emoji = 2Skip to contentSocialsForAIMenuSetupDocsMCPPricingCompareToolsSign inGet an API keyX (Twitter) character limit280, but not the way you'd count it.X weights characters. Links always count 23, emoji count 2, Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count 2, and most Latin text counts 1.Get an API keyRead the docs →The short answer · Updated Nov 1, 2026Posts on X can contain up to 280 characters, per X's developer documentation. X counts them by weight: every URL counts as 23 characters regardless of length because it's wrapped by t.co, every emoji counts as 2, and Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count as 2 each, so a post written entirely in Japanese fits 140 characters.How X counts charactersContentCounts asExampleLatin letters, digits, most punctuation1 eachhello = 5Spaces and line breaks1 eacha, two line breaks, b = 4Any URL23a 56-character https URL = 23Any emoji, including skin tones and ZWJ sequences2👍 = 2, 👍🏽 = 2, 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 = 2Chinese, Japanese, Korean characters2 eachこんにちは世界 = 14Other symbols outside X's light ranges2 each€100 = 5Attached images04 images add nothingFrom "Counting characters" on docs.x.com and the twitter-text config, read 2026-11-01. Examples computed with our counter, which uses the same weights.How does X count characters?X gives every character a weight of 1 or 2 and adds them up; the total must be 280 or less. The open-source twitter-text config that X points to gives weight 1 to four Unicode ranges: code points 0 to 4351 (Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, Hebrew, Arabic and more), and three small punctuation ranges between 8192 and 8247 that include en and em dashes and curly quotes. Everything else weighs 2.Two rules override that. Every URL counts as 23, whatever its length, because X wraps it with t.co. Every emoji counts as 2, regardless of how many code points it's built from; X's docs say zero-width joiners combine emoji visually without adding to the count. X also normalizes text to Unicode NFC before counting.A worked example: a tweet with a link and two emojiTake Shipped: webhooks for every post. Docs: https://socialsforai.com/docs 🚀🎉. In JavaScript, .length says 74. X says 68. Here is the math:The text before the link, Shipped: webhooks for every post. Docs: , is 40 characters of weight 1 = 40. The URL is 29 characters long but counts 23. The space after it is 1. The two emoji count 2 each = 4. Total: 40 + 23 + 1 + 4 = 68 of 280, leaving 212.The same string on Bluesky is 72 graphemes, because Bluesky counts the URL at its full length and each emoji as 1. Paste either into our X character counter to see the same number.Do links count toward the X character limit?Yes, always as 23. A 12-character link and a 200-character link both cost 23, so long tracking URLs are free in length terms and short ones save nothing. They do cost money through the API: X's pricing page lists a post with a URL at $0.200 versus $0.015 without, and our preflight adds an x_link_cost warning when a post contains one. The X API pricing page works through the totals.One caveat in our counter: it treats only text starting with http:// or https:// as a URL. A bare domain like example.com/pricing is counted at its full length, 19. Whether X treats a bare domain as a link depends on X's own URL detection, so write links with https:// and both counts agree.Do emoji, accents and CJK count double?Emoji and CJK do; most accented Latin letters don't. Concrete counts from our counter, which applies X's weights:👍 = 2, 👍🏽 (with a skin tone) = 2, 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 (a 7-code-point family) = 2, 🇺🇸 = 2. Complexity doesn't matter.こんにちは世界 (7 Japanese characters) = 14. 안녕하세요 (5 Korean) = 10. 你好 = 4. A post entirely in CJK fits 140 characters.café, Привет (Cyrillic) and مرحبا (Arabic) count 1 per letter: 4, 6 and 5.€ counts 2, because it sits outside X's weight-1 ranges. €100 = 5.Unicode "bold" letters like 𝗕𝗼𝗹𝗱 count 2 each = 8, double the plain word. Don't use them on X if space is tight.A decomposed accent (e plus a combining mark) counts 1 on X after NFC normalization. Our counter normalizes the same way, so it counts 1 too.Do mentions, hashtags, line breaks and images count?Mentions and hashtags count like normal text, including the @ and #: Hi @alice, thanks for the report #bugfix is 40. X's docs make one exception: the @mentions X fills in automatically at the start of a reply don't count, but our API doesn't create replies, so every mention you write counts.Line breaks count 1 each; a newline is code point 10, inside X's weight-1 range. X's docs say attached media counts 0. Attach up to 4 images through our API without touching the text budget.What happens if you go over 280 through the API?With our API, nothing reaches X. Preflight counts the text with X's weights and returns a 422 preflight_failed whose issue reads, for a 283-character post, "Text is 283 characters; X allows 280." with the fix "Shorten it by 3+ characters, or set platform_options.x.text to a shorter version." Send dry_run: true to get the same answer without risk. A Twitter bot that fills templates should dry-run each new template once.Longer posts exist on X. Its API changelog records that, as of August 20, 2024, longform posts can be created through API v2 with a length of 25k characters. Our API caps X at 280 weighted characters today, so a longer post needs a shorter X version in platform_options.How do I shorten a post to fit 280?Work in this order, cheapest first.Cut emoji and CJK punctuation first: each one you remove gives back 2.Keep one link. A second link costs another 23 and doesn't change the price tier you already hit.Drop the link from the X version if cost matters: it saves 23 characters and drops X's fee from $0.200 to $0.015. Moving it to a reply doesn't help, because a reply with a URL is billed at $0.200 too.Write a separate X version in platform_options.x.text and keep the long one for Bluesky and LinkedIn. See crossposting.Sources, read 2026-11-01: Counting characters (docs.x.com) · twitter-text weighting config (GitHub) · X API pricing (docs.x.com) · X API changelog (docs.x.com)QuestionsWhat developers askWhat is the character limit on X (Twitter)?+Posts on X can contain up to 280 characters, per X's developer documentation. Characters are weighted: Latin letters, digits and most punctuation count 1, while emoji and Chinese, Japanese and Korean characters count 2, and every URL counts 23. X's API changelog also records longform posts of up to 25k characters through API v2.Does a link count against the X character limit?+Yes, always as 23 characters, however long or short the URL is, because X wraps every link with its t.co shortener. Through the API, a link also changes the price: X lists a post with a URL at $0.200 versus $0.015 without one.Do emoji count as one character on X?+No. Every emoji counts as 2, regardless of complexity, per X's docs. A thumbs-up, a thumbs-up with a skin tone, a flag and a four-person family emoji all count 2, even though the family is 7 code points and 11 JavaScript string units.Why does my character count differ from X's?+Most counters use string length. JavaScript's .length counts UTF-16 units, so emoji show as 2 to 11 and URLs at their full length, while X counts emoji as 2 and URLs as 23. Our X character counter and our API's preflight both apply X's weights, so they match what X enforces.How many characters can a tweet in Japanese have?+140. X counts each Chinese, Japanese and Korean character as 2, so 140 Japanese characters weigh 280. In our counter, 140 repetitions of the hiragana あ weigh exactly 280, and a 141st makes it 282, over the limit. Mixed text adds up per character: Latin letters and spaces count 1, Japanese characters and full-width punctuation count 2.Do images count toward the X character limit?+No. X's docs say media attached to a post counts as 0 characters. Through our API you can attach up to 4 images, at most 5 MB each, with optional alt text, and the full 280 stays available for text. Image URLs in the media array are not part of the text, so they don't count as 23 either.Keep readingX character counterBluesky character limitLinkedIn character limitX API pricingHow to make an X botGet an API key and send your first post in five minutes.Get an API keyRead the quickstart →
